e: Mesopotamian wars of the Early Dynastic period.
Assyria is established.
Cylinder seal from Sumer and its impression are made. It is now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
Evidence of long-distance trade routes in South America.
Excavation and development of the Hypogeum of Ħal-Saflieni at Paola, Malta, a subterranean temple complex subsequently used as a necropolis.
Mohenjo-daro is about in size and has a population of c. 20,000 to 50,000.
N1c Y-DNA first found from Europe from Serteya II (located in modern day Smolensk Oblast in Russia).
People in what is now Peru rely on fish and mussels for food.
Rice was first introduced to what is now modern-day Malaysia.
Scribal schools flourish throughout Sumer.
Skara Brae is abandoned after approximately 600 years of occupation.
The Pyramid of Khafre, Giza, is built.
The sculpture Khafre Enthroned is made.
"Sculptors at work", relief from Saqqara, Fifth Dynasty. It is now at Egyptian Museum, Cairo, Egypt.
The Seated Scribe, a sculpture found at Saqqara, Fifth Dynasty of Egypt is made. It is now in Musée du Louvre, Paris.
Traditional date for the legendary foundation of Armenia by Hayk.
End of the Early Dynastic IIIa Period and beginning of the Early Dynastic IIIb Period in Sumer.
Kish is lost to Hamazi tribesmen of the Kurdistan mountains; Elam under the Awan dynasty occupies parts of Sumer.
By this time, kings in Sumer have ceased to be automatically high priests of the city deity. Infiltration and conquest of Mesopotamia by ancient Semitic-speaking peoples begins.
Construction of Stonehenge.
Large painted jar with birds in the border made in the Indus River Valley civilization and is now at Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
End of the Early Dynastic III period in Mesopotamia.
First destruction of the city of Mari.
Lugal-Zage-Si of Umma conquers Gu-Edin and unites Sumer as a single kingdom.
Pharaohs Teti, Userkare reign, Pepi I then rules into the 23rd century BC.
End of Fifth Dynasty. Pharaoh Unas died.
Sixth Dynasty of Egypt starts.
Semitic chieftain Sargon of Akkad's conquest of Sumer and Mesopotamia.
Dangun establishes Gojoseon, the first Korean kingdom, according to Korean mythology.
"Head of a man from Nineveh" (modern Kuyunjik, Iraq) is made. It is now in the Iraq Museum, Baghdad.
Canal Bahr Yusuf (current name) is created when the waterway from the Nile to the natural lake (now Lake Moeris) is widened and deepened to create a canal.
Indus Valley Civilization (Harappan) flourishing in modern-day eastern Pakistan - western India.
Metals start to be used in Northern Europe.
The Disc of Enheduanna, from Ur (modern Muqaiyir, Iraq) is made. It is now in the University of Pennsylvania Museum of Archaeology and Anthropology, University of Pennsylvania, Philadelphia.
The Unetice culture emerges in the modern-day Czech Republic.
"Queen Merye-ankhnes and her son Pepy II" is sculpted, Sixth dynasty of Egypt. The alabaster statuette is now at the Brooklyn Museum of Art, New York.
Enheduanna, high priestess of the moon god Nanna in Ur, was born.
The Stela of Naram-Sin, probably from Sippar, discovered in Susa (modern Shush, Iran), was made. It is now in the Musée du Louvre, Paris.
The beginning of the Meghalayan Stage, the last of the three stages of the Holocene.
Earliest evidence of maize cultivation in Central America.
Akkad, capital of the Akkadian Empire, becomes the largest city in the world, surpassing Memphis, capital of Egypt.
Mount Edgecumbe volcano erupts near present-day Sitka, Alaska.
Scord of Brouster farmstead established in the Shetland islands.
Ancient migrants from India reach Australia and mix with Indigenous Australians.
A Guti army swept down from the Zagros Mountains and defeated the demoralized Akkadian army. They took Agade, the capital of Akkad, and destroyed it thoroughly.
Austronesians reach the Batanes Islands of the Philippine Archipelago as part of the Austronesian expansion.
Ephemeral rule of Merenre Nemtyemsaf II in Egypt.
Possible date for the death of Pharaoh Pepi II Neferkare of the Sixth Dynasty of Egypt, the longest reigning monarch of history with 94 years on the throne.
Reign of Netjerkare Siptah, last pharaoh of the Sixth Dynasty of Egypt, who would later give rise to the legendary figure of Nitocris.
Akkadian Empire falls under attack by the Guti (Mesopotamia), a mountain people from the northeast.
Beginning of Middle Minoan period in Crete.
End of the reign of Pharaoh Neferirkare, last king of the Eighth Dynasty of Egypt. Beginning of the Ninth Dynasty, possibly after the overthrow of Neferirkare.
City state of Lagash in Mesopotamia is established.
The Epic of Gilgamesh is written in Mesopotamia in Akkadian.
Gudea, ruler (ensi) of Lagash, starts to reign.
"Model of a house and garden, from Thebes", Eleventh Dynasty of Egypt.
Gudea, ruler (ensi) of Lagash, dies.
Votive statue of Gudea from Lagash (modern Iraq) is made.
Utu-hengal, first king of the third dynasty of Ur, also called the Neo-Sumerian Empire.
Sumerian campaigns of Ur-Nammu.
The "Priest-king torso" was sculpted at Mohenjo-Daro, part of the Indus Valley Civilization.
Ancient Egypt: Pharaoh Mentuhotep IV died. End of Eleventh Dynasty. Pharaoh Amenemhat I started to rule. Start of Twelfth Dynasty.
Pharaoh Mentuhotep II, Eleventh dynasty of Egypt dies.
Political authority became less centralized in Ancient Egypt.
Erishum I became the thirty-third ruler of Assyria.
Senusret I launches a military campaign against Lower Nubia and conquers the region down to the Second Cataract.
The so-called king of Leubingen (today part of Sömmerda) was buried in a large barrow within a stone cairn inside a ring ditch.
"Harvest scene", tempera facsimile by Nina de Garis Davies of wall painting in the tomb of Khnumhotep II, Beni Hasan. Twelfth Dynasty.
Gungunum, king of Larsa, conquers Isin and takes its king Lipit-Ishtar into captivity. (Middle chronology).
Jishi Gorge flood. It may have sparked the beginning of the first Chinese dynasty (Xia, Erlitou culture).
Bön founder Tonpa Shenrab Miwoche is born.
Egyptian-Nubian war.
Fall of last Sumerian dynasty.
Late Harappan phase of the Indus Valley civilization begins.
Minoan Old Palace (Protopalatial) period starts in Crete.
Port of Lothal is abandoned.
Shalim-ahum and his son Ilu-shuma began to rule the city of Assur at around this time.
The Mokaya along the Pacific coast of present-day Chiapas, Mexico were preparing cacao beverages.
Transition from Early Helladic III to Middle Helladic culture in Greece.
Senwosret II (Twelfth Dynasty) started to rule. He built Kahun near his pyramid tomb complex at el-Lahun.
"Pectoral of Senwosret II", from the tomb of princess Sithathoryunet at el-Lahun was made. Twelfth Dynasty. It is now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
Pharaoh Senwosret II starts to rule.
Senwosret II (Twelfth Dynasty) died.
Senwosret III (Twelfth Dynasty) started to rule.
Pharaoh Senwosret II dies.
Pharaoh Senwosret III starts to rule.
Amenemhat III starts to rule.
Senusret III inspects the Nubian frontier, he leads four punitive campaigns against the Nubians.
Pharaoh Senwosret III dies.
Senwosret III (Twelfth Dynasty) died.
Head of Senusret III is made. Twelfth dynasty of Egypt. It is now kept at The Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City, Missouri.
The oldest known medical text in Egyptian history, the Kahun Gynaecological Papyrus, is written.
Shamshi-Adad I returns from exile and conquers Assur, emerging as the first Amorite king of Assyria.
Beginning of the Indo-Aryan migration.
Beginning of the Nordic Bronze Age in the period system devised by Oscar Montelius.
Decline of the Indus Valley Civilisation.
Amorite conquests of Uruk and Isin.
Egypt: Queen Sobekneferu dies. End of Twelfth Dynasty, start of Thirteenth Dynasty, start of Fourteenth Dynasty.
Zimrilim, the King of Mari, starts to rule.
Shang conquest of the Xia dynasty. China.
Mari sacked by Hammurabi. Zimrilim's palace is destroyed.
Zimrilim, the King of Mari, dies.
A colossal volcanic eruption at Mount Veniaminof, Alaska.
Hyksos occupation of Northern Egypt.
Mesopotamian Rebellions.
Aegean metalworkers are producing decorative objects rivaling those of Ancient Near East jewelers, whose techniques they seem to borrow.
Beginning of the Late Minoan period on Crete.
Belu-bani became the King of Assyria.
Bronze Age starts in China.
Indus Valley Civilisation comes to an end but is continued by the Cemetery H culture.
Lila-Ir-Tash started to rule the Elamite Empire.
Minoan Old Palace period ends and Minoan Second Palace period starts in Crete.
Lila-Ir-Tash the ruler of the Elamite Empire died. Temti-Agun I started to rule the Elamite Empire.
Belu-bani, the King of Assyria died.
Libaia became the King of Assyria.
Temti-Agun I, the ruler of the Elamite Empire, died. Tan-Uli started to rule the Elamite Empire.
Egypt: Development of leavened bread (date approximate).
Sharma-Adad I became the King of Assyria.
Iptar-Sin became the King of Assyria.
Tan-Uli, the ruler of the Elamite Empire, died.
Collapse of the 14th Dynasty of Egypt.
Conquest of Memphis by the Hyksos and collapse of the 13th Dynasty of Egypt.
Possibly, start of the Abydos Dynasty in Upper Egypt.
Start of the 15th (Hyksos) and 16th Dynasties of Egypt.
Jie of Xia is overthrown by Tang of Shang in the Battle of Mingtiao.
Bazaia became the King of Assyria.
Lullaia becomes the King of Assyria.
Mursili I becomes King of the Hittite Empire (middle chronology).
Samsu-Ditana becomes King of Babylon (middle chronology).
Shu-Ninua became the King of Assyria.
Building of El morro del tulcán Pyramid in Colombia.
Early Mycenaean culture: weapons, Cyclopean walls, and chariots.
Sharma-Adad II became the King of Assyria.
Tang of Shang established the Shang dynasty.
The date of the earliest discovered rubber balls.
Unetice culture ends in Czech Republic, eastern Europe.
Sack of Babylon by the Hittite king Mursilis I.
The overthrow of the ruling Amorite dynasty in Aleppo, Syria.
Cretan palaces at Knossos and other centres flourish despite disasters.
Egypt: End of Fifteenth Dynasty, end of Sixteenth Dynasty, end of Seventeenth Dynasty, start of Eighteenth Dynasty.
Shang dynasty of China established (according to the Bamboo Annals).
End of Seventeenth dynasty of Egypt, start of the Eighteenth Dynasty upon the coronation of Ahmose I (Low Chronology).
The city of Mycenae, located in the northeast Peloponnesus, comes to dominate the rest of Achaea, giving its name to Mycenaean civilization.
End of the First Dynasty of Babylon and the start of the Kassite dynasty—see History of Iraq.
End of Fifteenth Dynasty of Egypt.
The flood of Deucalion, according to O'Flaherty, Augustine, Eusebius, and Isidore (bishop of Seville).
Cecrops I, legendary King of Athens, dies after a reign of 50 years. Having survived his own son, he is succeeded by Cranaus.
Egypt conquers Nubia and the Levant.
Egypt started to conquer Nubia and the Levant.
Birth of Zoroaster (Avestan: Zarathushtra).
Early traces of Maya civilization developing in Belize.
Indo-Aryan migration is often dated to the 17th to 16th centuries.
Many scholars date early parts of the Rig Veda to roughly the 16th century.
Queen Hatsheput in Egypt.
Settlers from Crete, Greece move to Miletus, Turkey.
The Battle of the Ten Kings took place around this time.
The Phoenicians develop an alphabet—see Timeline of communication technology.
The element Mercury has been discovered in Egyptian tombs dating from this decade.
Amphictyon, son of Deucalion and Pyrrha and legendary King of Athens, dies after a reign of 10 years and is succeeded by Erichthonius I of Athens, a grandson of Cranaus.
Legendary King Erichthonius I of Athens dies after a reign of 50 years and is succeeded by his son Pandion I.
Beginning of Hittite empire.
Linear A reaches its peak of popularity.
The height of the Canaanite town of Ugarit. Royal Palace of Ugarit is built.
In Crete the use of bronze helmets (discovery at Knossos).
Palace of Minos destroyed by fire.
The heyday of the Phoenician city of Ugarit. A written alphabet is attested by Ugaritic texts.
A Mycenaean sanctuary is built in Phylakopi.
Joshua, leader of the Israelites, from the Hebrew Bible, is likely to have died around this time.
Akhetaton (Amarna) is constructed as the ephemeral capital of the pharaoh Akhenaten and dedicated to the sun god Aten. It is abandoned a few years after Akhenaten's death.
Phase III A2 of the Late Helladic period in Greece.
The Hagia Triada Sarcophagus is created in Crete.
The Bajío phase of the San Lorenzo site in Mexico; large public buildings are constructed.
The Igihalkid dynasty in Elam. They resume the title of "Kings of Anshan and Susa".
The reconstruction of the palace and Cyclopean enclosure at Mycenae, then at its peak under the reign of the legendary king and queen Perseus and Andromeda.
Phase III B of the Late Helladic period in Greece. Beehive tombs are constructed in Epirus and Thessaly, and a palace is constructed in Athens.
Pharaoh Tutankhamun dies and is buried in a richly furnished tomb in the Valley of the Kings.
The sinking of the Uluburun shipwreck in the Mediterranean Sea south of modern-day Kaş.
Approximately 4,000 men fight a battle at a causeway over the Tollense valley in Northern Germany, the largest known prehistoric battle north of the Alps.
The Lusatian culture in Poland, parts of the Czech Republic and Slovakia, eastern Germany and northern Ukraine.
The Egyptian and Hittite Empires clash in the Battle of Kadesh, with heavy losses to each side but no decisive outcome.
Lapita pottery discovered at the Bourewa site southwest of Viti Levu dates back to this period.
The Urnfield culture, characterized by vast cemeteries housing urns with the ashes of the deceased and offerings, marks the Late Bronze Age in Western Europe.
The culture of Pantalica develops inland in Sicily.
The Phoenicians found the port of Lisbon, Portugal.
The beginning of the first period by Shao Yong's concept of the I Ching and history.
Wu Ding, King of the Shang dynasty, dies.
End of the Nineteenth Dynasty of Egypt, start of the Twentieth Dynasty.
Collapse of Hittite power in Anatolia with the destruction of their capital Hattusa.
The last Kassite King, Anllil-nadin-akhe, is defeated by the Elamites.
Death of Pharaoh Ramesses V, from smallpox.
The Hekla 3 eruption triggers an 18-year period of climatic cooling.
Death of exiled Queen Helen of Sparta at Rhodes (estimated date).
Ramesses VII begins his reign as the sixth ruler of the Twentieth Dynasty of Egypt.
Legendary founding date of the city of Pyongyang.
Tiglath-Pileser I becomes King of Assyria.
Pharaoh Ramesses X of Egypt dies and is succeeded by Ramesses XI, probably his son, as 10th and final pharaoh of the Twentieth Dynasty of Egypt and last ruler of the New Kingdom of Egypt.
Tiglath-Pileser I of Assyria conquers the Hittites.
Melanthus, legendary King of Athens, dies after a reign of 37 years and is succeeded by his son Codrus.
Ramesses XI dies, ending the Twentieth Dynasty. He is succeeded by Smendes I, who founds the Twenty-first Dynasty.
Philistines capture the Ark of the Covenant from Israel in battle. (Approximate date).
Medon, King of Athens, dies after a reign of 20 years and is succeeded by his son Acastus.
King Wu of Zhou overthrows the last Shang dynasty king Di Xin and becomes first king of the Zhou dynasty founded by his father King Wen of Zhou.
On the death of Smendes I, king of Egypt, he is succeeded by two co-regents, Psusennes I and Neferkare Amenemnisu.
King Cheng of Zhou succeeds King Wu as ruler of the Zhou dynasty in China.
Neferkare Amenemnisu, king of Egypt, dies.
Saul becomes the first king of the Israelites, according to the Books of Samuel.
King Kang of Zhou succeeds King Cheng as ruler of the Zhou dynasty in China.
Acastus, King of Athens, dies after a reign of 36 years and is succeeded by his son Archippus.
India—Iron Age of India. Indian kingdoms rule India—Panchala, Kuru, Kosala, Pandya and Videha.
Amenemope succeeds Psusennes I as king of Egypt.
Archippus, King of Athens dies after a reign of 19 years and is succeeded by his son Thersippus.
Osorkon the Elder succeeds Amenemope as king of Egypt.
The end of first period by Sau Yung's concept of the I Ching and history.
Siamun succeeds Osorkon the Elder as king of Egypt.
Tiglath-Pileser II becomes King of Assyria.
David, king of the United Monarchy, dies.
Solomon becomes king of Israel, following the death of his father, King David. (traditional date).
Psusennes II succeeds Siamun as king of Egypt.
Solomon completes the construction of the First Temple in Jerusalem.
Alternative date to the founding of Rome.
Thersippus, King of Athens dies after a reign of 41 years and is succeeded by his son Phorbas.
Death of King Mo of Zhou, king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
King Gong of Zhou becomes king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
Egypt: Psusennes II dies, the last pharaoh of the Twenty-first Dynasty. Shoshenq I succeeds him, and founds the Twenty-second Dynasty.
Death of King Gong of Zhou, king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
Death of Tiglath-Pileser II king of Assyria.
Solomon, king of the ancient Israelites, dies.
Phorbas, King of Athens, dies after a reign of 30 years and is succeeded by his son Megacles.
Adad-nirari II succeeds his father Ashur-Dan II as king of Assyria.
Abijah, king of Judah, dies.
Jeroboam, the first king of the northern Hebrew kingdom of Israel, dies and is succeeded by his son Nadab.
The first year of King Yih of Zhou's reign is marked by a solar eclipse.
King Xiao of Zhou overthrows King Yih of Zhou and takes the throne.
Megacles, King of Athens, dies after a reign of 30 years and is succeeded by his son Diognetus.
Tukulti-Ninurta II succeeds his father Adad-nirari II as king of Assyria.
Naples some reports and excavations about the foundation of the city.
Soshenq II succeeds Osorkon I as king of Egypt.
King Yi of Zhou, son of King Yih, is restored to the throne.
Takelot I succeeds Soshenq II as king of Egypt.
Ashurnasirpal II succeeds his father Tukulti-Ninurta II as king of Assyria.
Death of King Yi of Zhou, king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
King Li of Zhou becomes king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
Ahab becomes king of Kingdom of Israel (approximate date).
Osorkon II succeeds Takelot I as king of the Twenty-second Dynasty of Egypt.
An exceptionally high flood from the Nile covers the floors of the Temple of Luxor.
Parshvanatha, 23rd Tirthankara of Jainism was born.
Kar Kalmaneser was conquered by the Assyrian king Shalmaneser III.
Diognetus, Archon of Athens, dies after a reign of 28 years and is succeeded by his son Pherecles.
The kingdom of Urartu is unified.
Aramu becomes king of Urartu.
Shalmaneser III succeeds Ashurnasirpal II as king of Assyria.
Battle of Karkar—An indecisive engagement between Assyrian king Shalmaneser III and a military alliance of the king of Damascus and lesser powers including the prince of Tyre.
Takelot II ascends to the throne of Upper Egypt.
The Middle Mumun Pottery Period begins in the Korean peninsula.
Pherecles, Archon of Athens, dies after a reign of 19 years and is succeeded by his son Ariphron.
Shalmaneser III devastates the territory of Damascus; Kingdom of Israel and the Phoenician cities send tribute.
Ahaziah of Judah and Jehoram of Israel are assassinated, either by the Israelite usurper Jehu, or the newly crowned Hazael of Aram-Damascus, per the Tel Dan stele.
Exile of King Li of Zhou, King of the Zhou dynasty of China.
Records of the Grand Historian regards this year as the first year of consecutive annual dating of Chinese history.
Gopala Dynasty started in Nepal, first dynasty to rule in a country named Nepal despite its present geographical boundaries.
Civil war breaks out in Egypt.
Shalmaneser III of Assyria leads an expedition against the Tabareni.
King Xuan of Zhou becomes King of the Zhou dynasty of China.
Ariphron, King of Athens, dies after a reign of 20 years and is succeeded by his son Thespieus.
Takelot II, king of Egypt, dies. Crown Prince Osorkon III and Shoshenq III, sons of Takelot, battle for the throne.
Death of Shalmaneser III, king of Assyria. He is succeeded by his son Shamshi-Adad V.
Pygmalion ascends the throne of Tyre.
Pedubastis I declares himself king of Egypt, founding the Twenty-third Dynasty.
Carthage is founded by Dido (traditional date).
Adad-nirari III succeeds his father Shamshi-Adad V as king of Assyria.
Adad-nirari III of Assyria conquers Damascus.
Death of Pedubastis I, pharaoh.
Etruscan civilization.
Thespieus, King of Athens, dies after a reign of 27 years and is succeeded by his son Agamestor.
Shalmaneser IV succeeds his father Adad-nirari III as king of Assyria.
Death of King Xuan of Zhou, king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
Founding of Erebuni (Էրեբունի) by the orders of King Argishtis I at the site of current-day Yerevan.
King You of Zhou becomes king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
The first historic solar eclipse is recorded in China.
Agamestor, King of Athens, dies after a reign of 17 years and is succeeded by his son Aeschylus.
Retrospectively set as the first Olympiad. The history of the Olympic Games is believed to reach as far back as the 13th century BC.
End of the reign of king Pygmalion of Tyre.
Ashur-Dan III succeeds his brother Shalmaneser IV as king of Assyria.
Death of Shoshenq III, king of Egypt.
Pārśvanātha, 23rd Tirthankara of Jainism died and attained nirvana.
End of the Western Zhou dynasty in China as "western" barbarian tribes sack the capital Hao. King You of Zhou is killed. Crown Prince Ji Yijiu escapes and will reign as King Ping of Zhou.
Beginning of the Eastern Zhou dynasty in China as King Ping of Zhou becomes the first King of the Zhou to rule from the new capital of Chengzhou (today Luoyang).
Founding of Cyzicus.
Aeschylus, King of Athens, dies after a reign of 23 years and is succeeded by Alcmaeon.
Ashur-nirari V succeeds Ashur-Dan III as king of Assyria.
Alcmaeon, King of Athens, dies after a reign of 2 years. He is replaced by Harops, elected Archon for a ten-year term.
Meles becomes king of Lydia.
The Lusatian culture city at Biskupin is founded.
The crown of Assyria is seized by Pul, who takes the name Tiglath-Pileser III.
Duke Zhuang of the Chinese state of Zheng comes to power.
Start of Ahaz's reign of Judah.
Tiglath-Pileser III conquers the city of Arpad in Syria after two years of siege.
Hiram II becomes king of Tyre.
King Tiglath-Pileser III of Assyria invades Israel, forcing it to pay tribute.
Naxus in Sicily founded as a colony of Chalcis in Euboea. (traditional date).
Syracuse (Sicily) was founded as a colony by Corinth.
Hoshea becomes the last king of Israel.
Mattan II succeeds Hiram II as king of Tyre.
Osorkon IV succeeds Sheshonq IV as king of the Twenty-second dynasty of Egypt.
Piye succeeds his father Kashta as king of the Nubian kingdom of Napata.
Piye invades Egypt, conquering Memphis, and receives the submission of the rulers of the Nile Delta. He founds the Twenty-fifth Dynasty of Egypt.
Babylonia makes itself independent of Assyria.
The Assyrians start a four-year siege of Tyre.
The diaulos footrace introduced at the Olympics.
Israel is conquered by Assyrian king Sargon II.
Spring and Autumn period of China's history begins as King Ping of Zhou of the Zhou dynasty reigns in name only.
End of the Assyrian siege of Tyre.
King Huan of Zhou of the Zhou dynasty becomes ruler of China.
Gyges becomes the ruler of Lydia.
Assyrian king Sargon conquers the Hittite stronghold of Carchemish.
Sargon II founds a new capital for Assyria at Dur-Sharrukin.
Roman legend marks this as the date that Romulus ended his rule.
Start of the reign of Roman King Numa Pompilius.
Numa Pompilius reforms the Roman calendar.
Numa Pompilius creates the office of Pontifex Maximus.
Spartan immigrants found Taras (Tarentum, the modern Taranto) colony in southern Italy.
Sennacherib succeeds Sargon II as king of Assyria.
Sennacherib moves the capital of Assyria to Nineveh.
King Hezekiah of Judah, backed by Egypt, revolts against king Sennacherib of Assyria. Sennacherib sacks many cities, but fails in his attempt to take Jerusalem.
End of the Villanovan culture in northern Italy and rise of the Etruscan civilization.
The Scythians start settling in Cimmerian areas, slowly replacing the previous inhabitants.
The Upanishads, a sacred text of Hinduism, are written around this time.
Khallushu succeeds Shuttir-Nakhkhunte as king of the Elamite Empire.
Death of King Huan of Zhou, king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
King Zhuang of Zhou becomes king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
The Cimmerians ravage Phrygia, possible migration of the Armenians.
King Sennacherib of Assyria defeats king Humban-nimena of Elam in the Battle of Halule.
Taharqa, a king of the Twenty-fifth Dynasty, ascends the throne of Egypt (approximate date).
King Sennacherib of Assyria sacks Babylon.
Gyges becomes king of Lydia.
Hezekiah succeeded by Manasseh as king of Judah.
Death of King Zhuang of Zhou, king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
Esarhaddon succeeds Sennacherib as king of Assyria.
King Xi of Zhou becomes king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
Phraortes becomes king of the Medes.
Death of King Xi of Zhou, king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
Esarhaddon leads the Assyrian army against rebellious Arab tribes and advances as far as the Brook of Egypt.
King Hui of Zhou becomes king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
Esarhaddon begins the rebuilding of Babylon.
Teispes becomes a king of Anshan.
Esarhaddon puts down a revolt in Ascalon supported by Taharqa, king of Egypt. In response, the Assyrians invade Egypt, but Taharqa can hold the invaders off.
Tullus Hostilius becomes king of Rome.
Esarhaddon again invades Egypt, capturing Memphis as well as a number of the royal family.
Argos defeats Sparta for the last time, this time using a hoplite phalanx, at the battle of Hysiae.
Assurbanipal succeeds his father Esarhaddon as king of Assyria.
Egypt revolts against Assyria.
Nineveh, capital of Assyria, becomes the largest city of the world, taking the lead from Thebes in Egypt.
Shamash-shum-ukin, son of Esarhaddon, becomes King of Babylon.
Byzantium founded by Megaran colonists under Byzas. (traditional date).
Assurbanipal captures and sacks Thebes, Egypt.
First naval battle in Greek recorded history, between Corinth and Corcyra.
Psamtik I succeeds Necho I as king of Lower Egypt.
Taharqa appoints his nephew Tantamani as his successor of Upper Egypt.
Estimated date of the impact that created the Kaali crater.
First known use of the Demotic script.
Psamtik I drives the Assyrians out of Egypt.
Cypselus becomes the first tyrant of Corinth.
Psamtik I extends his control over all of Egypt. End of Twenty-fifth Dynasty.
The Fall of Ashdod to the Egyptian forces. Psamtik I besieged Ashdod for almost three decades.
Atlanersa becomes ruler of the Napatan kingdom of Kush after the collapse of the Twenty-fifth Dynasty of Egypt.
Atta-Khumma-In-Shushinak and Khumbanigash II succeed Shilhak-In-Shushinak and Tempti-Khumma-In-Shushinak as kings of the Elamite Empire.
Babylonia rises in revolt under Shamash-shum-ukin against the Assyrians.
King Xiang of Zhou becomes king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
The town of Abdera in Thrace is founded by colonists from Clazomenae.
Babylonian revolt under Shamash-shum-ukin is crushed by the Assyrians.
Indabigash succeeds Tammaritu as a king of the Elamite Empire.
Pankration becomes an event at the Ancient Olympic Games.
King Assurbanipal of Assyria sacks Susa.
Ancus Marcius becomes king of Rome (traditional date).
Decisive victory of Assyria over Elamite Empire; Assurbanipal captures its last king Khumma-Khaldash III, annexes Elam, and lays waste the country.
Cylon, Athenian noble, seizes the Acropolis in a failed attempt to become king.
In the Battle of Chengpu, the Chinese kingdom of Jin and her allies defeat the kingdom of Chu and her allies.
Founding of Cyrene, a Greek colony in Libya (North Africa) (approximate date).
Sadyates becomes king of Lydia.
Death of Assurbanipal, king of Assyria; he is succeeded by Assur-etel-ilani (approximate date).
Nabopolassar revolts against Assyria, founds the Neo-Babylonian Empire.
Cyaxares becomes king of the Median Empire.
Medes and Babylonians assert their independence from Assyria and attack Nineveh (approximate date).
Sin-shar-ishkun succeeds his brother Assur-etel-ilani as king of Assyria (approximate date).
Text of Deuteronomy found in the Temple in Jerusalem. The Hebrew prophet Ezekiel said to be born this year.
Alyattes becomes king of Lydia.
Death of King Xiang of Zhou, king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
King Qing of Zhou becomes king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
Lucius Tarquinius Priscus becomes king of Rome.
Sack of Ashur by the Medes and Babylonians.
Death of King Qing of Zhou, king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
An alliance of Medes, Babylonians and Susianians besiege and conquer Nineveh. King Sin-shar-ishkun of Assyria is killed in the sack.
Ashur-uballit II attempts to keep the Assyrian empire alive by establishing himself as king at Harran.
Babylon, capital of Babylonia becomes the largest city of the world, taking the lead from Nineveh, capital of Assyria.
King Kuang of Zhou becomes king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
Necho II succeeds Psammetichus I as king of Egypt.
Jehoahaz succeeds his father Josiah as King of Judah, but is quickly deposed by Necho, who installs Jehoahaz's brother Jehoiakim in his place.
King Josiah of Judah dies in the Battle of Megiddo against Pharaoh Necho II of Egypt, who is on his way north to aid the rump Assyrian state of Ashur-uballit II.
The Babylonians defeat the Assyrian army of Ashur-uballit II and capture Harran. Ashur-uballit, the last Assyrian king, disappears from history.
Death of King Kuang of Zhou, king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
King Ding of Zhou becomes king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
Nebuchadnezzar II succeeds his father Nabopolassar as King of Babylon.
An alliance of Medes (from western Iran) and Scythians (who originated from the Eurasian Steppe) invade the northern and eastern parts of Assyria.
Foundation of Capua.
Foundation of Marseille by Phoceans (traditional date).
Foundation of Milan by Celts (approximate date).
Nebuchadnezzar builds the Hanging Gardens of Babylon.
Smyrna sacked and destroyed.
Jehoiachin succeeds Jehoiakim as King of Judah.
Psammetichus II succeeds Necho II as King of Egypt.
Solon appointed Archon of Athens; institutes democratic reforms.
Egyptian army sacks Napata, compelling the Cushite court to move to a more secure location at Meroe near the sixth Cataract.
Apries succeeds Psammetichus II as King of Egypt.
Jerusalem falls to the Babylonians, ending the Kingdom of Judah. The conquerors destroy Solomon's Temple and exile the land's remaining inhabitants. Babylonian Captivity for the Jews begins.
Death of King Ding of Zhou, king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
Astyages succeeds Cyaxares as King of the Medes.
King Jian of Zhou becomes king of the Zhou dynasty.
The Babylonians begin a siege against Tyre.
Pythian Games founded at Delphi (traditional date).
Cambyses I succeeds Cyrus I as King of Anshan and head of the Achaemenid dynasty (approximate date).
Isthmian Games founded at Corinth (traditional date).
Servius Tullius succeeds the assassinated Lucius Tarquinius Priscus as King of Rome (traditional date).
Nemean Games founded at Nemea (traditional date).
Death of King Jian of Zhou, king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
King Ling of Zhou becomes king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
Amasis II succeeds Apries as King of Egypt.
End of the Babylonian siege against the city of Tyre with a partial victory by the Babylonians. It was the longest siege of the city in history, lasting 13 years.
Pythagoras of Samos is born (approximate date).
Amtalqa succeeds his brother Aspelta as King of Kush.
Amel-Marduk succeeds Nebuchadnezzar as King of Babylon.
Croesus becomes King of Lydia.
Neriglissar succeeds Amel-Marduk as King of Babylon.
Pisistratus seizes the Acropolis of Athens and declares himself tyrant. He is deposed in the same year.
King Cambyses I of Anshan dies and is succeeded by his son Cyrus II the Great.
Hegesias removed as Archon of Athens.
The Chinese state of Jin defeats its rival Qin in battle.
Labashi-Marduk succeeds Neriglissar as King of Babylon.
Nabonidus succeeds Labashi-Marduk as King of Babylon.
Pisistratus is exiled from Athens to Euboea.
Medo-Persian conflict; Cyrus II overthrows the Median king Astyages, establishing the Persian Empire.
Abdera is destroyed by the Thracians.
The Late Mumun Period begins in the Korean peninsula.
Croesus, Lydian King, is defeated by Cyrus of Persia near the River Halys.
Cyrus of Persia completes his conquest of Lydia, and makes Pasargadae his capital.
Bimbisara establishes Haryanka dynasty of Magadha in India.
King Jing of Zhou becomes king of the Zhou dynasty of China.
People of Teos migrate to Abdera, Thrace to escape the yoke of Persia.
Pisistratus, tyrant of Athens, purifies the island of Delos (approximate date).
Prince Vijaya establishes a Sinhalese dynasty of Sri Lanka.
Greek city of Elea of southern Italy founded (approximate date).
Persians conquer Lycian city of Xanthos, now in southern Turkey (approximate date).
Babylon is conquered by Cyrus the Great, defeating Nabonidus.
Jews transported to Babylon are allowed to return to Jerusalem, bringing to a close the Babylonian captivity.
According to tradition, the Biblical prophet Daniel receives an angelic visit from the archangel Gabriel.
Competitions for tragedy are instituted at the City Dionysia festival in Athens.
Lucius Tarquinius Superbus becomes King of Rome.
Cambyses II succeeds Cyrus as King of Persia.
Gautama Buddha attains Enlightenment, and begins his ministry. He founds Buddhism in India. It becomes a major world religion.
Psammetichus III succeeds Amasis II as King of Egypt.
Cambyses II, ruler of Persia, conquers Egypt, defeating Psammetichus III. This is considered the end of the Twenty-sixth Dynasty, and the start of the Twenty-seventh Dynasty.
Babylon rebels against Persian rule.
Smerdis succeeds Cambyses II as ruler of Persia.
Darius I succeeds Smerdis as ruler of Persia.
The Babylonian rebellion against Persian rule is suppressed.
Cleomenes I succeeds Anaxandridas II as King of Sparta (approximate date).
King Dao of Zhou becomes king of the Zhou dynasty of China but dies before the end of the year.
Start of construction of a colossal new Temple of Olympian Zeus (Athens) by Pisistratus's sons, Hippias and Hipparchos (approximate date).
Indian subcontinent—Occupation of Punjab is completed by the Achaemenid King Darius I.
King Helü of Wu establishes the "Great City of Helü", the ancient name for Wuxi, as his capital in China.
Darius the Great subdues the Getae and east Thrace in his war against the Scythians.
The Kingdom of Macedonia, under King Amyntas I, becomes a vassal state to the Achaemenid Empire.
Demaratus succeeds Ariston as King of Sparta (approximate date).
End of reign of Lucius Tarquinius Superbus, last King of the traditional seven Kings of Rome.
Establishment of the Roman Republic.
Hippias, son of Pisistratus and tyrant of Athens, is expelled by a popular revolt supported by Cleomenes I, King of Sparta and his forces.
Office of pontifex maximus created in Rome.
Cleisthenes, Greek reformer, takes power and increases democracy.
Battle of Boju: Forces of the Kingdom of Wu under Sun Tzu defeat the forces of Chu.
First pair of Roman consuls elected.
Naxos rebels against Persian domination sparking the Ionian Revolt.
The Latin League defeats the Etruscans under Lars Porsena at Aricia.
Cleisthenes reforms democracy in Athens.
Confucius is appointed governor of Chung tu.
Gadir (present-day Cádiz) is captured by Carthage (approximate date).
In response to threats by the Sabines, Rome creates the office of dictator.
Naxos is attacked by the Persian Empire.
Bantu-speaking people migrate into south-west Uganda from the west (approximate date).
Darius I of Persia proclaims that Aramaic be the official language of the western half of his empire.
Foundation of first republic in Vaishali Bihar India.
Refugees from Teos resettle Abdera.
Sa Huynh-Kalanay Interaction Sphere extensive trade network started between the Sa Huynh and the Philippines and later expanded to Taiwan, Southern Thailand, and northeastern Borneo.
Signifies the end of the Nordic Bronze Age civilization in Oscar Montelius periodization system and begins the Pre-Roman Iron Age.
Aristagoras instigates the Ionian Revolt, beginning the Persian Wars between Greece and Persia.
Aristagoras, acting on behalf of the Persian Empire, leads a failed attack on the rebellious island of Naxos.
Sardis sacked by Athenian and Ionian troops.
Alexander I succeeds his father Amyntas I as king of Macedon.
Leontini subjugated by Hippocrates of Gela.
Battle of Lake Regillus: A legendary early Roman victory, won over either the Etruscans or the Latins.
Temple to Mercury on the Circus Maximus in Rome is built.
The Battle of Lade, where Persians take back Ionia.
The year Rome changed from an Aristocratic Republic to a Liberalized Republic.
Two tribunes of the plebs and two plebeian aediles are elected for the first time in Rome: the office of the tribunate is established.
Coriolanus captures the Volscian town of Corioli for Rome.
Piraeus, the port town of Athens, is founded.
Ajatashartu overthrows his father Bimbisara to become king of Magadha.
Gelo becomes Tyrant of Gela.
Leotychidas succeeds his cousin Demaratus as king of Sparta.
Phidippides runs 40 kilometers from Marathon to Athens to announce the news of the Greek victory; origin of the marathon long-distance race.
The Battle of Marathon, where Darius I of Persia is defeated by the Athenians and Plataeans under Miltiades.
Cities of Rhodes unite and start construction of the new city of Rhodes.
Leonidas I succeeds his brother Cleomenes I as king of Sparta after Cleomenes is judged insane.
Aegina and Athens go to war.
Athenian Archonship becomes elective by lot, an important milestone in the move towards radical Athenian democracy.
Egypt revolts against the Persians.
Siaspiqa becomes ruler of the Kushite kingdom of Meroe.
Egypt revolts against Persian rule.
First Buddhist Council at Rejgaha, under the patronage of King Ajatashatru. Oral tradition established for the first time.
First part of the Grand Canal of China is built.
Xerxes I succeeds Darius I as Great King of Persia.
Athenian playwright Aeschylus wins a poetry prize.
Persians regain control of Egypt.
Xerxes I abolishes the Kingdom of Babel and removes the golden statue of Bel (Marduk, Merodach).
Gautama Buddha dies.
Xerxes I of Persia starts planning his expedition against Greece.
The Isthmus of Corinth ends a war between Athens and Aegina.
Battle of Himera—The Carthaginians under Hamilcar are defeated by the Greeks of Sicily, led by Gelon of Syracuse.
Cimon and his friends burn horse-bridles as an offering to Athena and join the marines.
King Xerxes I of Persia sets out to conquer Greece.
Pleistarchus succeeds his father Leonidas I as king of Sparta.
Roman troops march against the Veientines.
Chinese philosopher Confucius dies.
Potidaea is struck by a tsunami.
The Battle of Plataea, the Greeks defeat the Persians, ending the Persian Wars.
Establishment of the Temple of Confucius at (modern-day) Qufu.
The Delian League is inaugurated.
Archidamus II succeeds his grandfather Leotychides, who is banished to Tegea, as king of Sparta.
King Xuan of Zhou becomes King of the Zhou dynasty.
Battle of Cumae—The Syracusans under Hiero I defeat the Etruscans and end Etruscan expansion in southern Italy.
Greek poet Pindar moves to Thebes.
The Chinese State of Wu is annexed by the State of Yue.
Carystus in Euboea is forced to join the Delian League (approximate date).
The tragedy The Persians is produced by Aeschylus.
Athenian politician Themistocles is ostracized.
Philosopher Socrates is born in Attica, Athens, Greece.
Antium captured by Roman forces.
King Zhending of Zhou becomes King of the Zhou dynasty of China.
Sophocles, Greek playwright, defeats Aeschylus for the Athenian Prize.
Delian League defeats Persia at the Battle of Eurymedon.
King Xerxes I of the Persian Empire is murdered by Artabanus the Hyrcanian. He is succeeded by Artaxerxes I, possibly with Artabanus acting as Regent.
Thasos revolts from the Delian League.
An earthquake in ancient Sparta, Greece leads to a Helot uprising and strained relations with Athens, one of the factors that lead to the Peloponnesian War.
Regent King Artabanus of Persia is killed by his charge Artaxerxes I.
Third Messenian war.
The revolt of Thasos against the Delian League comes to an end with their surrender.
Athenian politician Cimon is ostracized.
Cincinnatus becomes consul of the Roman Republic.
Egypt revolts against Persia, starting a six-year war. An Athenian force sent to attack Cyprus is diverted to support this revolt.
Physician Hippocrates is born in Kos, Greece.
Udayin succeeds his father Ajatashartu to become king of Magadha. Third king of Haryanka dynasty.
Destruction of the Sicilian town of Morgantina by Douketios, leader of the Sikels, according to Diodoros Siculus.
Ezra leads the second body of Jews from Babylon to Jerusalem.
Pleistoanax succeeds his father Pleistarchus as king of Sparta.
Greek playwright Aeschylus completes the Oresteia, a trilogy that tells the story of a family blood feud. The plays will have a great influence on future writers.
Athenian statesman Pericles' greatest reform, allowing common people to serve in any state office, inaugurates Golden Age of Ancient Athens.
Battle of Oenophyta—The Athenians defeat the Thebans and take control of Boeotia.
Battle of Tanagra—The Spartans defeat the Athenians, near Thebes.
Decree of Artaxerxes I to re-establish the city government of Jerusalem. See Ezra 7, Daniel 9 and Nehemiah 1 in Old Testament.
A thirty years' truce concluded between Athens and Lacedaemon.
Euripides presents his first known tragedy, Peliades, in the Athenian festival of Dionysia.
Athens loses a fleet and possibly as many as 50,000 men in a failed attempt to aid an Egyptian revolt against Persia.
Hostilities between Segesta and Selinunte, two Greek cities on Sicily.
The treasury of the Delian League is moved from Delos to Athens.
Taiyuan, a city in China, gets flooded.
Athens makes peace with Sparta and wages a war against Persia.
The decemviri come to power in the Roman Republic. They enact the Twelve Tables, the foundation of Roman Law.
Perdiccas II succeeds Alexander I as king of Macedonia (approximate date).
Wars of the Delian League: Athenians under Cimon defeat the Persian fleet.
Construction begins on the Temple of Hephaestus in Athens.
Herodotus completes his History, which records the events concerning the Persian War.
Romans revolt against the decemvirate. The decemvirs resign and the tribunate is re-established.
The Peace of Callias between the Delian League and Persia ends the Persian Wars.
The Twelve Tables are promulgated to the people of Rome—the first public laws of the Roman Republic.
Phidias finishes a 9 meter high statue of Athena on the Acropolis.
Achaeus of Eretria, a Greek playwright, shows his first play.
Athens begins construction of the Parthenon, at the initiative of Pericles.
Battle of Coronea—The Athenians are driven out of Boeotia.
Artaxerxes I gives Nehemiah permission to rebuild Jerusalem.
Pericles declares Thirty Years' Peace between Athens and Sparta.
The Lacus Curtius is created by a lightning strike in Rome. It is consecrated by Gaius, Mettius or Marcus Curtius.
Foundation of the Greek colony of Thurii in Italy. Its colonists include Herodotus and Lysias.
The Roman Republic creates the office of censor, initially exclusive to patricians.
Sophocles writes Antigone.
King Ai of Zhou becomes King of the Zhou dynasty of China but dies before the year's end.
Democritus proposes the existence of indivisible particles, which he calls atoms.
King Kao of Zhou becomes King of the Zhou dynasty of China.
According to legend, Gaius Servilius Ahala saves Rome from Spurius Maelius.
Cincinnatus again becomes dictator of the Roman Republic; during his term he defeats the Volsci.
Ictinus and Callicrates finish construction of the Parthenon, located on Athens' Acropolis.
The Statue of Zeus at Olympia by Phidias, one of the seven wonders of the world, is completed.
Anaxagoras tries to square the circle with a straightedge and compass.
Conflict occurs between the Greek island of Kerkyra and its mother-city Corinth.
Battle of Sybota between Kerkyra and Corinth.
Burial of Marquis Yi of Zeng in China.
Athens adopts a 19-year cycle of synchronizing solar and lunar calendars.
Athens defeats Corinth in the battle of Potidaea.
The Greek colony of Heraclea is founded by Tarentum and Thurii.
Defeat of the Aequi by the Romans under the dictator Aulus Postumius Tubertus.
The Peloponnesian War begins between Sparta and Athens and their allies.
Athens suffers a major pestilence, believed to be caused by epidemic typhus.
First performance of Sophocles's Oedipus Rex.
The philosopher Xenophon is born.
An outbreak of a plague kills over one-third of the population of Athens.
Battle of Chalcis—Chalcidians and their allies are defeated by Athens.
Battle of Naupactus—Phormio defeats the Peloponnesian fleet.
King Sitalkes of Thrace invades Macedonia.
Mytilene rebels against Athens but is crushed.
Sparta attempts to crush a rebellion on Corcyra, but cancels the effort when the Athenians try to intercept them.
The Greek colony of Cumae in Italy falls to the Samnites.
The philosopher Plato is born.
Platea surrenders to the Spartans, who execute over 200 prisoners and destroy the city.
The Athenians intervene in Sicily to blockade Sparta from the island.
The leaders of the Mytilenian revolt are executed.
Demosthenes unsuccessfully besieges the Corinthian colony of Leukas.
When Ambracia invades Acarnania, they seek help from the Spartans and Athenians respectively. The Athenians then defeat the Spartans in the Battle of Olpae.
Demosthenes captures the port of Pylos in the Peloponnesus.
The Athenians invade Sphacteria and defeat the Spartans in the Battle of Pylos.
Sicily withdraws from the war and expels every foreign power. Thus, Athens is forced to withdraw from the island.
The Athenians try to capture Megara, but are defeated by the Spartans.
The Athenians propose a cease-fire, which the Spartan general Brasidas ignores.
The Spartans defeat the Athenians in the Battle of Amphipolis, where the Athenian Cleon and the Spartan Brasidas are both killed.
The Peace of Nicias puts a temporary end to the hostilities between Athens and Sparta.
Alcibiades is elected strategos of Athens and begins dominating Athenian politics.
The Peace of Nicias is broken when Sparta defeats Argos.
The Spartans win a major victory over the Athenians in the Battle of Mantinea, the biggest land battle of the Peloponnesian War.
The Athenians adhere to a plea of help from Sicily and start planning an invasion of the island.
The Athenians capture the island of Melos and treat the inhabitants with great cruelty.
Alcibiades defects from Athens to Sparta after having learned about his death sentence.
The Athenians try to make a breakthrough in their siege of Syracuse but are defeated by the Spartans.
Caria allies itself with Sparta.
Nagadaska is deposed by people of Magadha. Thus, ending Haryanka dynasty. He succeeded by Shishunaga who founded Shaishunaga dynasty.
The Persian Empire starts preparing an invasion of Ionia and signs a treaty with Sparta about it.
Athens regains control over its vital grain route from the Black Sea by defeating Sparta in the Battle of Cyzicus.
Athens recaptures Byzantium, thereby putting an end to its revolt against Athens and taking control of the whole Bosporus.
The Carthaginians invade Sicily.
The city of Rhodes is founded.
Alcibiades returns to Athens in triumph after an absence of seven years.
The Athenian fleet is routed by the Spartan one in the Battle of Notium, which gives Alcibiades' opponents a reason to strip him of command. He never returns to Athens again.
Athens defeats Sparta in the Battle of Arginusae and the blockade of Conon is lifted.
Sparta sues for peace, but Athens rejects this.
The Carthaginians once again invade Sicily and return to Carthage with spoils of war, but also with the plague.
Dionysius the Elder rises to power in Syracuse. He signs a peace with Carthage and starts consolidating and expanding his influence.
The Spartan king Pausanias lays siege to Athens, which makes the city start starving.
Egypt rebels against Persian rule, and gains full independence and sovereignty, Amyrtaeus proclaimed pharaoh.
The Athenians adopt the Ionian alphabet.
The Chinese state of Jin is divided into three smaller nations.
The first hydraulic engineering in China for a large irrigation canal system is designed by Ximen Bao.
Thrasybulus restores the Athenian democracy and grants an almost general amnesty.
Cyrus the Younger rebels against the Persian king Artaxerxes II but is, however, eventually slain in battle.
Jōmon period ends in Ancient Japan.
London has its origins as far back as this time.
The Carthaginians occupy Malta.
The Egyptians successfully revolt against Persian rule.
The Kingdom of D'mt is disestablished.
The Greek philosopher Socrates is sentenced to death by Athenian authorities, condemned for impiety and the corruption of youth. He refuses to flee into exile and dies by drinking hemlock.
Marcus Furius Camillus is made dictator by the Romans. Camillus finally destroys the Etruscan city of Veii in southern Etruria.
Kalashoka succeeds his father Shishunaga to become king of Magadha. Second Buddhist Council is held during his reign.
The "Corinthian War" begins, with Athens, Thebes, Corinth and Argos (with the backing of Persia) against Sparta.
Dionysius I, tyrant of Syracuse, begins an attempt to extend his rule to the Greek cities of southern Italy. He unsuccessfully besieges Rhegium.
The Pharaoh of Egypt, Hakor (Akoris), concludes a tripartite alliance with Evagoras, king of Cyprus, and Athens.
Plato, having left Athens on Socrates' death to visit Megara and possibly Egypt, travels to Syracuse at the invitation of Dionysius I's brother-in-law Dion.
The Chinese city of Handan is founded by the State of Zhao.
Lysias, the Athenian orator, on the occasion of the Olympiad, rebukes the Greeks for allowing themselves to be dominated by the Syracusan tyrant Dionysius I and by the barbarian Persians.
The Greeks found the colony of Pharos at the site of today's Stari Grad on the island of Hvar, defeating Iadasinoi warriors brought in for its defense.
The 19 year lunar cycle is introduced into the Babylonian calendar.
The second Buddhist council is convened by king Kalasoka and held at Vaisali.
Wu Qi is assassinated at the funeral of King Diao of Chu, although his assassins are executed shortly after by the newly enthroned King Su of Chu.
Cleombrotus I succeeds his brother Agesipolis I as king of Sparta.
The states of Han, Wei and Zhao deposed Duke Jing of Jin and divided the last remaining Jin territory between themselves, which marked the final end of the Jin state.
Duke Xiao became ruler of Qin.
Shang Yang implemented his first set of reforms in Qin.
Duke Hui of Wei is the first to claim the royal title of king (Chinese: 王) for himself, proclaiming themselves fully independent kingdoms.
The rulers of Qi and Wei mutually recognized each other as "kings": King Wei of Qi and King Hui of Wei, in effect declaring their independence from the Zhou court.
King Huiwen becomes ruler of Qin.
Alexander fights his last great battle, the Battle of the Hydaspes river. He and his general Craterus defeat the Indian king Porus.
Alexander the Great dies in Babylon.
Chandragupta Maurya overthrows Dhana Nanda with help his guru Chanakya and becomes King of Magadha having Durdhara (Dhana Nanda's sister) as queen. Establishment of the Maurya dynasty.
Qin conquers Shu and Ba.
Upon the ascension of King Nan, East Zhou becomes an independent state. The king comes to reside in what becomes known as West Zhou.
King Hui of Qin dies, follows by prime minister Zhang Yi one year later. The new monarch, King Wu, reigns only four years before dying without legitimate heirs.
Ptolemy personally commands a fleet that captures the coastal regions of Lycia and Caria from Antigonus.
Cleopatra of Macedon is assassinated by the order of Antigonus.
Ptolemy crosses from Asia Minor into Greece, where he takes possession of Corinth, Sicyon and Megara.
Ptolemy makes peace with Cassander.
The Chinese King Wuling of Zhao reforms the military of the State of Zhao by putting more emphasis on cavalry over charioteers.
The city of Segesta in Sicily is destroyed by Agathocles.
The tyrant Agathocles takes on the title of King of Sicily. He extends his influence into southern Italy and the Adriatic.
The southern part of Syria is occupied by Ptolemy.
The end of the 4th century BC and the start of the 3rd century BC.
The Samnites defeat the Romans under Lucius Cornelius Scipio Barbatus in the Battle of Camerinum, the first battle of the Third Samnite War.
The Chinese State of Qin reduced the threat of the State of Wei and the State of Han with the Qin victory in the Battle of Yique.
The Pharos of Alexandria is completed.
Achaean League founded in Greece.
Antiochus I Soter, on the assassination of his father Seleucus becomes emperor of the Seleucid Empire.
Construction of the Colossus of Rhodes is completed.
King Pyrrhus of Epirus invades Italy in an attempt to subjugate the Romans and bring Italy under a new empire ruled by himself.
Singidunum and Taurunum, today's Belgrade and Zemun, are founded by Scordisci Celts.
In the Battle of Lysimachia, the invasion by Gauls is finally defeated by Antigonus II of Macedon.
The First Syrian War erupts between Antiochus I Soter of the Seleucid dynasty and Ptolemy II Philadelphus of the Ptolemaic dynasty over control of Syria and southern Anatolia.
Ashoka the Great ruled the Maurya Empire.
Kalinga War takes place between Ashoka the Great and the kingdom of Kalinga.
First Punic War breaks out between the Carthaginian Empire and the Roman Republic.
Antiochus II Theos, 2nd son, at the death of his father becomes emperor of the Seleucid Empire.
Ashoka inscribes the Edicts of Ashoka.
Battle of Changping between the State of Qin and the State of Zhao in China; a decisive Qin victory.
An Dương Vương overthrows the Hồng Bàng dynasty in Viet Nam.
Thục dynasty takes over Vietnam.
The death of Antiochus II sparks the Third Syrian War; Ptolemy III conquers Syria and Babylon from the Seleucids, but loses the Nesiotic League to Antigonus II.
Surprise attack on the Macedonian garrison at Corinth. Expansion of the Achaean League.
First Punic War ends in Carthaginian defeat. Rome demands large reparations, and annexes Sicily and Corsica.
On May 15, Chinese mathematicians observed and recorded the passage of the Halley's Comet.
Simuka declares independence from Mauryan rule and establishes the Satavahana Empire.
The Chinese Qin State conquers Han.
Last tyrants on the Peloponnese abdicate, Argos joins the Achaean League, Athens liberated from Macedonian garrison.
The First Illyrian War ends with a Roman victory.
The attempted assassination of Ying Zheng (嬴政), king of Qin State, by Jing Ke (荊軻) from Yan failed.
A large Gallic army is defeated by the Romans at the Battle of Telamon.
The Chinese Qin State conquers Wei.
The Chinese Qin State conquers Chu.
Spartan defeat in the Battle of Sellasia ends the Cleomenean War.
The Chinese Qin State conquers Yan and Zhao.
With the conquest of the State of Qi, Qin Shi Huang (秦始皇) unifies the whole of China into one empire that also included northern Vietnam, forming the Qin dynasty.
Second Punic War begins. Hannibal makes his famous Alpine crossing to invade Italy, the Roman heartland.
Antiochus III invades the Levant in the Third Syrian War, but is defeated by Ptolemy IV at the Battle of Raphia.
Hannibal famously crushed the Roman legions at the Battle of Cannae.
Qin Shi Huang (秦始皇) of the Chinese Qin dynasty ordered construction of the Great Wall of China.
Qin Shi Huang dies while on a trip to the far eastern reaches of his empire in an attempt to procure an elixir of immortality from Taoist magicians.
Zhao Tuo (Triệu Đà) defeats the Vietnamese king An Dương Vương.
Triệu dynasty of Viet Nam is inaugurated.
Civil war of the Chu-Han contention in China.
Qin dynasty falls after men from all over China revolts, attacking officials, raising armies, and declaring themselves kings of seized territories.
The Cretan War begins between Macedonia and its allies against the Greek polis of Rhodes and its allies, resulting in a Rhodian victory.
In East Asia, the Chu-Han contention comes to a close, Xiang Yu commits suicide, and the Han dynasty of China is founded by Liu Bang.
Romans defeat Carthage, ending the Second Punic War. Carthage's territories are reduced to some of its North African holdings, and crippling reparations are demanded by Rome.
Battle of Panium: Antiochus III of the Seleucid Empire defeats Ptolemy V of Egypt.
The Second Macedonian War between Rome and Macedon begins.
Fifth Syrian War: Antiochus III takes control of Coele Syria and Judea.
(June) Flamininus defeats Philip V, king of Antigonid Macedonia at the Battle of Cynoscephalae, ending the Second Macedonian War.
Battle of Thermopylae: Manius Acilius Glabrio drives Antiochus III out of Greece.
Battle of Magnesia: Rome and Pergamon drive Antiochus III out of Asia Minor.
Galatian War: Gnaeus Manlius Vulso and Pergamon defeat the Galatians.

The Xiongnu attack northern China.

The Lusitanians begin the Lusitanian War against Rome.
Alexander Balas starts a revolt against Demetrius I Soter with the support of Jonathan Maccabaeus.
Hasmonean victories restore autonomy to Judea.

Hyspaosines of Characene takes control of Babylonia.
Ptolemy VIII regains control of Alexandria.
Zhang Qian returns to China after a protracted journey through the west.
Artabanus II of Parthia is killed in battle with the Yuezhi and succeeded by his son Mithridates II.
Mithradates II of Parthia regains control of Babylonia and Characene.
Assassination of Gaius Gracchus.
Ptolemy VIII of Egypt dies and is succeeded by his wife Cleopatra III and son Ptolemy IX Soter.
The Cimbri and Teutones arrive on the banks of the Danube in Noricum, clashing with Roman allies, beginning the Cimbrian War.
Jugurtha of Numidia's elimination of his co-regents sparks the Jugurthine War with Rome.

China conquers Dian.
King Ugeo of Gojoseon kills a Chinese envoy, sparking the Gojoseon–Han War.
Chinese troops destroy Wanggeom seong, capital of Wiman Joseon, establishing the Four Commanderies of Han to govern the northern part of Korea.
Gaius Marius attains his first consulship.
Gaius Marius and Sulla bring an end to the Jugurthine War.
Battle of Arausio: Cimbri and Teutones annihilate a Roman army.
A mass-manumission leads to the Second Servile War in Sicily.
War of the Heavenly Horses, China defeats Dayuan at great cost.
Gaius Marius defeats the Teutones at the Battle of Aquae Sextiae.
Gaius Marius defeats the Cimbri at the Battle of Vercellae, ending the Cimbrian War.
Ariarathes VIII is forced out of Cappadocia by Mithridates VI of Pontus, and dies soon afterwards.
Cyrene is left to the people of Rome by its ruler Ptolemy Apion.
King Alexander Jannaeus of Judea wins the Siege of Gaza.
Tigranes the Great becomes king of Armenia.
Ariobarzanes I Philoromaios becomes king of Cappadocia with Roman backing.
Crown Prince Ju Revolt in China.
The assassination of Marcus Livius Drusus leads to the Social War in Italy.
Mithridates VI of Pontus's invasion of Cappadocia leads to the First Mithridatic War with the Roman Republic.
Valagamba of Anuradhapura gains control of all of Sri Lanka.
Significant native Egyptian uprising against foreign rule during the reign of Ptolemy IX.
Sulla becomes the first Roman general in history to march on Rome.
Civil war between the Roman consuls Cornelius Cinna and Octavius.
Emperor Wu of Han dies and is succeeded by his eight-year-old son Zhao, with Jin Midi, Shangguang Jie and Huo Guang as regents.
Siege of Athens ends with Roman conquest of Athens.
The death of the regent of China Jin Midi unleashes the rivalry of his co-regents Shangguang Jie and Huo Guang.
Aretas III of the Nabataeans conquers Damascus.
Sulla defeats the forces of Mithridates VI in Greece at the Battle of Orchomenus.
Lucius Licinius Murena wages the Second Mithridatic War.
Sulla makes peace with Mithridates VI and marches on Rome.
Tigranes of Armenia takes control of Syria after the implosion of the Seleucid dynasty.
Sertorius flees from Sulla to North Africa via Hispania.
The Dacian king Burebista comes to power and unites the Dacian tribes.
Sulla is appointed dictator of the Roman state, and brings about major reforms.
Conflict between the regents Shangguang Jie and Huo Guang results in the destruction of the Shangguang clan and Huo Guang becoming the de facto ruler of China.
Maues, King of the Sakas, conquers Gandhara and Taxila.
Sertorius invades Hispania and sets up his own regime, beginning the Sertorian War.
Fu Jiezi assassinated the king of Loulan on behalf of the Han dynasty.
Kanva dynasty replaces the Shunga dynasty in Magadha.
Emperor Zhao of Han dies and is succeeded by the unsuitable Prince He of Changyi and then by Xuan. Huo Guang continues to be de facto ruler of China.
Mithridates VI of Pontus disputes Nicomedes IV of Bithynia's bequest of his kingdom to the Roman Republic, beginning the Third Mithridatic War.
A slave rebellion led by the escaped gladiator Spartacus leads to the Third Servile War.
Lucullus defeats Mithridates at Tenedos, Cyzicus, and the Rhyndacus and he flees east to Armenia.
Pompey the Great ends the Sertorian War (restoring Roman control of Hispania) and the Third Servile War (restoring Roman control of southern Italy).
Wusun and China attack the Xiongnu.
Lucullus invades Armenia (Battle of Tigranocerta) and reestablishes the Seleucids in Syria.
Huo Guang dies and Emperor Xuan of Han assumes full power. The Huo clan is eliminated over the following two years.
Pompey replaces Lucullus as leader of the Roman forces in the Third Mithridatic War.
Pompey is given a three-year extraordinary command against the pirates plaguing the Mediterranean and defeats them in forty days.
Aristobulus II seizes power from John Hyrcanus II in Judea.
Pompey drives Mithridates VI out of Asia Minor (Battle of the Lycus).
Cicero denounces and defeats the Catilinarian conspiracy.
Mithridates VI commits suicide, ending the Third Mithridatic War.
Nabataean kingdom becomes a Roman vassal.
Orgetorix and the Helvetii's attempt to migrate into southwestern France leads Julius Caesar to take military action, beginning the Gallic Wars.
Julius Caesar, Pompey, and Crassus form the First Triumvirate.
The Sakas conquer Mathura.
Alexandrian Riots against Ptolemy XII. Egyptians anger erupted against Greek rule, and expelled the king, who fled to Rome for support.
Battle of Bibracte - Julius Caesar conquers the Helvetii.
Clodius becomes the leading figure in Roman urban politics. Cicero goes into exile.
Germans invade Gaul and are defeated by Julius Caesar at Battle of Vosges.
Huhanye rebels against his distant cousin Woyanqudi Chanyu of the Xiongyu, beginning the Xiongnu civil war.
Cicero recalled from exile through the machinations of Milo and his mob.
Julius Caesar invades and defeats the Belgae at the Battle of the Sabis.
Silla is founded in southeastern Korea.
Vikramaditya defeats the Sakas at Ujjain and founds the Vikram Samvat calendar era.
Caesar's invasions of Britain.
Ambiorix's revolt against Julius Caesar in Gaul.

Huhanye Chanyu of the Xiongnu become a Chinese vassal.
The Parthians defeat the Romans under Crassus in the Battle of Carrhae, ending the First Triumvirate.
Pompey joins the Optimates and becomes sole Consul in Rome.
Vercingetorix's revolt in Gaul (Battle of Gergovia, Battle of Alesia).
Siege of Uxellodunum marks the end of the Gallic Wars and the final Roman conquest of Gaul.
Julius Caesar crosses the Rubicon river and takes the city of Rome, beginning Caesar's Civil War.

Julius Caesar decisively defeats Pompey at the Battle of Pharsalus.
Ptolemy XIII deposes his co-regent Cleopatra, beginning the Ptolemaic civil war in Egypt.
Cleopatra restored to the Ptolemaic throne after the Battle of the Nile.
Year of six kings in Anuradhapura in Sri Lanka.
China abandons control of Hainan as a cost-cutting measure.
Julius Caesar takes control of Africa at the Battle of Thapsus.
Julius Caesar wins the Battle of Munda, regaining control of Hispania and ending the Roman Civil War.
Assassination of Julius Caesar on the Ides of March.
Burebista death, Dacian empire collapses into four then five smaller kingdoms.
Julius Caesar named Dictator perpetuo.
Julius Caesar re-founds Carthage and Corinth as Roman colonies.
Octavian, Mark Antony, and Lepidus form the Second Triumvirate and take control of Rome.
Second Triumvirate defeats Julius Caesar's assassins at the Battle of Philippi.
Lucius Antonius and Octavian fight the Perusine War.
Pacorus I conquers Roman Syria.
Octavian divorces Scribonia and marries Livia Drusilla on January 17th.
Ventidius defeats the Parthians at the Battle of Mount Gindarus, reclaiming Roman Syria.
Goguryeo is founded in southern Manchuria (traditional date according to Samguk Sagi).
Herod the Great becomes king of Judea.
Mark Antony invades Parthia.
Battle of Naulochus: Second Triumvirate gains control of Sicily from the rebel Sextus Pompey.
Battle of Zhizhi: Gan Yanshou and Chen Tang launch an unauthorised expedition which prevents the Xiongnu from extending their power into Central Asia.
Cleopatra and Mark Antony perform the Donations of Alexandria.
Emperor Yuan of Han dies and is succeeded by his son Cheng. Empress Wang Zhengjun becomes Empress Dowager and her brother is placed in command of the armed forces and administration.
Disagreements between Octavian and Mark Antony cause the outbreak of the Final War of the Roman Republic.
Battle of Actium: Octavian defeats troops under Mark Antony and Cleopatra, becoming de facto ruler of the Roman empire.
Octavian annexes Egypt.
Revolt of Thebes erupts in Egypt immediately following the Roman annexation.
Satavahana dynasty replaces the Kanva dynasty in Magadha.
A solar eclipse occurs as predicted by Thales, while Alyattes is battling Cyaxares. This leads to a truce. This is one of the cardinal dates from which other dates can be calculated.
Galatia annexed by Rome after the death of Amyntas of Galatia.
Judas Maccabaeus, son of Mattathias of the Hasmonean family, restores the Temple in Jerusalem (Hanukkah, Maccabean Revolt).
Conclusion of major fighting in the Cantabrian Wars marks the end of the Roman conquest of Hispania.
Baekje is founded in mid-western Korea (traditional date according to Samguk Sagi).
Augustus establishes the Rhine limes.
Babylonians capture Jerusalem, replace Jehoiachin with Zedekiah as king.
The Temple of Jupiter on Rome's Capitoline Hill is dedicated on the Ides of September.
Construction is completed on the Temple in Jerusalem.
Pannonia annexed to the Roman empire by the future emperor Tiberius.
Wang Mang becomes head of the Chinese armed forces and administration.
Birth of Jesus of Nazareth (see Chronology of Jesus' birth and death, Anno Domini, and Common Era for further details).
A severe aridification event that probably lasted the entire 22nd century BC and caused the collapse of several Old World civilizations.
Judea annexed to the Roman province of Syria after the death of King Herod.
Solar eclipse darkens Egypt (computed, no clear historical record of observation).
Emperor Ai of Han appoints his unpopular homosexual lover Dong Xian as head of armed forces and administration.
Emperor Ai of Han dies and is succeeded by his eight year old cousin Ping. Wang Mang is appointed regent and begins wide-ranging reforms.
Yorkist troops led by Edward, Duke of York defeat Lancastrians under Owen Tudor and his son Jasper Tudor, Earl of Pembroke in Wales.
The Earl of Warwick's army is defeated by a Lancastrian force under Queen Margaret, who recovers control of her husband.
Edward IV defeats Queen Margaret to make good his claim to the English throne (thought to be the bloodiest battle ever fought in England).
Five Good Emperors of Rome: Nerva, Trajan, Hadrian, Antoninus Pius and Marcus Aurelius.
The Grand Anicut, an ancient dam, is constructed by a Chola king.
The Dacian Wars. After two conflicts, Dacia is annexed as a Roman province.
A war with Parthia results in Armenia and Mesopotamia being temporarily annexed into the Roman Empire.
Kitos War, adjunct to the Jewish–Roman wars.
Hadrian's Wall is built across what is now Northern England.
The Kushan ruler Kanishka ruled present-day Pakistan and northern India.
Bar Kokhba's revolt against Rome.
Huvishka, Kushan ruler.
The Antonine Wall is built across what is now central Scotland.
Marcion, rejected by Church of Rome, founds Marcionism.
Roman–Parthian War of 161–166.
The Antonine Plague in Rome.
Disasters of the Partisan Prohibitions.
The Bucolic War broke out in Egypt between the Egyptians and the Romans.
Reign of Commodus, Roman emperor.
The Liang Province Rebellion in northwest China.
The Yellow Turban Rebellion of the Han dynasty in China.
The end of the Han dynasty.
Warlords across China launch a campaign against Dong Zhuo.
Reign of the Roman emperor Septimius Severus.
Year of the Five Emperors of Rome: Pertinax, Didius Julianus, Pescennius Niger, Clodius Albinus and Septimius Severus.
The Chinese naval Battle of Red Cliffs occurs.
Caracalla, Roman Emperor.
Constitutio Antoniniana grants citizenship to all free Roman men.
The Alexandrian Revolt erupts in Alexandria, Egypt and Caracalla responded in severe brutality.
The Han dynasty comes to an end with establishment of the Three Kingdoms in ancient China.
The Three Kingdoms period.

Sassanid dynasty of Persia launches a war to reconquer lost lands in the Roman east.
Zhuge Liang dies of illness at the standoff of Wuzhang Plains.
Crisis of the Third Century shook the Roman Empire.
The Kingdom of Hatra dissolved after the Fall of Hatra to Persia.
Mani preaches Manichaeism at the Sasanian court.
Battle of Xingshi in China.
Valerian's massacre of Christians.
Roman Emperor Valerian I is taken captive by Shapur I of Persia.
Cao Wei conquers the Shu Han Kingdom.
The Jin dynasty is founded after the overthrow of the Cao Wei dynasty by Sima Yan.
The Jin dynasty reunites China under one empire after the conquest of Eastern Wu.
Diocletian, Roman Emperor.
The War of the Eight Princes, a civil war by the Sima Clan in China.
The Thebaid and Coptos Revolts erupt in Egypt against Roman rule.
Emperor Diocletian forms the Tetrarchy in Rome.
Massive Egypt-wide rebellion was sparked against Roman rule in Egypt.
Kofun era, the first part of the Kofun period in Japan.
Armenia first to adopt Christianity as state religion.
The Sixteen Kingdoms in China begins.
Constantine the Great, ends persecution of Christians in the Roman Empire (see also Constantinian shift) and Constantinople becomes new seat of government (New Rome).
Butuan Boat One, the oldest known Balangay, a multi-purpose ship native to the Philippines is built.
Constantine the Great calls the First Council of Nicaea to pacify Christianity in the grip of the Arian controversy.
The Kingdom of Aksum adopts Christianity.
Samudragupta expands the Gupta Empire.
Constantine the Great is baptized a Christian on his death bed.
About this time the Kingdom of Aksum conquers the Kingdom of Kush.
At some time during this period, the Huns began to attack the Sassanid Empire.
An earthquake with a magnitude of at least eight strikes the Eastern Mediterranean. The following tsunami causes widespread destruction in Crete, Greece, Libya, Egypt, Cyprus, and Sicily.
Visigoths appear on the Danube and are allowed entry into the Roman Empire in their flight from the Huns.
Battle of Adrianople: Roman army is defeated by the Visigoth cavalry. Emperor Valens is killed.
Theodosius I, Roman emperor, bans pagan worship, Christianity is made the official religion of the Empire.
Chandragupta II reigns over the golden age of the Gupta Empire.
First Council of Constantinople reaffirms the Christian doctrine of the Trinity by adding to the creed of Nicaea.
Battle of Fei River in China.
Roman emperor Theodosius I dies, causing the Roman Empire to split permanently.
The Battle of Canhe Slope occurs.
The Chinese Buddhist monk Faxian sails through the Indian Ocean and travels throughout Sri Lanka and India bring and gather Buddhist scriptures.
Kumarajiva, a Buddhist monk and translator of sutras into Chinese, arrives in Chang'an.
Mesrop Mashtots introduces number 36 of the 38 letters of the newly created Armenian Alphabet.

Rome ransacked by the Visigoths led by King Alaric.
Suebi establish the first independent Christian kingdom of Western Europe in Gallaecia.
St. Augustine, Bishop of Hippo, begins to write The City of God.
Kumaragupta, Gupta emperor.
Northern and Southern dynasties in China.
The Jin dynasty comes to an end by Liu Yu.
K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo' reestablishes Copan.
The Ilopango volcano erupts, devastating the Mayan cities in present-day El Salvador.
First Council of Ephesus, the third ecumenical council which upholds the title Theotokos or "mother of God", for Mary, the mother of Jesus Christ.
Vandals conquer Carthage.
Historical linguist Albert C. Baugh dates Old English from around this year.
Council of Chalcedon, the fourth ecumenical council which taught of Jesus Christ as one divine person in two natures.
The Huns under Attila facing the Romans and the Visigoths are defeated in the Battle of Chalons.
The Persians declare war on the Armenians.
Pope Leo I meets in person with Attila on the Mincio River and convinces him not to ransack Rome.
The Metropolis of Aquileia is destroyed by Attila and his army.
Death of Attila. The Hunnic Empire is divided between Attila's sons.
Battle of Nedao. Germanic tribes destroy the main Hunnic army and do away with Hunnic domination.
Skandagupta, the last great Gupta emperor.
The city of Chichen Itza is founded in Mexico.
The Egyptian rebels assassinate Proterius, and dragged his body through the streets of Alexandria and burned it. Timothy II Aelurus anti-Chalcedonian pope elected by Egyptians.
Death of Dengizich, last Khan of the Hunnic Empire.
Riothamus, King of the Britons, helps the Roman Emperor in Brittany against the Visigoths.
Deposition of Romulus Augustulus by Odoacer: traditional date for the Fall of Rome in the West.
Chan Buddhists found the Shaolin Monastery on Mount Song in Henan, China.
Clovis I becomes King of the Western Franks upon the death of Childeric I.
Territory of modern Ukraine is established in Kiev.
Clovis defeats Syagrius and conquers the last free remnants of the Western Roman Empire.
(Approximate date) Battle of Mount Badon. According to legend, British forces led by King Arthur defeated the invading Saxons.
King Clovis I defeats and subjugates the Kingdom of Thuringia in Germany.
Theodoric the Great ousts Odoacer to become King of Italy.
Northern Gaul is united under the Frankish King Clovis I, founder of the Merovingian dynasty.

Chinese annals mentioned the existence of the Buddhist Kingdom, Kanto Lim in South Sumatra, presumably in the neighborhood of present-day Palembang.

Eastern Roman Emperor Anastasius I dies and is succeeded by Justin I.
Romans obtain silkworm eggs and begin silkworm cultivation.
Boethius writes his On the Consolation of Philosophy.

Justinian I succeeds Justin I as Emperor of the Eastern Roman Empire.
Saint Benedict of Nursia founds the monastery of Monte Cassino in Italy.
Reign of Persian Shah Khosrau I.
Nika riots in Constantinople; the cathedral is destroyed. They are put down a week later by Belisarius and Mundus; up to 30,000 people are killed in the Hippodrome.
Battle of Camlann, final battle of legendary King Arthur.
First pandemic of bubonic plague (Plague of Justinian) hits Constantinople and the rest of Byzantine Empire.
One of Justinian's edict leads to the Three-Chapter Controversy.
Nubian Kingdom of Nobatia converts to Christianity.
Kingdom of Funan dies out.
Bumin Khagan founded the Turkic Khaganate in Central Asia.
Buddhism introduced to Japan from Baekje during the Asuka period.
Second Council of Constantinople.
Eviction of the Ostrogoths from Rome, and the re-unification of all Italy under Roman rule.
Buddhist monk Jnanagupta translates 39 sutras from Sanskrit to Chinese.
First Council of Braga.
The monastery on Iona is founded by St. Columba.
Birth of Lǐ Yuān, founder of the Tang dynasty and Emperor of China under the name of Gaozu.
Lombards invade Italy and establish a federation of dukedoms under a king.
Nubian kingdom of Alodia converts to Christianity.
Nubian kingdom of Makuria converts to Christianity.
Birth of the last Islamic Prophet Muhammad.
Second Council of Braga.
The Roman Empire is invaded by various Slavs, who plunder the Balkans.
China's last of the Southern dynasties, the Chen dynasty invents matches.File:Sueben-Reich.jpg thumb The Suebi Kingdom would eventually be conquered by the Visigoths in the 6th century.
The world's oldest ongoing company, Kongō Gumi, is founded in Osaka, Japan.
Reign of Persian Shah Hormizd IV.
Egyptian official Abaskiron led a major native rebellion against the Byzantine rule in Egypt.
Reign of Roman Emperor Maurice.
Suebian Kingdom conquered by Visigoths in Spain.
Reccared, king of the Visigoths in Spain, converts to Catholicism.
Shivadeva ascends the throne of the Lichchhavi dynasty in Nepal.
China reunified under the Sui dynasty.
Third Council of Toledo adds the "filioque" clause to the Nicene Creed in Spain.
Bahram Chobin usurps the Persian throne.
Gregory the Great succeeds Pope Pelagius II (who dies of plague) as the 64th pope.
Khosrau II is restored as the Shah of Persia.
Beginning of the Bengali Calendar or (বঙ্গাব্দ Bônggabdô or Banggabda).
Pope Gregory sends Roman monks led by Augustine to England.
Smallpox spreads from India into Europe.
The Third Chinese domination of Vietnam starts following the collapse of the Early Lý dynasty.
The end of a major Egyptian rebellion that lasted 20 years against the rule of the Byzantine Empire in Egypt.
Last mention of the Roman Senate in Gregorian Register. It mentions that the senate acclaimed the statues of emperor Phocas and empress Leontia.
Hōryū-ji temple believed to have been completed in Ikaruga, Japan.
A great number of Slavs enter the Roman lands of the Balkans. Later forming tribal confederacies.
Pacal the Great becomes king of the Mayan city-state of Palenque.
The Sasanian Empire under Shah Khosrow II sacks Jerusalem, taking away the relic of the True Cross.
Sasanian shah Khosrow II invades Egypt.
Æthelfrith of Northumbria defeats the Welsh in a battle at Chester in England.
Tang dynasty of China initiated by Li Yuan.
The Chenla kingdom completely absorbed Funan.
Year one of the Islamic calendar begins, during which the Hijrah occurs—Muhammad and his followers emigrate from Mecca to Medina in September.
The Frankish merchant Samo, supporting the Slavs fighting their Avar rulers, becomes the new ruler of the first known Slav state in Central Europe.
The Avars, the Slavs and the Persians jointly besiege but fail to capture Constantinople.
Emperor Heraclius defeats the Persians, ending the Roman–Persian Wars.
Tang campaign against the Eastern Turks, Chinese Tang dynasty forces under commanders Li Jing and Li Shiji destroy the Göktürk Khanate.
