The Muslim conquests begin.
Alopen, a Persian Christian priest, introduces Nestorian Christianity into China.
Emperor Taizong issues an edict of universal toleration of religions; Nestorian Christians build a church in Chang'an.
Muslim conquest of Palestine.
Muslim conquest of Egypt and Armenia.
Unsuccessful revolt of Ashina Jiesheshuai of the Turkic people against Tang China.
The Coptic period, in its more specific definition, ends when Islam is introduced into Egypt.
Arab armies face first Defeat in The First Battle of Dongola against Christian Nubians.
The outbreak of the Alexandria Rebellion in Egypt, a revolt of the Egyptians against the Rashidun Caliphate.
Chinese Emperor Gaozong permits establishment of Christian monasteries in each of 358 prefectures.
The Arab–Khazar wars begin.
Emperor Yazdegerd III is murdered in Merv, ending the rule of Sassanid dynasty in Persia.
Arab armies defeated again in the Second Battle of Dongola resulting in the baqt possibly the longest treaty in history.
The First Fitna occurs.
The Chinese Tang dynasty under Emperor Gaozong of Tang defeats Western Turkic Kaganate.
Two Chinese monks, Zhi Yu and Zhi You, reconstruct the 3rd century south-pointing chariot mechanical compass-vehicle for Emperor Tenji of Japan.

Conquest of Kabul by Muslims.
The end of the Goguryeo–Tang War, as Goguryeo fell to a joint attack by Tang China and Unified Silla of Korea, the latter of which held the former Goguryeo domains.
I-tsing visited Srivijaya and Malayu in Sumatra and Kedah in Malay peninsula on his way to Nalanda, India.
The first Arab siege of Constantinople begins.

Battle of Karbala took place near Kufa, which resulted in the death of Husayn ibn Ali and the division of Muslim community.
Bulgaria is recognized as an independent country by the Byzantine Empire.
Revival of the Turkic Khaganate by the efforts of Ilterish Qaghan and Tonyukuk.

Emperor Justinian II of the Byzantine Empire defeats the Bulgarians.
Pro-Buddhist imperial consort Wu Zetian seizes power and rules as Empress of China.
Buddhism is made the state religion of China.
Active but unofficial anti-Christian persecution begins in China.
North–South States Period begins in Korea.
The Arabs capture Carthage from the Byzantine Empire.
The Mount Edziza volcanic complex erupts in northern British Columbia, Canada.
The Sumatra-based Srivijaya naval kingdom flourishes and declines.
Wet-field rice cultivation, small towns and kingdoms flourish. Trade links are established with China and India.
The Taihō Code is enacted in late Asuka period Japan.
Death of Arab caliph Abd al-Malik, his succession by his nominated heir and elder son al-Walid.

Overthrow of Empress Wu Zetian, the reign of China's first and only sole-ruling empress ends.

Palenque is conquered by Toniná.
Caliphate campaigns in India Arab Expansions Halted.
Emperor Xuanzong reigned, the time was considered one of China's high points.
Liutprand, King of the Lombards begins his reign.
Metropolitan episcopal see is established by the Church of the East in Chinese capital of Chang'an.
Death of Dajian Huineng, sixth and last Patriarch of Chán Buddhism.
Treaty of Tudmir, signed between Abd al-'Aziz, the commander of Muslim troops invaiding Spain and Theodemir, the Christian king of a southern region is Spain.
Death of al-Walid I and he was succeeded by his brother Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik.
Sanjaya ascends the throne to be the first king of the Mataram kingdom.
Death of caliph Sulayman ibn Abd al-Malik and his succession by his cousin and nominated heir Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz.
Siege of Constantinople. The Bulgarians and the Byzantines decisively defeat the invading Arabs, thus halting the Arab advance toward Europe.
Death of caliph Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and succession of his cousin Yazid II on 4 February 720.
The uprising of the Egyptians against the Umayyad Arab rule in Egypt, which led to the beginning of the Bashmurian revolts that lasted 112 years.
Death of caliph Yazid II and he was succeeded by his brother and nominated heir Hisham.
Byzantine Emperor Leo III the Isaurian destroys the icon of Christ above the Chalke Gate in the capital city of Constantinople, beginning the first phase of the Byzantine Iconoclasm.
Bede completes his (Ecclesiastical History of the English People).
The Sanjaya dynasty is founded around this time according to the Canggal inscription.
Quiriguá declares independence from Copan.
Battle of Akroinon. Byzantines win their first large-scale victory in a pitched battle against the Arabs.
Death of Arab caliph Hisham and succession of his nephew and heir Al-Walid II.
Assassination of Al-Walid II, Succession of Yazid III to the Caliphal throne on 17 April 744.
Arabian armies defeat Chinese Tang dynasty troops in the Battle of Talas, in the high Pamirs near Samarkand, and conquer Central Asia completely.
The Hindu Mataram kingdom flourishes and declines.
Death of Abbasid caliph al-Saffah and ascension of caliph al-Mansur to Arab Caliphate.
The An Shi Rebellion devastates China during the mid Tang dynasty.
King Offa of Mercia becomes dominant ruler in England.
Arab and Persian pirates and travelers burn and loot the Chinese city of Guangzhou, while the Tang Dynasty authorities shut the port down for the next five decades.
The construction of the famous Indonesian Buddhist structure Borobudur began, probably as a non-Buddhist shrine.
Marriage of Abbasid princess Raytah and Muhammad (future al-Mahdi).
Pepin dies; Charles becomes king at Noyan and his brother Carloman becomes king at Soissons.
Death of caliph al-Mansur and he was succeeded by al-Mahdi.
Kalasan temple constructed, according to the Kalasan inscription.
Marriage of Abbasid princess Zubaidah and Harun al-Rashid. The Xi'an Stele is erected in China.
Chinese geographer Jia Dan describes large lighthouse pillars built in the Persian Gulf, which is confirmed a century later by al-Mas'udi and al-Muqaddasi.
Death of Abbasid caliph al-Hadi and ascension of caliph Harun al-Rashid.
The Empress Irene of Athens convenes the Seventh Ecumenical Council, ending the first phase of Byzantine Iconoclasm.
Battle of Marcelae. The Bulgarian victory over the Byzantines marks the end of the half-century political instability in Bulgaria.
The Manjusrigrha (Sewu) temple is completed according to Manjusrigrha inscription.
The Frisian–Frankish wars come to an end with the last uprising of the Frisians.
The first written account of a Viking raid carried out on the abbey of Lindisfarne in northern England.
Emperor Kanmu moves the capital to Heian-kyō (present day Kyoto), initiating the Heian period of Japan.
An Arab fleet sails up the Tiber.
Beginning of the ancient West African state of Takrur or Tekrour, which flourished roughly parallel to the Ghana Empire.
On Christmas Day, Charlemagne is crowned the first Holy Roman Emperor by Pope Leo III.
Rule of Aghlabids as an autonomous province of Caliphate in North Africa, with their capital at Tunis.
The agriculturally based Buddhist Sailendra kingdom flourishes and declines.
Jayavarman II of the Khmer people in Cambodia founds the Khmer empire and establishes the Angkorian dynasty.
Construction on the Leshan Giant Buddha in Tang dynasty China is complete, after 90 years of rock-carving on a massive cliff-side.
Tang dynasty was under the rule of Emperor Xianzong of Tang.
War between the Byzantine Empire and Bulgaria.
Byzantines are heavily defeated by the Bulgars at Versinikia.
Period of serious Arab naval raids on shores of Tyrrhenian and Adriatic seas.
Charlemagne dies in the city of Aachen.
A 30-year peace agreement is signed between Bulgaria and the Byzantine Empire.
Muḥammad ibn Mūsā al-Khwārizmī writes his treatise on Algebra The Compendious Book on Calculation by Completion and Balancing.
Battle of Ellandun: King Egbert of Wessex defeats Mercia and establishes the kingdom of Wessex as the supreme Kingdom in England.
Borobudur is completed during the reign of Samaratungga.
Aghlabids established emirate (province) in Sicily and subsequently raids Southern Italy.
The Ghana (Wagadu) Empire is established.
Sweet Dew Incident occurs. Emperor Wenzong of the Tang dynasty conspires to kill the powerful eunuchs of the Tang court, but the plot is foiled.
Vlastimir defeats Presian.
Death of Louis the Pious.
Dublin is founded on the east coast of Ireland by the Vikings.
The first Viking raid in Iberia.File:Europe 843ad viking incursions map.png thumb Viking raids and division of the Frankish Empire at the Treaty of Verdun in 843.
Buddhism is persecuted and banned in China.
Emperor Xuānzong of Tang reigned. He was considered the last capable emperor of the Tang dynasty.
The first Norse settlers arrive on Iceland.
Prambanan is completed. According to the Shivagrha inscription, Rakai Pikatan — the husband of Pramodhawardhani — defeated Balaputra.
Muslims establish the University of Al Karaouine as a madrasa in Fez, Morocco.
Assassination of Abbasid caliph al-Mutawakkil and decline of the Abbasid Caliphate.File:Al-Mutawakkil.png thumb Coin issued during al-Mutawakkil's reign in the mid-9th century.
The Bagratuni dynasty of Medieval Armenia begins with Ashot I.
The beginning of the Rurik dynasty in Rus'.
Period of schism between Eastern and Western churches.
The Chinese author Duan Chengshi describes the slave trade, ivory trade, and ambergris trade of Somalia in East Africa.
Christianization of Bulgaria under Boris I.
Onward revival of the Byzantine Empire under the Macedonian dynasty.
Ahmad ibn Tulun breaks away from the Abbasid Caliphate and establishes the independent Tulunid dynasty, first Egyptian independent state since the Ptolemaic Kingdom.
An earthquake and tsunami struck Japan's Sanriku coast, killing 1,000 people.
Zanj Rebellion against the Abbasids.
Christianization of the Serbs.
Prague Castle founded.
Reign of Alfred the Great, the first king of the English.
Iceland settled by Ingolfur Arnarson from Norway.
Huang Chao leads an unsuccessful rebellion against the Tang dynasty in China.
Battle of Ethandun results in the victory of Alfred the Great over the Danish warlord Guthrum.
Abbo Cernuus becomes witness to the Siege of Paris by Vikings.
Arrival of the disciples of Saints Cyril and Methodius, Clement of Ohrid and Naum of Preslav in Bulgaria. Development of the Cyrillic Alphabet.
Egyptian Tulunid army defeats the Abbasid army in the Battle of Tawahin, Egypt maintains autonomy.
The Carolingian Empire declines and falls after the death of Charles the Fat.
The year of the Magyars arrival in Pannonia. This year is widely accepted as the beginning of the Hungarian "Landtaking".
King Alfred the Great of Wessex, First King of The English, dies.
King Balitung creates the Mantyasih inscription containing the list of Mataram kings, moves the capital from Mamratipura to Poh Pitu, and expands Prambanan temple.
Loire Vikings overrun Brittany; Breton court flees to the England of Edward the Elder.
Zhu Quanzhong deposes Emperor Ai of Tang and establishes a new Later Liang dynasty.
The Fatimid Caliphate arises in Kabylie, Kutama Tribe.
Parantaka I of the Chola dynasty drives out the Pandyan from southern India into Lanka (now Sri Lanka), which he also eventually conquers.
Petar of Serbia, prince of Serbia, baptised a Christian.
The Viking Rollo granted County of Rouen by France: official foundation of Normandy.
The Warmadewa dynasty rules Bali.
The Bulgarians destroyed the Byzantine army in the Battle of Anchialus, one of the bloodiest battles in the Middle Ages.
The medieval Croatian state becomes a unified kingdom under King Tomislav.
Kingdom of England becomes a unified state.
Official recognition of an independent national Church in Europe, the Bulgarian Patriarchate.
During the reign of King Wawa, the capital of Mataram kingdom in Kewu Plain is devastated, probably by the massive eruption of Mount Merapi.
Ziyarid dynasty is established in northern Iran.
Alan II, with support from Æthelstan, commences the reconquest of Brittany.
Gorm the Old becomes the first recognized king of Denmark, and thus the Danish Monarchy is founded.
Goryeo dynasty unifies Later Three Kingdoms of Korea.
Mpu Sindok moves the capital again from Tamwlang to Watugaluh, both near bank of Brantas River in modern Jombang in East Java.
The Nri Kingdom in what is now Southeastern Nigeria starts.
Formation of the Tu'i Tonga Empire and of the Tuʻi Tonga dynasty in Tonga.
The beginning of the Medieval Warm Period.
The Battle of Lechfeld sees a decisive victory for Otto I the Great, King of the Germans, over the Hungarian harka Bulcsú and the chieftains Lél (Lehel) and Súr.
Seljuks convert to Islam.
Zhao Kuangyin establishes Song dynasty.
Khazar kingdom is attacked and defeated by Kievan Rus.
Mieszko I, first duke of Poland, baptised a Christian.
Battle of Silistra between Kievan Rus and Bulgars.
Cairo is founded near Fustat.
Song dynasty recorded the ancient sovereign state of Ma-i on the list of states conducting trade in the south seas and the government's efforts to regulate and tax this "luxurious" trade.
Cairo becomes the new Egyptian capital, and the seat of the Fatimid Caliphate.
Failure of the Second Qarmatian invasion of Egypt.
Ghaznavids dynasty, as the first Turk Sultanate, was established in Central Asia.
The Siege of Tripoli ends in an Egyptian victory over the Byzantine Army.
Song dynasty reunites China.
Al-Azhar University is established in Cairo during the rule of the Fatimid dynasty.
Dynastic marriage between princess Mahendradatta of Javanese Isyanas and king Udayana of Balinese Warmadewas.
Queen Gudit leads her rebellion against the Aksumite dynasty of Abyssinia.
The Norseman Erik the Red begins the colonisation of Greenland.
Ah Mekat Tutul Xiu unified Uxmal, Mayapan, and Chichen Itza founding The League of Mayapan.
Vladimir I, Prince of Kievan Rus', baptised a Christian.
Airlangga, son of King Udayana and Queen Mahendradatta was born in Bali.
King Dharmawangsa of Mataram kingdom launches a naval invasion on Palembang in an unsuccessful attempt to conquer Srivijaya.
Dharmawangsa commissioned the translation of the Mahabharata into Old Javanese.
Samanid dynasty was defeated and conquered by Ghaznavids.
Establishment of the Eastern Settlement and Western Settlement in Greenland.
Sweyn Forkbeard conquers Norway.
Baitoushan volcano on what would be the Chinese-Korean border, erupts with a force of 6.5, the fourth largest Holocene blast.
Japanese Lady Murasaki Shikibu writes The Tale of Genji.
Norsemen, led by Leif Eriksson, establish short-lived settlements in and around Vinland in North America.
Song dynasty court prohibited Butuan from exporting several items with their predilection due to issues on rules and regulation.
The library and university Dar Al-Hekma is founded in Egypt under the Fatimids.
The Treaty of Shanyuan is signed between the Chinese Song dynasty and the Khitan Liao dynasty.
King Dharmawangsa's Mataram kingdom falls under the invasion of King Wurawari from Lwaram (highly possible Srivijayan ally in Java).
Lý Thái Tổ overthrows the Anterior Lê dynasty of Vietnam, establishing the Lý dynasty.
The Second Goryeo-Khitan War; the Korean king is forced to flee the capital temporarily, but is unable to establish a foothold and fearing a counterattack, the Khitan forces withdrew.
Danish king Sweyn Forkbeard conquers England.
The Book of Healing, a vast philosophical and scientific encyclopaedia, is written by Avicenna, Persian scholar.
The Byzantine armies of Basil II are victorious over Samuil of Bulgaria in the Battle of Kleidion.
In the Battle of Nesjar in Oslofjord, Norway, the forces of Olav Haraldsson fought the forces of Sveinn Hákonarson, with a victory for Olav.
The Byzantine armies of Basil Boioannes are victorious at the Battle of Cannae against the Lombards under Melus of Bari.
The First Bulgarian Empire is conquered by the Byzantine Empire.
The Third Goryeo-Khitan War; the Korean General Kang Kam-ch'an inflicted heavy losses to Khitan forces at the Battle of Kwiju. The Khitans withdrew and both sides signed a peace treaty.
Airlangga establishes the Kingdom of Kahuripan.
Ruler Rajendra Chola I moves the capital city of the empire from Thanjavur to Gangaikonda Cholapuram.
The Chola dynasty of India uses its naval powers to conquer the South East Asian kingdom of Srivijaya, turning it into a vassal.
The King of Srivijaya appeals to the Song dynasty Chinese, sending a diplomatic mission to their capital at Kaifeng.
Fatimid Caliphate of Egypt defeats the Syrian Arab Bedouin tribes in the Battle of al-Uqhuwana.
Sanghyang Tapak inscription in the Cicatih River bank in Cibadak, Sukabumi, West Java, mentioned about the establishment of sacred forest and Kingdom of Sunda.
An earthquake strikes the Jordan Valley, followed by a tsunami along the Mediterranean coast, killing tens of thousands.
Canute the Great dies, and his kingdom of present-day Norway, England, and Denmark was split amongst three rivals to his throne.
Raoul Glaber chronicles a devastating three-year famine induced by climatic changes in southern France.
William Iron Arm ventures to the Mezzogiorno.
Ferdinand I of León conquers the Kingdom of Galicia.
Fatimid army of Egypt defeats the Crusaders in the Battle of Teqoa.
Duncan I of Scotland slain in battle. Macbeth succeeds him.
Airlangga divides Kahuripan into two kingdoms Janggala and Kadiri and abdicates in favour of his successors.
Chinese artisan Bi Sheng invents ceramic movable type printing.
Samuel Aba became King of Hungary.
The Normans establish Melfi as the capital of southern Italy.
The Kingdom of Nri of West Africa is said to have started in this year with Eze Nri Ìfikuánim.
The Zirids, a Berber dynasty of North Africa, break their allegiance with the Fatimid court of Egypt and recognize the Abbasids of Baghdad as the true caliphs.
Fujiwara no Yorimichi converts the rural villa at Byōdō-in into a famous Japanese Buddhist temple.
A large supernova is observed by astronomers, the remnants of which would form the Crab Nebula.
The Battle of Atapuerca is fought between García V of Navarre and Ferdinand I of León.
The Seljuk Turks capture Baghdad, taking the Buyid Emir Al-Malik al-Rahim prisoner.
Ferdinand I of León, King of Castile and King of León, is crowned Imperator totius Hispaniae (Emperor of All Hispania).
William II of England the son of William the Conqueror, was born.
Anawrahta, ruler of the Pagan Kingdom, defeated the Mon city of Thaton, thus unifying all of Myanmar.
Invasion of the Banu Hilal, Kairouan destroyed, Zirids reduced to a tiny coastal strip, remainder fragments into petty Bedouin emirates.
Macbeth, king of Scotland, dies in battle against the future king Malcolm III.
Norman conquest of Sicily in the Mediterranean Sea.
The Great German Pilgrimage, consisting of around unarmed 7,000 pilgrims, travels to Jerusalem under the leadership of Gunther of Bamberg.
Independence of the Kingdom of Galicia and Portugal under the rule of Garcia.
Seljuks first invasion to Georgia under leadership of Alp Arslan.
In the Battle of Stamford Bridge, the last Anglo-Saxon King Harold Godwinson defeated his brother Tostig Godwinson and Harold III of Norway.
Seljuks destroyed Georgia for the second time.
The reign of Japanese Emperor Go-Sanjō brings about a brief period where central power is taken out of the hands of the Fujiwara clan.
Virarajendra Chola begins sending military raids into Malaysia and Indonesia.
The death of Athirajendra Chola and the ascension of Kulothunga Chola I marks the transition between the Medieval Cholas and the Chalukya Cholas.
Defeat of the Byzantine Empire at the Battle of Manzikert by the Seljuk army of Alp Arslan, ending three centuries of a Byzantine military and economic Golden Age.
The Battle of Golpejera is fought between Sancho II of Castile and Alfonso VI of Castile.
The Seljuk Turks capture Ankara from the Byzantines.
The Seljuk Turks capture Jerusalem from the Fatimids, and cut pilgrim transit.
Henry IV suppresses the rebellion of Saxony in the First Battle of Langensalza.
The Ghana Empire is attacked by the Almoravids, who sack the capital of Koumbi Saleh, ending the rule of king Tunka Manin.
The Song Chinese allies with southern Vietnamese Champa and Cambodian Chenla to conquer the Lý dynasty, which is an unsuccessful campaign.
The Walk to Canossa by Henry IV of the Holy Roman Empire.
The revolt of Nikephoros III against Byzantine ruler Michael VII.
Franks start to settle around the Way of Saint James (Today, modern North Spain).
Malik Shah I reforms the Iranian Calendar.
Birth of Urraca of León and Castile future Queen of Castille and León.
The enormous Chinese historical work of the Zizhi Tongjian is compiled by scholars under Chancellor Sima Guang, completed in 294 volumes and included 3 million written Chinese characters.
Alfonso VI of Castile captures the Moorish Muslim city of Toledo, Spain.
The Katedralskolan, Lund school of Sweden is established by Canute IV of Denmark.
The Battle of az-Zallaqah between the Almoravids and Castilians.
The Italian cities of Genoa and Pisa engage in the African Mahdia campaign.
William II of England, son of William the Conqueror, is crowned king of England.
The University of Bologna is established.
Normans from the Duchy of Normandy take control of Malta and surrounding islands.
The Byzantine Empire under Alexios I Komnenos and his Cuman allies defeat Pechenegs at the Battle of Levounion.
Battle of Alnwick: Malcolm III of Scotland is killed by the forces of William II of England.
The Kipchaks defeat princes of Kievan Rus at the Battle of the Stugna River.
Vikramaditya VI, ruler of the Western Chalukya Empire, defeats the army of Kulothunga Chola I in the Battle of Vengi.
A succession crisis following the reign of the Fatimid Caliph Ma'ad al-Mustansir Billah sparks a rebellion which leads to the split of Ismaili Shia into the new Nizari religious branch.
El Cid, the great Spanish hero, conquers the Muslim city of Valencia.
The astronomical clock tower of Kaifeng, China—engineered by the official Su Song—is completed.
Pope Urban II calls upon Western Europeans to take up the cross and reclaim the Holy Lands, officially commencing the First Crusade.
University of Oxford in England holds its first lectures.
Diego Rodriguez, a son of El Cid, dies in the Battle of Consuegra, an Almoravid victory.
The Siege of Nicaea during the First Crusade.
Pope Urban II makes an appearance at the Siege of Capua.
The Dongpo Academy of Hainan, China is built in honor of the Song dynasty Chinese official and poet Su Shi, who was exiled there for criticizing reforms of the New Policies Group.
The Siege of Antioch during the First Crusade.
The birth of Hildegard of Bingen, Doctor of the Church, abbess, monastic leader, mystic, prophetess, medical, German composer and writer, polymath.
After building considerable strength, David IV of Georgia discontinues tribute payments to the Seljuk Turks.
After the Kingdom of Jerusalem is established, the Al-Aqsa Mosque is made into the residential palace for the kings of Jerusalem.
Death of the great Spanish hero Rodrigo Díaz "El Cid Campeador".
The Siege of Jerusalem by European Crusaders.
On August 5, Henry I is crowned King of England.
On December 25, Baldwin of Boulogne is crowned as the first King of Jerusalem in the Church of the Nativity in Bethlehem.
David the Builder takes over Kakheti and Hereti (now parts of Georgia).
King Coloman unites Hungary and Croatia under the Hungarian Crown.
Muslims conquer Señorío de Valencia.
The Fatimids of Egypt defeat the Kingdom of Jerusalem in the Battle of Ramla.
A church council is convened by King David the Builder in Urbnisi to reorganize the Georgian Orthodox Church.
In the Battle of Ertsukhi, King David the Builder defeats an army of Seljuks.
King Jayawarsa of Kadiri (on Java) ascends to the throne.
Battle of Tinchebray.
By the Treaty of Devol, signed in September, Bohemond I of Antioch has to submit to the Byzantine Empire, becoming the vassal of Alexius I.
In the Battle of Nakło, Boleslaus III Wrymouth defeats the Pomeranians and re-establishes Polish access to the sea.
On August 24, in the Battle of Hundsfeld, Boleslaus III Wrymouth defeats Emperor Henry V of Germany and stops German expansion eastward.
On June 10, Bertrand of Toulouse captures the County of Tripoli (northern Lebanon/western Syria).
On April 14, during Henry V's first expedition to Rome, he is crowned Holy Roman Emperor.
The Georgian army occupies Rustavi in the war with the Muslims.
The Byzantine army defeats the Turks at Philomelion.
The Knights Templar are founded to protect Christian pilgrims in Jerusalem.
On January 16, the Council of Nablus, a council of ecclesiastic and secular lords in the crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem, establishes the first written laws for the kingdom.
On December 25, St. Norbert and 29 companions make their solemn vows in Premontre, France, establishing the Premonstratensian Order.
King David the Builder captures Tbilisi and declares it the capital city of Georgia, ending 400 years of Arab rule.
The Battle of Beroia (Modern-day Stara Zagora, Bulgaria) results in the disappearance of the Pechenegs Turkish tribe as an independent force.
The Jurchen dynasty of China forces Koryo (now Korea) to recognize their suzerainty.
In April or May, David I is crowned King of the Scots.
In November, the Jurchens of the Jin dynasty declare war on the Song dynasty, beginning the Jin–Song wars.
Lothair of Supplinburg, duke of Saxony, is elected Holy Roman Emperor instead of the nearest heir, Frederick of Swabia, beginning the great struggle between Guelphs and Ghibellines.
On June 11, in the Battle of Azaz, the Crusader states, led by King Baldwin II of Jerusalem, defeat the Seljuk Turks.
The Northern Song dynasty loses power over northern China to the Jin dynasty.
On June 24, the Kingdom of Portugal gains independence from the Kingdom of León at the Battle of São Mamede;.
On Christmas Day, Roger II is crowned King of Sicily, the royal title being bestowed on him by Antipope Anacletus II.
Papal schism, Pope Innocent II vs. Antipope Anacletus II.
The Southern Song dynasty establishes China's first permanent standing navy, although China had a long naval history prior. The main admiral's office is at the port of Dinghai.
King Jayabaya of Kadiri ascends to the throne.
The Anarchy takes place, during a period of civil war in England.
Suger begins rebuilding the abbey church at St Denis north of Paris, which is regarded as the first major Gothic building.
Egyptian military commander Ridwan ibn Walakhshi becomes vizier of Egypt.
On July 22, the future King Louis VII of France marries Eleanor, the Duchess of Aquitaine.
In April, the Second Lateran Council ends the papal schism.
On July 25, the Portuguese defeat the Almoravids led by Ali ibn Yusuf in the Battle of Ourique; Prince Afonso Henriques is acclaimed King of Portugal by his soldiers.
On July 5, in the Treaty of Mignano, Pope Innocent II confirms Roger II as King of Sicily, Duke of Apulia, and Prince of Capua and invests him with his titles.
Collapse of the Ancestral Puebloan culture at Chaco Canyon (modern-day New Mexico).
Afonso Henriques is proclaimed King of Portugal by the cortes.
Manuel I Komnenos is crowned as Byzantine emperor after the death of John II Komnenos.
The Treaty of Zamora recognizes Portuguese independence from the Kingdom of León. Portugal also recognizes the suzerainty of the pope.
On December 24, Edessa falls to the Atabeg Zengi.
The Second Crusade is launched in response to the fall of the County of Edessa.
On October 25, the four-month-long Siege of Lisbon successfully brings the city under definitive Portuguese control, expelling the Moorish overlords.
The Wendish Crusade against the Polabian Slavs (or "Wends") in what is now northern and eastern Germany.
Ramon Berenguer IV, Count of Barcelona marries Petronilla, the Queen of Aragon.
On December 27, Henry II is crowned King of England at Westminster Abbey.
The Moroccan-born Muslim geographer Muhammad al-Idrisi publishes his Geography.
Pope Adrian IV grants overlordship of Ireland to Henry II of England in the bull Laudabiliter.
The Treaty of Sahagún ends the war between Castile and León.
In the siege of Ani, troops from the Kingdom of Georgia take control over the city, only to have it sold for the second time to the Shaddadids, a Kurdish dynasty.
Kilij Arslan II, Sultan of Rum, makes peace with the Byzantine Empire, recognizing the emperor's primacy.
Egyptian military commander Shawar becomes vizier and de facto Caliph of the Fatimid Caliphate of Egypt.
Genghis Khan, the founder of the Mongol Empire, is born as Temüjin in present-day Mongolia.
The Norwegian Law of Succession takes effect.
Tensions and disputes between the Pagan Empire and the Kingdom of Polonnaruwa causes the Sinhalese under Parakramabahu the Great to raid Burma.
King Valdemar I of Denmark conquers Arkona on the Island of Rügen, the strongest pagan fortress and temple in northern Europe.
Political disputes within the Pandya Empire sparks the decade-long Pandyan Civil War.
On December 29, Thomas Becket is murdered in Canterbury Cathedral.
On November 11, Henry II of England lands in Ireland to assert his claim as Lord of Ireland.
Saladin deposes the last Fatimid Caliph Al-'Āḍid and rules Egypt.
The Pandyan city of Madurai is sacked by the Sinhalese army due to an attempt to drive off the rival throne claimant, Kulasekara Pandyan.
Sinhalese king Parakramabahu the Great gains a decisive victory by invading the Chola Empire as an ally of the Pandyas in the Pandyan Civil War.
On July 12, William I of Scotland is captured by the English in the Battle of Alnwick. He accepts the feudal overlordship of the English crown and pays ceremonial allegiance at York.
Saladin establishes the Ayyubid Sultanate of Egypt, becoming the first Sultan of Egypt. Egypt remains an autonomous state.
Hōnen Shōnin (Genkū) founds the Jōdo shū (Pure Land) sect of Buddhism.
The Treaty of Windsor is signed by King Henry II of England and the High King of Ireland, Ruaidrí Ua Conchobair.
The Genpei War in Japan.
The Portuguese Navy defeats a Muslim fleet off the coast of Cape Espichel.
Parakramabahu the Great conducts a large-scale raid on Burma, after a ship transporting a Sinhalese princess to the Khmer Empire is attacked by Burmese naval fleets.
Religious reformations of Theravada Buddhism in Pagan Burma under the patronage of Narapatisithu are continued with the end of the Polonnaruwa-Pagan War.
Revolt of the people of Constantinople against the Latins, whom they massacre, proclaiming Andronicus I Comnenus as co-emperor.
On September 24, Andronicus I Comnenus has his nephew Alexius II Comnenus strangled.
Diet of Pentecost organised by Emperor Frederick I in Mainz.
On March 24, Queen Tamar, King of Georgia, accedes to the throne as sole ruler after reigning with her father, George III, for six years.
Andronicus I Comnenus is deposed and, on September 12, executed as a result of the Norman massacre of the Greeks of Thessalonika.
Beginning in this year the Kamakura shogunate deprives the emperor of Japan of political power.
The Uprising of Asen and Peter against the Byzantine Empire leads to the restoration of the Bulgarian Empire.
The cathedral school (Katedralskolan) in Lund, Sweden, is founded. The school is the oldest in northern Europe and one of the oldest in all of Europe.
On January 27, the future Holy Roman Emperor Henry VI marries Constance of Sicily, the heiress to the Sicilian throne.
In August, the Swedish royal and commercial center Sigtuna is attacked by raiders from Karelia, Couronia, and/or Estonia.
On July 4, in the Battle of Hattin, the Egyptian troops led by Saladin defeats the Kingdom of Jerusalem.
The Riah were introduced into the Habt and south of Tetouan by the Almohad caliph, Abu Yusuf Yaqub al-Mansur, and Jochem and Acem were introduced in Tamesna.
On November 11, William II of Sicily dies and is succeeded by his illegitimate cousin Tancred, Count of Lecce instead of Constance.
On September 3, Richard I is crowned King of England at Westminster.
The Third Crusade is an attempt by European leaders to wrest the Holy Land from Egypt during the reign of Saladin.
Holy Roman Emperor Henry VI attacked the Kingdom of Sicily from May to August but fails and withdrawn, with Empress Constance captured.
On September 7, Saladin is defeated by Richard I of England at the Battle of Arsuf.
In April, Isabella I begins her reign as Christian Queen of the Kingdom of Jerusalem.
In the Battle of Jaffa, King Richard the Lionheart defeats Saladin.
Minamoto no Yoritomo is appointed Sei-i Taishōgun, "barbarian-subduing great general", shōgun for short, the first military dictator to bear this title.
Sultan Shahābuddin Muhammad Ghori establishes the first Muslim empire in India for 14 years by defeating Prithviraj Chauhan.
Nalanda, the great Indian Buddhist educational centre, is destroyed.
Emperor Henry VI conquers the Kingdom of Sicily.
On June 16, the struggle of Shamqori. Georgian forces annihilate the army of Abu Baqar.
Pope Innocent III writes to Kaloyan, inviting him to unite the Bulgarian Church with the Roman Catholic Church.
Construction begins on the Grand Village of the Natchez near Natchez, Mississippi. This ceremonial center for the Natchez people is occupied and built until the early 17th century.
Battle of Basian occurs on July 27, between Kingdom of Georgia and Seljuks.
Battle of Mirebeau occurs on August 1, between Arthur I of Brittany and John of England.
Introduction of by Fibonacci.
Fall of Normandy from Angevin hands to the French King, Philip Augustus, end of Norman domination of France.
Islamization of Bengal by Bakhtiyar Khalji and oppression of Buddhism in East India.
The Battle of Adrianople occurred on April 14 between Bulgarians under Tsar Kaloyan of Bulgaria, and Crusaders under Baldwin I,, the first emperor of the Latin Empire of Constantinople.
Genghis Khan is declared Great Khan of the Mongols.
The Delhi Sultanate is established in Northern India under the Mamluk Dynasty.
Francis of Assisi founds the Franciscan Order.
The Albigensian Crusade is declared by Pope Innocent III.
Frederick of Sicily is crowned King of the Romans at Mainz.
The Kingdom of France defeats the Crown of Aragon at the Battle of Muret.
France defeats the English and Imperial German forces at the Battle of Bouvines.
King John signs Magna Carta at Runnymede.
Battle of Lipitsa between Russian principalities.
Maravarman Sundara I reestablishes the Pandya Dynasty in Southern India.
Fifth Crusade captures Egyptian Ayyubid port city of Damietta; ultimately the Crusaders withdraw.
Frederick II, Holy Roman Emperor is crowned in Rome.
The Kingdom of Mapungubwe was established.
Merv, Herat, Bamyan and Nishapur are destroyed in the Mongol invasion of the Khwarazmian Empire.
The Battle of Mansurah end in a decisive victory for the Egyptians and forced the surrender of the Crusaders and their departure from Egypt.
Andrew II of Hungary signs the Golden Bull which affirms the privileges of Hungarian nobility.
The Signoria of the Republic of Venice is formed and consists of the Doge, the Minor Council, and the three leaders of the Quarantia.
Volga Bulgaria defeats the army of the Mongol Empire at the Battle of Samara Bend.
Trần dynasty of Vietnam was established by Emperor Trần Thái Tông's ascension to the throne after his uncle Trần Thủ Độ orchestrated the overthrow of the Lý dynasty.
Dispute between the so-called second Lombard League and Emperor Frederick II.
Estonians are finally subjugated to German crusader rule during the Livonian Crusade.
First clash between Gregory IX and Emperor Frederick II.
Sixth Crusade under the excommunicated Emperor Frederick II, who returns Jerusalem to the Crusader States in a negotiated settlement with the Egypt's Sultan, Al-Kamil.
Emperor Frederick II promulgates the Constitutions of Melfi, a far-reaching legal code influential in the development of continental European statehood.
The Mongols besiege Kaifeng, the capital of the Jin dynasty, capturing it in the following year.
Battle of Ganter, Ken Arok defeated Kertajaya, the last king of Kediri, thus established Singhasari kingdom Ken Arok ended the reign of Isyana Dynasty and started his own Rajasa dynasty.
Egyptian garrison resisted an attack on fortress of Trapessac and a relief force decimated the Knight Templars, inflicting them a crushing defeat in the Battle of Trapessac.
Emperor Frederick II virtually annihilates the forces of the second Lombard League at the Battle of Cortenuova.
Mongol Empire conquers Kievan Rus.
Sukhothai becomes the first capital of Sukhothai Kingdom.
A Crusader army led by Theobald I of Navarre is defeated by the Egyptians in the Battle at Gaza.
Third conflict between the Holy Roman Empire and the Papacy.
Russians defeat the Swedish army at the Battle of the Neva.
Mongol Empire defeats Hungary at the Battle of Mohi and defeats Poland at the Battle of Legnica. Hungary and Poland ravaged.
Mongol Empire under Tair Bahadur besiege the city of Lahore at the Siege of Lahore.
Russians defeat the Teutonic Knights at the Battle of Lake Peipus.
Second Holy Roman Empire–Papacy War.
Egyptian Ayyubid army and Khwarezmian army defeat the Crusaders and their Muslim allies at the Battle of La Forbie.
End of the Portuguese Reconquista against the Moors, when King Afonso III of Portugal reconquers the Algarve.
Death of Emperor Frederick II on December 13th.
The Mamluk Sultanate is founded in Egypt.
Baab Mashur Malamo established the Sultanate of Ternate in Maluku.
Baghdad captured and destroyed by the Mongols, effective conclusion of the Abbasid Caliphate in Baghdad.
Pandayan Emperor Jatavarman Sundara I invades Eastern India and northern Sri Lanka.
Treaty of Paris is signed between Louis IX and Henry III.
Mongols first major war defeat in the Battle of Ain Jalut against the Egyptians.
Toluid Civil War begins between Kublai Khan and Ariq Böke for the title of Great Khan.
Byzantines under Michael VIII retake Constantinople from the Crusaders and Venice.
Iceland brought under Norwegian rule, with the Old Covenant.
Dominican theologian Thomas Aquinas begins to write his Summa Theologiae.
Fall of the Crusader State of Antioch to the Egyptians.
Goryeo dynasty swears allegiance to the Yuan dynasty.
The Zagwe dynasty is displaced by the Solomonic dynasty.
Edward I of England and Charles of Anjou arrive in Acre, starting the Ninth Crusade against Egypt led by Baybars.
The Battle of Qaqun ends in an Egyptian victory over the European coalition forces.
Second Council of Lyon attempts to unite the churches of the Eastern Roman Empire with the Church of Rome.
The Mamluk-Makurian War ends in an Egyptian victory under Sultan Baybars and the deposition of David II.
Battle of Elbistan: the Egyptians forces defeat and overwhelm the Mongol forces. Egyptian forces marched unopposed to Kayseri in the heart of Anatolia in triumph and enters the city.
Passage of the last and most important of the Paris Condemnations by Bishop Tempier, which banned a number of Aristotelian propositions.
The Chola Dynasty in Southern India officially comes to an end.
The Song dynasty ends after losing the Battle of Yamen to the Mongols.
The Egyptians defeat the Mongols in the Second Battle of Homs.
The Mongols launch their second invasion of Japan, but like their first invasion they are repelled by the Samurai and the Kamikaze winds.
Aragon acquires Sicily after the Sicilian Vespers.
King Kertanegara launches the Pabali expedition to Bali, integrating Bali into the Singhasari territory.
Peterhouse, Cambridge founded by Hugo de Balsham, the Bishop of Ely.
Second Mongol raid against Hungary, led by Nogai Khan.
Kertanegara insulted the envoy of Kublai Khan, who demanded that Java pay tribute to the Yuan Dynasty.
The County of Tripoli falls to the Egyptian Bahri Mamluks led by Qalawun.
By the Edict of Expulsion, King Edward I of England orders all Jews to leave the Kingdom of England.
Mamluk Sultan of Egypt al-Ashraf Khalil captures Acre, thus ending the Crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem (the last Christian state remaining from the Crusades).
The Swiss Confederation of Uri, Schwyz, and Unterwalden forms.
Jayakatwang, duke of Kediri, rebels and kills Kertanegara, ending the Singhasari kingdom.
King Mangrai founds the Lanna kingdom.
Marco Polo, on his voyage from China to Persia, visits Sumatra and reports that, on the northern part of Sumatra, there were six trading ports, including Ferlec, Samudera and Lambri.
Mongol invasion of Java. Kublai Khan of Yuan dynasty China, sends punitive attack against Kertanegara of Singhasari, who repels the Mongol forces.
On 10 November, the coronation of Nararya Sangramawijaya as monarch, marks the foundation of the Hindu Majapahit kingdom in eastern Java.
First War of Scottish Independence begins.
Membership in the Mazor Consegio or the Great Council of Venice of the Venetian Republic is sealed and limited in the future to only those families whose names have been inscribed therein.
Ottoman Empire is established under Osman I.
Aji Batara Agung Dewa Sakti founds the Kingdom of Kutai Kartanegara/Sultanate of Kutai in the Tepian Batu or Kutai Lama.
Islam is likely established in the Aceh region.
The Turku Cathedral was consecrated in Turku.
The city of Bilbao was founded.
Fall of Outremer: Egyptians seize all the Crusader campaign’s possessions in the Holy Land.
Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt defeats the Mongols in the Battle of Marj al-Saffar. Egyptians enter Damascus and chases the Mongols as far as Al-Qaryatayn in Syria.
King Jayanegara succeeds Kertarajasa Jayawardhana as ruler of Majapahit.
The Avignon papacy transfers the seat of the Popes from Italy to France.
An Italian Franciscan friar, Mattiussi, visited Sumatra, Java, and Banjarmasin in Borneo. In his record he described the kingdom of Majapahit.
Władysław I the Elbow-high is crowned King of Poland which leads to its later unification.
Dante Alighieri: Divine Comedy.
Malietoafaiga ordered cannibalism to be abolished in Tutuila (present-day American Samoa).
Forced out of previous habitations, the Mexica found the city of Tenochtitlan.
Tver Uprising against the Golden Horde.
Tribhuwana Wijayatunggadewi succeeds Jayanegara as ruler of Majapahit.
The Battle of Posada results in a major Wallachian victory, sanctioning the independence of the first Romanian principality, Wallachia.
The Genkō War in Japan deposes the Kamakura Shogunate, ending the Kamakura Period and beginning the Kenmu Restoration under Emperor Go-Daigo.
The death of the Ilkhan Abu Said causes the disintegration of the Mongol rule in Persia.
The Kenmu Restoration ends and the Muromachi period begins in Japan; start of the Nanboku-chō period.
The Vijayanagara Empire is founded in South India by Harihara I.
The Hundred Years' War begins when Edward III of England lays claim to the French throne.
In Saint George's Night Uprising, pagan Estonians launch a last large-scale attempt to rid themselves of the non-indigenous Christian religion.
The French recruit troops and ships in Genoa, Monaco, and Nice.
King Valdemar IV of Denmark sells the Duchy of Estonia to the Teutonic Order.
Official elevation to Patriarchate of an independent national Church in Europe, the Serbian Orthodox Church.
The principality of Moldavia emerges between the Eastern Carpathians and the Prut river.
Adityawarman moved the capital of Dharmasraya and established the kingdom of Malayupura in Pagarruyung, West Sumatra.
The Black Death kills around a third of the population of Europe.
Ramathibodi I establishes the Ayutthaya Kingdom.
The Red Turban Rebellions break out along the Huai River valley, beginning a nearly 20-year period of uprisings against the Mongol-led Yuan dynasty in China.
Fa Ngum established the Lan Xang kingdom in Laos.
The Diet of the Hansa is held in Lübeck, formalising what up until then had only been a loose alliance of trading cities in northern Europe and officially founding the Hanseatic League.
Scotland retains its independence with the signing of the Treaty of Berwick, thus ending the Wars of Scottish Independence.
The Old Javanese text Nagarakertagama is written.
Tepanec Tlatoani Acolnahuácatl accepts Acamapichtli as the first tlatoani of Tenochtitlan for the Mexica Empire.
Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt defeats a coalition of Kingdom of Cyprus, Republic of Genoa, and Knights Hospitaller in the Battle of Tripoli, ending the raid in a disaster.
The end of the Mongol-led Yuan dynasty in China and the beginning of the Ming dynasty.
The Battle of Maritsa, the Serbs are defeated by the Ottomans, with most of Serb nobility being killed.
Battle of the Vozha River between Russians and Mongols.
Ciompi Revolt occurs in Florence.
Russian principalities defeat the Golden Horde at the Battle of Kulikovo.
John Wycliffe is dismissed from the University of Oxford for criticism of the Catholic Church, leading to the Lollardy movement in England.
Peasants' Revolt in England.
Barquq rise to power to start the Burji dynasty, the Circassian Mamuluk Dynasty in Egypt.
Khan Tokhtamysh captures Moscow.
Battle of Aljubarrota between Portugal and Castile. Portugal maintains independence.
Union of Krewo between Poland and Lithuania.
Battle of Kosovo between Serbs and Ottoman Turks; Prince Lazar, Sultan Murad I and Miloš Obilić are killed.
Wikramawardhana succeeds Sri Rajasanagara as ruler of Majapahit.
Anti-Jewish pogroms spread throughout Spain and Portugal, and many thousands of Jews are massacred.
Emperor Go-Kameyama of Japan abdicates in favor of rival claimant Go-Komatsu, in order to end the Nanboku-chō period of conflict between the Northern and Southern imperial courts.
Taejo of Joseon establishes the Joseon Dynasty.
Capture of Baghdad: Baghdad returns to the Jalayirid Sultanate under Egyptian patronage.
The Second Bulgarian Empire ends, with the capture of the last stronghold fortress of Vidin and its king Ivan Sratsimir by the Ottomans.
Reign of Chimalpopoca begins as the third tlatoani of Tenochtitlan.
The Kalmar Union is established, uniting Norway, Sweden and Denmark into one kingdom.
Zhu Di launches the Jingnan campaign from Beiping (Beijing) to unseat his nephew, the Jianwen Emperor.
Dilawar Khan establishes the Malwa Sultanate in present-day central India.
Ottoman and Timurid Empires fight at the Battle of Ankara resulting in the capture of Bayezid I by Timur.
Sultanate of Malacca founded by Parameswara.
The settlement of the Canary Islands signals the beginning of the Spanish Empire.
Ottoman Interregnum, a civil war between the four sons of Bayezid I.
The Yongle Emperor moves the capital of China from Nanjing to Beijing.
Regreg War, Majapahit civil war of secession between Wikramawardhana against Wirabhumi.
The Sultanate of Sulu is established by Sharif ul-Hāshim.
The Battle of Grunwald is the decisive battle of the Polish–Lithuanian–Teutonic War leading to the downfall of the Teutonic Knights.
The last Welsh war of independence, led by Owain Glyndŵr.
Khizr Khan, deputised by Timur to be the governor of Multan, takes over Delhi founding the Sayyid dynasty.
Battle of Agincourt fought between the Kingdom of England and France.
Henry the Navigator leads the conquest of Ceuta from the Moors marking the beginning of the Portuguese Empire.
Jan Hus is burned at the stake as a heretic at the Council of Constance.
The Hussite Wars in Bohemia.
Construction of the Chinese Forbidden City is completed in Beijing.
In Sub-saharan Africa the Ife Empire has collapsed.
Deva Raya II succeeds his father Veera Vijaya Bukka Raya as monarch of the Vijayanagara Empire.
The Mamluk Sultanate launched campaigns against Cyprus, which becomes a tributary state of the Egyptians.
Catholic University of Leuven (Belgium) founded by Pope Martin V.
Reign of Itzcoatl begins as the fourth tlatoani of Tenochtitlan and the first emperor of the Aztec Empire.
Joan of Arc ends the Siege of Orléans and turns the tide of the Hundred Years' War.
Queen Suhita succeeds her father Wikramawardhana as ruler of Majapahit.
The Edessa Campaigns ends in an Egyptian victory over Aq Qoyunlu.
Rajah Lontok and Dayang Kalangitan become co-regent rulers of the ancient kingdom of Tondo.
The Edessa Campaigns ends with the Egyptians annexing Urfa.
The Catholics and Utraquists defeat the Taborites at the Battle of Lipany, ending the Hussite Wars.
Egypt's Mamluk Sultanate defeats the Ottoman Empire in the Battle of Diyarbakır, and the Egyptians annexes Harpoot.
Pachacuti founds the Inca Empire.
Eton College founded by Henry VI.
Oba Ewuare comes to power in the West African city of Benin, and turns it into an empire.
Reign of Moctezuma I begins as the fifth tlatoani of Tenochtitlan and emperor of the Aztec Empire.
Under Moctezuma I, the Aztecs become the dominant power in Mesoamerica.
A civil war between the Tutul Xiues and Cocom breaks out in the League of Mayapan. As a consequence, the league begins to disintegrate.
Jan van Eyck, Flemish painter, dies.
Portuguese navigators cruise West Africa and reestablish the European slave trade with a shipment of African slaves sent directly from Africa to Portugal.
Leonardo Bruni defines Middle Ages and Modern times.
Abdur Razzaq visits India.
King Sejong the Great publishes the hangul, the native phonetic alphabet system for the Korean language.
Ottoman Empire under Sultan Murad II defeats the Polish and Hungarian armies under Władysław III of Poland and János Hunyadi at the Battle of Varna.
The Kazan Khanate defeats the Grand Principality of Moscow at the Battle of Suzdal.
Mallikarjuna Raya succeeds his father Deva Raya II as monarch of the Vijayanagara Empire.
Wijaya Parakrama Wardhana, succeeds Suhita as ruler of Majapahit.
Esen Tayisi leads an Oirat Mongol invasion of China which culminate in the capture of the Zhengtong Emperor at Battle of Tumu Fortress.
Saint Srimanta Sankardeva was born.
Dayang Kalangitan became the Queen regnant of the ancient kingdom of Tondo that started Tondo's political dominance over Luzon.
Bahlul Khan Lodhi ascends the throne of the Delhi sultanate starting the Lodhi dynasty.
Rajasawardhana, born Bhre Pamotan, styled Brawijaya II succeeds Wijayaparakramawardhana as ruler of Majapahit.
Reign of Rajasawardhana ends.
The Battle of Castillon is the last engagement of the Hundred Years' War and the first battle in European history where cannons were a major factor in deciding the battle.
The Fall of Constantinople marks the end of the Byzantine Empire and the death of the last Roman Emperor Constantine XI and the beginning of the Classical Age of the Ottoman Empire.
After defeating the Teutonic Knights in the Thirteen Years' War, Poland annexes Royal Prussia.
Wars of the Roses – English civil war between the House of York and the House of Lancaster.
Girishawardhana, styled Brawijaya III, becomes ruler of Majapahit.
Joan of Arc is posthumously acquitted of heresy by the Catholic Church, redeeming her status as the heroine of France.
The Siege of Belgrade halts the Ottomans' advance into Europe.
Construction of Edo Castle begins.
The League of Mayapan disintegrates. The league is replaced by seventeen Kuchkabal.
The city of Sarajevo is founded by the Ottomans.
Mehmed the Conqueror is driven back by Wallachian prince Vlad III Dracula at The Night Attack.
Edward IV of England secretly marries Elizabeth Woodville.
Singhawikramawardhana, succeeds Girishawardhana as ruler of Majapahit.
The Sengoku period is one of civil war in Japan.
Uzun Hasan defeats the Black Sheep Turkoman leader Jahān Shāh.
Birth of Guru Nanak Dev. Beside followers of Sikhism, Guru Nanak is revered by Hindus and Muslim Sufis across the Indian subcontinent.
Matthias Corvinus of Hungary conquers some parts of Bohemia.
Reign of Axayacatl begins in the Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan as the sixth tlatoani and emperor of the Aztec Triple Alliance.
The Moldavian forces under Stephen the Great defeat the Tatars of the Golden Horde at the Battle of Lipnic.
The kingdom of Champa suffers a massive defeat by the Vietnamese king Lê Thánh Tông.
Abu Abd Allah al-Sheikh Muhammad ibn Yahya becomes the first Wattasid Sultan of Morocco.
Burgundy Wars of France, Switzerland, Lorraine and Sigismund II of Habsburg against the Charles the Bold, Duke of Burgundy.
Muscovy conquers Novgorod.
Reign of Singhawikramawardhana ends.
The Great Mosque of Demak is the oldest mosque in Java, built by the Wali Songo during the reign of Sultan Raden Patah.
Battle of Breadfield, Matthias Corvinus of Hungary defeated the Turks.
JagatGuru Vallabhacharya Ji Mahaprabhu was born.
After the Great standing on the Ugra river, Muscovy gained independence from the Great Horde.
Reign of Tizoc begins as the seventh tlatoani of Tenochtitlan and the emperor of the Aztec Triple Alliance.
Spanish Inquisition begins in practice with the first auto-da-fé.
Portuguese navigator Diogo Cão becomes the first European to enter the Congo.
The Jews are expelled from Andalusia.
William Caxton, the first printer of books in English, prints his translation of Aesop's Fables in London.
Henry VII defeats Richard III at the Battle of Bosworth and becomes King of England.
Ivan III of Russia conquered Tver.
Matthias Corvinus of Hungary captured Vienna, Frederick III, Holy Roman Emperor ran away.
Saluva Narasimha Deva Raya drives out Praudha Raya ending the Sangama Dynasty.
The Ottoman Empire loses Adana to the Egyptians following their defeat against the Mamluk Sultanate in the Adana campaign.
Reign of Ahuitzotl begins as the eighth tlatoani of Tenochtitlan and emperor of the Aztec Triple Alliance.
Sher Shah Suri, is born in Sasaram, Bihar.
Hongzhi Emperor ascends the throne, bringing Confucian ideology under his administration.
Portuguese Navigator Bartolomeu Dias sails around the Cape of Good Hope.
The Egyptians defeat the Ottoman Empire in the Ottoman–Mamluk War, and a peace treaty was signed, restoring the status quo ante bellum.
Boabdil's surrender of Granada marks the end of the Spanish Reconquista and Al-Andalus.
Christopher Columbus landed in the Americas from Spain.
Ferdinand and Isabella sign the Alhambra Decree, expelling all Jews from Spain unless they convert to Catholicism; 40,000–200,000 leave.
Christopher Columbus landed on modern-day Puerto Rico.
Leonardo da Vinci creates the first known design for a helicopter.
Spain and Portugal sign the Treaty of Tordesillas and agree to divide the World outside of Europe between themselves.
The Italian Wars lead to the downfall of the Italian city-states.
Manuel I succeeds John II as the king of Portugal.
Vasco da Gama's first voyage from Europe to India and back.
Michelangelo's Pietà in St. Peter's Basilica is made in Rome.
Ottoman fleet defeats Venetians at the Battle of Zonchio.
University "Alcalá de Henares" in Madrid, Spain is built.
Around late 15th century Bujangga Manik manuscript was composed, tell the story of Jaya Pakuan Bujangga Manik, a Sundanese Hindu hermit journeys throughout Java and Bali.
Charles of Ghent (future Lord of the Netherlands, King of Spain, Archduke of Austria, and Holy Roman Emperor) was born.
Guru Nanak begins the spreading of Sikhism, the fifth-largest religion in the world.
Islam becomes the dominant religion across the Indonesian archipelago.
Portuguese navigator Pedro Álvares Cabral claims Brazil for Portugal.
Spanish navigator Vicente Yáñez Pinzón encounters Brazil but is prevented from claiming it by the Treaty of Tordesillas.
The Ottoman fleet of Kemal Reis defeats the Venetians at the Second Battle of Lepanto.
Michelangelo returns to his native Florence to begin work on the statue David.
First reported African slaves in the New World.
The Crimean Khanate sacks Sarai in the Golden Horde, ending its existence.
Leonardo da Vinci begins painting the Mona Lisa and completes it three years later.
Nostradamus is born on either December 14 or December 21.
Spain defeats France at the Battle of Cerignola. Considered to be the first battle in history won by gunpowder small arms.
A period of drought, with famine in all of Spain.
Death of Isabella I of Castile; Joanna of Castile becomes the Queen.
Foundation of the Sultanate of Sennar by Amara Dunqas, in what is modern Sudan.
Martin Luther enters St. Augustine's Monastery at Erfurt, Germany, on 17 July and begins his journey to instigating the Reformation.
Zhengde Emperor ascends the throne of Ming dynasty.
At least two thousand converted Jews are massacred in a Lisbon riot, Portugal.
Christopher Columbus dies in Valladolid, Spain.
Leonardo da Vinci completes the Mona Lisa.
Poland is invaded by Tatars from the Crimean Khanate.
Afonso de Albuquerque conquered Hormuz and Muscat, among other bases in the Persian Gulf, taking control of the region at the entrance of the Gulf.
The first recorded epidemic of smallpox in the New World on the island of Hispaniola. It devastates the native Taíno population.
Michelangelo paints the Sistine Chapel ceiling.
The Christian-Islamic power struggle in Europe and West Asia spills over into the Indian Ocean as Battle of Chaul during the Portuguese-Mamluk War.
Krishnadevaraya ascends the throne of Vijayanagara Empire.
The 'great plague' in various parts of Tudor England.
Afonso de Albuquerque of Portugal conquers Goa in India.
Afonso de Albuquerque of Portugal conquers Malacca, the capital of the Sultanate of Malacca in present-day Malaysia.
Copernicus writes Commentariolus, and proclaims the Sun the center of the Solar System.
The southern part (historical core) of the Kingdom of Navarre is invaded by Castile and Aragon.
Henry VIII defeats the French at the Battle of the Spurs.
Machiavelli writes The Prince, a treatise about political philosophy.
Sultan Selim I ("The Grim") orders the massacre of Shia Muslims in Anatolia (present-day Turkey).
The Battle of Flodden Field in which invading Scots are defeated by Henry VIII's forces.
The Portuguese mariner Jorge Álvares lands at Macau, China, during the Ming dynasty.
Vasco Núñez de Balboa, in service of Spain arrives at the Pacific Ocean (which he called Mar del Sur) across the Isthmus of Panama. He was the first European to do so.
The Battle of Chaldiran, the Ottoman Empire gains decisive victory against Safavid dynasty.
The Battle of Orsha halts Muscovy's expansion into Eastern Europe.
Ascension of Francis I of France as King of France following the death of Louis XII.
The Ottoman Empire wrests Eastern Anatolia from the Safavids after the Battle of Chaldiran.
The Ottomans conquer the last beyliks of Anatolia, the Dulkadirs and the Ramadanids.
The Ottomans defeat the Mamluks and gain control of Egypt, Arabia, and the Levant.
The Reformation begins when Martin Luther posts his Ninety-five Theses in Saxony.
The Sweating sickness epidemic in Tudor England.
Mir Chakar Khan Rind leaves Baluchistan and settles in Punjab.
Barbary pirates led by Hayreddin Barbarossa, a Turk appointed to ruling position in Algiers by the Ottoman Empire, raid Provence and Toulon in southern France.
Death of Emperor Maximilian; Charles I of Austria, Spain, and the Low Countries becomes Emperor of Holy Roman Empire as Charles V, Holy Roman Emperor.
Hernán Cortés leads the Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire.
Spanish expedition commanded by Magellan and Elcano are the first to Circumnavigate the Earth.
The Portuguese established a trading post in the village of Lamakera on the eastern side of Solor (in present-day Indonesia) as a transit harbour between Maluku and Malacca.
The first European diplomatic mission to Ethiopia, sent by the Portuguese, arrives at Massawa 9 April, and reaches the imperial encampment of Emperor Dawit II in Shewa 9 October.
The reign of Suleiman the Magnificent marks the zenith of the Ottoman Empire.
Vijayanagara Empire forces under Krishnadevaraya defeat the Adil Shahi under at the Battle of Raichur.
After building fortifications at Tuen Mun, the Portuguese attempt to invade Ming dynasty China, but are expelled by Chinese naval forces.
Belgrade (in present-day Serbia) is captured by the Ottoman Empire.
Jiajing Emperor ascended the throne of Ming dynasty, China.
November, Ferdinand Magellan's expedition reaches Maluku (in present-day Indonesia) and after trade with Ternate returns to Europe with a load of cloves.
Pati Unus leads the invasion of Malacca (in present-day Malaysia) against the Portuguese occupation. Pati Unus was killed in this battle, and was succeeded by his brother, sultan Trenggana.
Philippines encountered by Ferdinand Magellan. He was later killed in the Battle of Mactan in central Philippines in the same year.
August, Luso-Sundanese Treaty signed between Portugal and Sunda Kingdom granted Portuguese permit to build a fortress in Sunda Kelapa.
The Portuguese ally themselves with the rulers of Ternate (in present-day Indonesia) and begin construction of a fort.
Sweden gains independence from the Kalmar Union.
The Cacao bean is introduced to Spain by Hernán Cortés.
German Peasants' War in the Holy Roman Empire.
Giovanni da Verrazzano is the first European to explore the Atlantic coast of North America between South Carolina and Newfoundland.
German and Spanish forces defeat France at the Battle of Pavia, Francis I of France is captured.
Timurid Empire forces under Babur defeat the Lodi dynasty at the First Battle of Panipat, end of the Delhi Sultanate.
Mughal Empire, founded by Babur.
The Ottomans defeat the Kingdom of Hungary at the Battle of Mohács.
Mughal Empire forces defeat the Rajput led by Rana Sanga of Mewar at the Battle of Khanwa.
Protestant Reformation begins in Sweden.
Sack of Rome with Pope Clement VII escaping and the Swiss Guards defending the Vatican being killed. The sack of the city of Rome considered the end of the Italian Renaissance.
Imam Ahmad Gurey defeats the Ethiopian Emperor Dawit II in the Battle of Shimbra Kure, the opening clash of the Ethiopian–Adal War.
The Austrians defeat the Ottoman Empire at the siege of Vienna.
Treaty of Zaragoza defined the antimeridian of Tordesillas attributing the Moluccas to Portugal and Philippines to Spain.
The Church of England breaks away from the Catholic Church and recognizes King Henry VIII as the head of the Church.
The Inca Civil War is fought between the two brothers, Atahualpa and Huáscar.
Foundation of São Vicente, the first permanent Portuguese settlement in the Americas.
Francisco Pizarro leads the Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire.
Anne Boleyn becomes Queen of England.
Elizabeth Tudor is born.
Affair of the Placards, where King Francis I becomes more active in repression of French Protestants.
Jacques Cartier claims Canada for France.
The Ottomans capture Baghdad from the Safavids.
The Münster Rebellion, an attempt of radical, millennialist, Anabaptists to establish a theocracy, ends in bloodshed.
Catherine of Aragon dies in Kimbolton Castle, in England.File:ImperioOtomanoSimplificado-en.svg thumb Territorial expansion of the Ottoman Empire under Suleiman (in red and orange).
Establishment of the Inquisition in Portugal.
Foundation of Buenos Aires (in present-day Argentina) by Pedro de Mendoza.
In England, Anne Boleyn is beheaded for adultery and treason.
The Portuguese establish Recife in Pernambuco, north-east of Brazil.
William Tyndale's partial translation of the Bible into English is published, which would eventually be incorporated into the King James Bible.
Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada founds Bogotá.
Spanish–Venetian fleet is defeated by the Ottoman Turks at the Battle of Preveza.
Hernando de Soto explores inland North America.
The Society of Jesus, or the Jesuits, is founded by Ignatius of Loyola and six companions with the approval of Pope Paul III.
Amazon River is encountered and explored by Francisco de Orellana.
An Algerian military campaign by Charles V of Spain (Habsburg) is unsuccessful.
Capture of Buda and the absorption of the major part of Hungary by the Ottoman Empire.
Pedro de Valdivia founds Santiago in Chile.
Sahib I Giray of Crimea invades Russia.
Akbar The Great is born in the Rajput Umarkot Fort.
Spanish explorer Ruy López de Villalobos named the island of Samar and Leyte Las Islas Filipinas honoring Philip II of Spain and became the official name of the archipelago.
Copernicus publishes his theory that the Earth and the other planets revolve around the Sun.

The Wahhabis of the First Saudi State sack Karbala.
The Wahhabis of the First Saudi State capture Mecca and Medina.
William Symington demonstrates his Charlotte Dundas, the "first practical steamboat".
Austrian Empire founded by Francis I.
World population reaches 1 billion.
The rise of Muhammad Ali to power, and Egypt gains de facto autonomy from Ottoman rule and begin a comprehensive modernization phase.
Elisha Collier invents the Flintlock Revolver.
February 1 Eruption of Mayon Volcano.
Shaka's Zulu Kingdom becomes the largest in Southern Africa.
The Republic of Colombia (Gran Colombia) achieves independence after Simón Bolívar's triumph at the Battle of Boyacá.
The modern city of Singapore is established by the British East India Company.
Discovery of Antarctica.
Dissolution of the Maratha Empire.
Liberia founded by the American Colonization Society for freed American slaves.
First Mexican Empire, as Mexico's first post-independence government, ruled by Emperor Agustín I of Mexico.
Pedro I of Brazil declared Brazil's independence from Portugal on 7 September.
Monroe Doctrine declared by US President James Monroe.
The Decembrist revolt.
Sir Robert Peel founds the Metropolitan Police Service, the first modern police force.
Egyptian Army defeats the Ottoman Empire in the Egyptian–Ottoman War.
November Uprising ends with crushing defeat for Poland in the Battle of Warsaw.
Imam Shamil's rebellion in Russian-occupied Caucasus.
The Texas Revolution in Mexico resulted in the short-lived Republic of Texas.
By this time, 46,000 Native Americans have been forcibly relocated in the Trail of Tears.
Anglo-Afghan Wars lead to stalemate and the establishment of the Durand line.
Treaty of Nanking cedes Hong Kong to the British.
The first wagon train sets out from Missouri.
Rochdale Society of Equitable Pioneers establish what is considered the first cooperative in the world.
The Great Famine of Ireland leads to the Irish diaspora.
California Gold Rush.
Seneca Falls Convention is the first women's rights convention in the United States and leads to the battle for women's suffrage.
The Communist Manifesto published.
Earliest recorded air raid, as Austria employs 200 balloons to deliver ordnance against Venice.
Franz Hermann Schulze-Delitzsch establishes the first cooperative financial institution.
The Little Ice Age ends around this time.
The Great Exhibition in London was the world's first international Expo or World Fair.
Frederick Douglass delivers his speech "The Meaning of July Fourth for the Negro" in Rochester, New York.
Sir Joseph Whitworth designs the first long-range sniper rifle.
Construction of Big Ben is completed.
Suez Canal is constructed.
Giuseppe Garibaldi launches the Expedition of the Thousand.
Russia abolishes serfdom.
Muslim Rebellion in north-west China.
Reconstruction in the United States; Slavery is banned in the United States by the Thirteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution.
Canada is formed, via the process of Canadian Confederation.
Michael Barrett is the last person to be publicly hanged in England.
The Suez Canal opens linking the Mediterranean to the Red Sea.
Long Depression in Western Europe and North America.
Official dismantling of the Cultivation System and beginning of a 'Liberal Policy' of deregulated exploitation of the Netherlands East Indies.
Famine in Persia is believed to have caused the death of 2 million.
The Paris Commune briefly rules the French capital.
Yellowstone National Park, the first national park, is created.
The Khedivate of Egypt defeat the Sultanate of Darfur and annexes Darfur.
The Home Rule Movement is established in Ireland.
The annexation of the Emirate of Harar and northern Somali coast by the Egyptians.
HMS Challenger surveys the deepest point in the Earth's oceans, the Challenger Deep.
Battle of the Little Bighorn leads to the death of General Custer and victory for the alliance of Lakota, Cheyenne and Arapaho.
The massive expansion in population, territory, industry and wealth in the United States is referred to as the Gilded Age.
Great Railroad Strike in the United States may have been the world's first nationwide labour strike.
The Jules Ferry laws are passed in France establishing free, secular education.
Wave of pogroms begins in the Russian Empire.
Krakatoa volcano explosion, one of the largest in modern history.
The quagga is rendered extinct.
Construction of the Statue of Liberty; Coca-Cola is developed.
Founding of the shipping line Koninklijke Paketvaart-Maatschappij (KPM) that supported the unification and development of the colonial economy.
The Golden Law abolishes slavery in Brazil.
A republican military coup establishes the First Brazilian Republic. The parliamentary constitutional monarchy is abolished.
Eiffel Tower is inaugurated in Paris.
First use of the electric chair as a method of execution.
Fingerprinting is officially adopted for the first time.
The World's Columbian Exposition was held in Chicago celebrating the 400th anniversary of Christopher Columbus's arrival in the New World.
New Zealand becomes the first country to enact women's suffrage.
The Coremans-de Vriendt law is passed in Belgium, creating legal equality for French and Dutch languages.
Philippine Revolution ends declaring Philippines free from Spanish rule.
Empress Dowager Cixi of China engineers a coup d'état, marking the end of the Hundred Days' Reform; the Guangxu Emperor is arrested.
The United States gains control of Cuba, Puerto Rico, and the Philippines after the Spanish–American War.
Admiral Fredrik von Otter becomes Prime Minister of Sweden.
American explorer Robert Peary is the first person to sight Kaffeklubben Island.
Boxer Rebellion: Boxers gather about 20,000 people near Peking, and kill hundreds of European citizens, including the German ambassador.
Boxer Rebellion: Foreign diplomats in Peking, Qing dynasty China, demand that the Boxer rebels (who oppose foreign interests in the country) be disciplined.
Boxer Rebellion: Peacekeepers from various European countries arrive in China, where they eventually unite with Japanese forces.
Eight nations invade China at the same time and ransack Forbidden City.
Held in Paris, prominently featuring the growing art trend Art Nouveau.
Herbert Kitchener succeeds Frederick Roberts as commander-in-chief of the British forces in South Africa and implements a scorched earth strategy.
Second Boer War: British troops defeat the Boers at Ladysmith, South Africa.
The Chinese province of Manchuria is invaded by the Russian Empire.
The first Michelin Guide is published for French motorists.
The first zeppelin airship flight, by Zeppelin LZ 1, is carried out over Lake Constance, near Friedrichshafen, Germany.
Two U.S. Navy cruisers are sent to Central America to protect American interests in a dispute between Nicaragua and Costa Rica.
Anti-Semitic rioting breaks out in Budapest.
Auguste Deter is first examined by German psychiatrist Dr. Alois Alzheimer, leading to a diagnosis of the condition that will carry Alzheimer's name.
Cuba becomes a United States protectorate.
In Bremen, an assassination attempt is made on Wilhelm II, German Emperor.
Michigan schoolteacher Annie Edson Taylor goes over Niagara Falls in a barrel and survives.
The Hawaii Territory Legislature convenes for the first time.
The National Association of Professional Baseball Leagues (later renamed Minor League Baseball), is formed in Chicago.
The State funeral of Queen Victoria, held at St George's Chapel, Windsor Castle, UK, is attended by many European royals, including Kaiser Wilhelm II and Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria.
The Sultan of Turkey orders 50,000 troops to the Bulgarian frontier because of unrest in Macedonia.
The first United Kingdom Fingerprint Bureau is established at Scotland Yard, the Metropolitan Police headquarters in London, by Edward Henry.
The first claimed powered flight is made, by German-born American aviator Gustave Whitehead, in his Number 21, in Connecticut.
Vice President Theodore Roosevelt becomes the 26th president of the United States, upon President William McKinley's death.
A newspaper cartoon depicting U.S. President "Teddy" Roosevelt refusing to shoot a bear cub inspires creation of the first teddy bear by Morris Michtom in New York City.
Alfonso XIII of Spain begins his reign.
Australian officers Breaker Morant and Peter Handcock are executed for the murder of Boer prisoners of war near Louis Trichardt.
Erik Gustaf Boström returns as Prime Minister of Sweden.
Fluminense Football Club is founded in Rio de Janeiro.
Rimsky-Korsakov's opera Servillia premieres in St. Petersburg.
The 1st Conference of the International Woman Suffrage Alliance takes place in Washington, D.C.
The 7.5 Guatemala earthquake shakes Guatemala with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe), killing between 800 and 2,000.
The Electric Theatre, the first movie theater in the United States, opens in Los Angeles.
The London School of Economics is opened by Lord Rosebery.
The first Aswan Dam on the Nile is completed.
Venezuela: President Castro's army overcomes rebels in seven-day battle.
Atlético Madrid is founded as a professional association football club in Spain.
Edward VII is proclaimed Emperor of India.
First modern World Series: The Boston Americans defeat the Pittsburgh Pirates in eight games.
Having abolished the Sokoto Caliphate in West Africa, the new British administration accepts the concession of its last vizier.
Orville Wright flies an aircraft with a petrol engine, the Wright Flyer, at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina in the first documented and successful powered and controlled heavier-than-air flight.
Pope Pius X succeeds Pope Leo XIII as the 257th pope.
The British Admiralty announces plans to build the Rosyth Dockyard as a naval base at Rosyth in Scotland.
The English-language South China Morning Post newspaper is first published in Hong Kong.
The Hay–Bunau-Varilla Treaty is signed by the United States and Panama, giving the U.S. exclusive rights over the Panama Canal Zone.
The Paris–Madrid race for automobiles begins, during which at least eight people are killed; the French government stops the event at Bordeaux and impounds all of the competitors' cars.
The Second Congress of the All-Russian Social Democratic Labour Party is held in exile in Brussels, transferring to London.
The first Tour de France is held; Maurice Garin wins it.
The first stock-car event is held at the Milwaukee Mile.
The town of Heppner, Oregon is nearly destroyed by a cloud burst that results in a flash flood that kills about 238 people.
A fire aboard the steamboat General Slocum in New York City's East River kills 1,021.
Aleister Crowley writes The Book of the Law, a text central to Thelema, in Cairo.
German journalist Anna Rüling, in a speech to the Scientific-Humanitarian Committee in Berlin, makes the first known public statement of the socio-legal problems faced by lesbians.
Griffin Park football ground, home of Brentford F.C., opens in London.
Ismael Montes becomes President of Bolivia.
Panama and Uruguay establish diplomatic relations.
Puccini's opera Madama Butterfly debuts at La Scala in Milan, to no great acclaim. On May 28 a revised version opens in Brescia, to huge success.
Scottish National Antarctic Expedition: Led by William Speirs Bruce, the Antarctic region of Coats Land is discovered from the Scotia.
The Daytona Educational and Industrial Training School for Negro Girls, predecessor of Bethune–Cookman University, is opened in Florida by Mary McLeod Bethune.
The St. Petersburg Soviet urges a run on the banks; the attempt fails, and the executive committee is arrested.
The distress signal CQD is established, only to be replaced 2 years later by SOS.
Albert Einstein submits for publication his paper "On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies", establishing his theory of special relativity.
British Princess Margaret of Connaught marries Prince Gustaf Adolf of Sweden, Duke of Skåne, the future King Gustaf VI Adolf.
Grand Duke Sergei Alexandrovich of Russia, the Governor-General of Moscow and uncle of Tsar Nicholas II, is assassinated.
In a major defeat in the Russo-Japanese War, Russian General Anatoly Stessel surrenders Port Arthur, located on mainland China, to the Japanese.
Las Vegas, Nevada, is founded when of land adjacent to the Union Pacific Railroad tracks are auctioned to form what becomes Downtown Las Vegas.
The British Imperial Penny Post is extended to include Australia.
The Russian Council appointed by Tsar Nicholas II meets at Peterhof and approves a plan for a national Duma, the first representative assembly in the Empire.
The millennia-old imperial examination system for the civil service is abolished in Qing dynasty China.
The popular fictional character Arsène Lupin, the gentleman thief, is introduced in France.
An aeroplane of Alberto Santos-Dumont takes off at Bagatelle in France, and flies 60 meters. This is the first officially recorded powered flight in Europe.
Courrières mine disaster: An explosion in a coal mine in France kills 1,060.
In the Grand Duchy of Finland, a new electoral law is ratified, guaranteeing full women's suffrage, the first in modern Europe. Women can also stand in national elections.
In the Russian Empire, the Fundamental Laws are announced at the first state Duma.
International Exhibition opens in Christchurch, New Zealand.
Karl Staaff steps down as Prime Minister of Sweden over the issue of expanded voting rights. He is replaced by right-wing naval officer and public official Arvid Lindman.
Mahatma Gandhi coins the term Satyagraha, to characterize the nonviolence movement in South Africa.
Reginald Fessenden makes the first radio broadcast: a poetry reading, a violin solo, and a speech, from Brant Rock, Massachusetts.
The National Consultative Assembly (Majlis) of Iran convenes for the first time.
The RMS Mauretania is launched on the River Tyne, becoming the world's largest ship.
The United Kingdom, France and Italy sign an agreement to preserve, in Ethiopia, the integrity of the ancient empire of Abyssinia.
The steamboat Dix sinks en route from Seattle to Port Blakely claiming the lives of approximately 50 passengers and crew.

British Cunard Line passenger liner sets out on her maiden voyage, from Liverpool (England) to New York City.
Guglielmo Marconi initiates commercial transatlantic radio communications between his high power longwave wireless telegraphy stations in Clifden, Ireland, and Glace Bay, Nova Scotia.
Hershey Park opens in Hershey, Pennsylvania.
New Zealand and Newfoundland become dominions of the British Empire.
The 5th Congress of the Russian Social Democratic Labour Party convenes in secret in London.
The American Great White Fleet begins its circumnavigation of the world.
The Austrian Lloyd steamship Imperatrix, from Trieste to Bombay, is wrecked on Cape of Crete and sinks; 137 lives are lost.
The Peking to Paris motor race is won by Prince Scipione Borghese, driving a 7-litre 35/45 hp Itala.
The first taxicabs with taximeters begin operating in London.
