The steamship Larchmont collides with the Harry Hamilton in Long Island Sound; 183 lives are lost.
Tiflis bank robbery: Bolsheviks attack a cash-filled bank coach in the centre of Tiflis, Georgia, killing 40 people.
UPS is founded by James E. (Jim) Casey in Seattle, Washington.
Černová massacre: Fifteen people are shot during the consecration of a Catholic church in Hungary (modern-day Slovakia).
After an intense power struggle, Sultan Abdelaziz of Morocco is deposed and is succeeded by his brother Abd al-Hafid.
Alpha Kappa Alpha, the first race inclusive sorority is founded on the campus of Howard University in Washington, D.C.
At Masjed Soleyman in southwest Persia, the first major commercial oil discovery in the Middle East is made. The rights to the resource are quickly acquired by the United Kingdom.
Classes begin at Benjamin Franklin Institute of Technology in Boston, Massachusetts, established under the terms of Franklin's will.
Emperor Puyi ascends the Chinese throne at age 2 in succession to his uncle. He will reign for 3 years, then again for 11 days, and finally for 11 years as a puppet emperor.
H. H. Asquith of the Liberal Party takes office as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom, succeeding Sir Henry Campbell-Bannerman.

Panathinaikos A.O., a well-known professional multi-sports club of Greece, is founded in Athens.
Robert Peary sets sail for the North Pole.
The British Nimrod Expedition led by Ernest Shackleton sets sail from New Zealand for Antarctica on the Nimrod.
The Federal Bureau of Investigation is founded in the United States.

The University of Omaha, precursor of the University of Nebraska Omaha, is founded as a private non-sectarian college.
Adana massacre: Ottoman Turks kill 15,000–30,000 Armenian Christians, in the Adana Vilayet.
Blue Anchor Line passenger/cargo liner, on her second voyage from Australia to Britain, leaves Durban and is lost without trace with all 211 aboard.
Colombia recognizes the independence of Panama.
Construction begins on the RMS Titanic, at the Harland and Wolff Shipyard in Belfast.
Einar Dessau uses a shortwave radio transmitter in Denmark.
French forces capture Abéché, capital of the Wadai Empire in central Africa.
In Nicaragua, 500 revolutionaries are executed by order of dictator José Santos Zelaya. The United States responds by sending 2 warships.
In Portugal, a magnitude 6.0 earthquake strikes near Lisbon, killing at least 60 people.
Japan and China sign the Gando Convention, which gives Japan a way to receive railroad concessions in Manchuria.
Members of the Nimrod Expedition claim to have found the magnetic South Pole (but the location recorded may be incorrect).

The Payne–Aldrich Tariff Act is passed in the United States Congress.
The association football team Borussia Dortmund is founded in Dortmund, Germany.
The association football team Coritiba is founded in Curitiba, Brazil.

A fire during a barn-dance in Ököritófülpös, Hungary, kills 312 people after ballroom decorations catch alight.
Abé people in the French West Africa colony of Côte d'Ivoire rise against the colonial administration; the rebellion is brutally suppressed by the military.
Chinese expedition to Tibet: A force of 2,000 Chinese troops march into Lhasa, the capital of Tibet; the 13th Dalai Lama, Thubten Gyatso, is forced to flee to British India.

First Girl Guide troops registered in the United Kingdom, under the supervision of Agnes Baden-Powell.

Albania declares independence from the Ottoman Empire.

John Flammang Schrank attempts to assassinate Theodore Roosevelt in Milwaukee.
Roald Amundsen, in Hobart, Tasmania, announces his success in reaching the South Pole the previous December.

The Overseas Railroad officially opens on the Florida Keys.
The Republic of China is established.
Igor Sikorsky becomes the first person to pilot a 4-engine fixed-wing aircraft.
Mexican Revolution: Pancho Villa returns to Mexico from his self-imposed exile in the United States.

Mexican Revolution: President Francisco I. Madero and Vice President José María Pino Suárez are forced to resign.

The United States Soccer Federation is formed.
The Woman Suffrage Procession takes place in Washington, D.C. led by Inez Milholland on horseback.
Battle of Le Cateau: British, French, and Belgian forces make a successful tactical retreat from the German advance.

The Exposition Internationale is held at Lyon, France.

The Teoloyucan Treaties are signed in the State of Mexico.
Woodrow Wilson's envoy, Edward Mandell House, meets Kaiser Wilhelm II.

Chilembwe uprising: Baptist minister John Chilembwe initiates an ultimately unsuccessful uprising against British colonial rule in Nyasaland (modern-day Malawi).

Women's suffrage in national elections is introduced in Denmark.
Hipólito Yrigoyen is elected President of Argentina.
Lassen Volcanic National Park is established in California.
Mary Pickford becomes the first movie star to sign a million-dollar contract, making her one of the highest-paid people in the world.
Mary, a circus elephant, is hanged in the town of Erwin, Tennessee for killing her handler, Walter "Red" Eldridge.

U.S. President Woodrow Wilson signs legislation creating the National Park Service.

WWI: The Egyptian Expeditionary Force begins the occupation of the Sinai Peninsula.

In Petrograd, 40,000 ethnic Estonians demand national autonomy within Russia.
Russian troops mutiny, abandon the Austrian front, and retreat to Ukraine; hundreds are shot by their commanding officers during the retreat.
The Green Corn Rebellion, an uprising by several hundred farmers against the WWI draft, takes place in central Oklahoma.
The United States enacts the Espionage Act.
The United States ends its search for Pancho Villa.
The enactment of the Jones Act grants Puerto Ricans United States citizenship.

Finnish Civil War: The battle of Tampere ends.
Operations against the Marri and Khetran tribes in Balochistan by British authorities begin.
Porvenir massacre: Texas Rangers, U.S. Cavalry soldiers and local ranchers kill 15 unarmed Mexican villagers, both men and boys.
Suspects in the Chicago Restaurant Poisonings are arrested, and more than 100 waiters are taken into custody for poisoning restaurant customers with a lethal powder called Mickey Finn.
WWI – Charge at Haritan: Units of the Desert Mounted Corps battle with Ottoman forces for the last time in WWI.

WWI: British armies and their Arab allies roll into Syria.

Benito Mussolini founds his Italian Fascist political movement in Milan.
Estonian and Latvian Wars of Independence: The advancing pro-German Baltische Landeswehr initiates war against Estonia in Northern Latvia.
In Belgium, a new electoral law introduces universal manhood suffrage and gives the franchise to certain classes of women.
Pressburg (Bratislava) becomes the capital of Slovakia.
Russian Civil War: Southern Front counteroffensive – The Red Army commanded by Vladimir Yegoryev attacks the White Volunteer Army of General Anton Denikin but is defeated.
Russian Civil War: The Red Army's Caspian-Caucasian Front begins the Northern Caucasus Operation against the White Army, but fails to make progress.
The Dutch airline KLM is founded.
The Florida Keys hurricane kills 600 in the Gulf of Mexico, Florida and Texas.
The Founding Congress of the Comintern opens in Moscow.
The French Army blows up the bridge over the Dniester at Bender, Moldova, to protect the city from the Bolsheviks.
Workers' councils in Berlin end the general strike; the Spartacist uprising is over.
Bukhara operation: The Russian Red Army and Young Bukharians overthrow the Emirate of Bukhara, leading to the establishment of the Bukharan People's Soviet Republic.

Polish–Soviet War: Battle of Warsaw – The Red Army is defeated.
Polish–Soviet War: Poland sues for peace with Soviet Russia (which refuses).
Polish–Soviet War: Polish and anti-Soviet Ukrainian troops attack the Red Army in Soviet Ukraine.
Russian Civil War: The forces of Russian White Admiral Alexander Kolchak surrender in Krasnoyarsk; the Great Siberian Ice March ensues.
Sigma Tau Gamma is founded on campus at the University of Central Missouri in Warrensburg, Missouri.
The Edmonton Symphony Orchestra holds its first concert, in Alberta.
The Treaty of Seeb is signed, ending the Muscat rebellion and granting the Imamate of Oman autonomy from the Sultanate of Muscat and Oman.
The first draft of the Mandate for Palestine is submitted to the League of Nations.
Venustiano Carranza is buried in Mexico City; all of his mourning allies are arrested. Adolfo de la Huerta is elected provisional president.
A Socialist congress at Vienna ends with the International Working Union of Socialist Parties founded.
A general strike begins in Norway, begun by 120,000 workers led by Ole O. Lian.
In the United States, the Sheppard–Towner Act is signed by President Harding, providing federal funding for maternity and child care.
In the continuing Rif War, the Spanish Army defeats rifkabyl rebels in Morocco.
Italian battleship Leonardo da Vinci is righted in Taranto Harbour.
King Faisal I of Iraq is crowned in Baghdad.
Spanish Premier Eduardo Dato e Iradier is assassinated while exiting the parliament building in Madrid.
Teaching at the University of Szeged begins, in the Kingdom of Hungary.
The Communist Party of Czechoslovakia is founded.
The Spanish liner Santa Isabel breaks in two and sinks off Villa Garcia, Mexico, with the loss of 244 of the 300 people on board.
The Third Congress of the Communist International takes place.
Third Silesian Uprising: Poles in Upper Silesia rise against the Germans.
Upper Silesia votes for re-annexation to Germany.
White Castle hamburger restaurant opens in Wichita, Kansas, foundation of the world's first fast food chain.

Dáil Éireann, the parliament of the Irish Republic, ratifies the Anglo-Irish Treaty by 64–57 votes.
In Washington, D.C., United States, the Lincoln Memorial is dedicated.
Joseph Stalin is appointed General Secretary of the Central Committee of the Soviet Communist Party.
Mahatma Gandhi is arrested in Bombay for sedition.
Modern Art Week in São Paulo marks the start of Modernism in Brazil.
Radio station WLW in Cincinnati begins broadcasting.

The Cherkess (Adyghe) Autonomous Oblast is established within the Russian SFSR.

The trial of Edith Thompson and Frederick Bywaters ends at the Old Bailey in London, for the murder of Thompson's husband; both are found guilty and sentenced to hang.

American explorer Roy Chapman Andrews discovers the first dinosaur eggs near Flaming Cliffs, Mongolia.
British Prime Minister Bonar Law resigns, due to ill health.

Küstrin Putsch: Outside Berlin, Major Ernst Buchrucker, a leader of the Black Reichswehr, attempts a putsch by seizing several forts.
Lithuania begins the Klaipėda Revolt to annex the Klaipėda Region (Memel Territory).
The Irish Free State joins the League of Nations.
The Kandersteg International Scout Centre comes into existence in Switzerland.
The first British Track & Field championships for women are held in London.
The fourth tropical storm of the year forms just north of Panama.
Vladimir Lenin suffers his third stroke, which renders him bedridden and unable to speak; consequently he retires from his position as Chairman of the Soviet government.
Ernst Alexanderson sends the first facsimile across the Atlantic Ocean, which goes to his father in Sweden.
GMT: A radio time signal is broadcast for the first time, from the Royal Greenwich Observatory.
Gopinath Saha shoots Ernest Day, whom he has mistaken for Sir Charles Tegart, the police commissioner of Calcutta, and is arrested soon after.
Harry Grindell Matthews attempts to demonstrate his "death ray" to the War Office in the United Kingdom.
Horacio Vásquez wins the Dominican Republic general election, becoming president, coinciding with the end of United States military occupation.
Municipal Grant Park Stadium, in Chicago, Illinois (later known as Soldier Field) is officially dedicated.
Napalpí massacre: Around 400 indigenous people of Toba ethnicity are massacred in Argentina.
Ramsay MacDonald becomes the first Labour Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
Sweden's Prime Minister Ernst Trygger and his cabinet, is replaced by Hjalmar Branting and his third and last government.
The International Chess Federation (FIDE) is founded.
The Trial of the 149 begins in Estonia, eventually resulting in the conviction of 129 communists, including several members of the Riigikogu.
U.S. Army pilots John Harding and Erik Nelson complete the first aerial circumnavigation of the globe. It has taken them 175 days and 74 stops before their return to Seattle.
A communist assault on St Nedelya Church claims roughly 150 lives in Sofia, Bulgaria.
At 22:42 local time a 7.0 earthquake shakes the Chinese province of Yunnan killing 5,000 people.
English explorer Percy Fawcett sends a last telegram to his wife before he disappears in the Amazon.
Pope Pius XI's encyclical Quas primas, on the Feast of Christ the King, is promulgated.
The ' is held in Paris, giving a name to the Art Deco style.
The French complete their evacuation of the Ruhr region of Germany.
The General Election Law is passed in Japan, extending suffrage to all males aged 25 and over.
The Locarno Treaties are negotiated.
The Syrian Federation is officially dissolved, the State of Aleppo and the State of Damascus having been replaced by the State of Syria.
The major money forgery and fraud of Alves dos Reis is exposed in Portugal.
The silent film El Húsar de la Muerte is released in Santiago, Chile.
Werner Heisenberg, Max Born and Pascual Jordan published their Umdeutung paper, reporting a breakthrough in quantum physics, in Zeitschrift für Physik in Germany.
İsmet İnönü is appointed prime minister in Turkey.
A Caudron C.61 aircraft, operated by Compagnie Internationale de Navigation Aérienne, crashes in Czechoslovakia.
An ammunition explosion on troopship Kuang Yuang near Jiujiang, China, kills 1,200.
An assassination attempt against Italian Fascist leader Benito Mussolini fails.
British and Belgian troops leave Cologne.
English detective story writer Agatha Christie disappears from her home in Surrey; on December 14 she is found under her husband's mistress's surname at a Harrogate hotel.
In Greece, Georgios Kondylis ousts Theodoros Pangalos.
Liberal politician Carl Gustaf Ekman succeeds Rickard Sandler as Prime Minister of Sweden.
The United Kingdom general strike begins at midnight, in support of a strike by coal miners.
The United States Numbered Highway System, including U.S. Route 66, is established.
The first Lebanese constitution is established.
Theodoros Pangalos declares himself dictator in Greece.
British police officers raid the office of the Soviet trade delegation in London.
Carving of the sculptures at Mount Rushmore, South Dakota, begins.
Chiang Kai-shek marries Soong Mei-ling in Shanghai.
The 7.6 Gulang earthquake affects Gansu in northwest China with a maximum Mercalli intensity of XI (Extreme), leaving over 40,000 dead.
The British Broadcasting Company becomes the British Broadcasting Corporation, when its royal charter of incorporation takes effect. John Reith becomes the first Director-General.
The Peace Bridge opens between Fort Erie, Ontario, and Buffalo, New York.
The U.S. Federal Radio Commission (later renamed the Federal Communications Commission) begins to regulate the use of radio frequencies.
The first fully electronic television system is achieved by Philo Farnsworth.
Yugoslavia severs diplomatic relations with Albania.
İsmet İnönü forms a new government in Turkey.
British bacteriologist Frederick Griffith reports the results of Griffith's experiment, indirectly demonstrating that DNA is the genetic material.
Charles Jenkins Laboratories' W3XK station begins broadcasting on 6.42 MHz, using 48 lines.
In Scotland, May Donoghue finds the remains of a snail in her ginger beer, leading to the landmark negligence case Donoghue v Stevenson.
Jinan incident: An armed conflict between the Imperial Japanese Army (allied with Northern Chinese warlords) and the Kuomintang's southern army occurs in Jinan, China.
Persija Jakarta Association football club is founded as Voetbalbond Indonesische Jacatra.
Scottish-born inventor John Logie Baird broadcasts a transatlantic television signal from London to Hartsdale, New York.
Students take over the medical wing of Rosario University in Argentina.
The Muslim Brotherhood is founded in Egypt by Islamic scholar and schoolteacher Hassan al-Banna.
The Phi Sigma Alpha fraternity is founded at the University of Puerto Rico, Río Piedras Campus.
The women's organisation Gruaja Shiqiptare is founded in Albania, with Princess Senije as its chair.
All Quiet on the Western Front (Im Westen nichts Neues), by Erich Maria Remarque, is published in book form.
Aristide Briand presents his plan for the United States of Europe.
Fritz von Opel pilots the first rocket-powered aircraft, the Opel RAK.1, in front of a large crowd in Frankfurt am Main.
In New York City, the Museum of Modern Art (MoMA) opens to the public. The first exhibition Cézanne, Gauguin, van Gogh and Seurat is seen by 47.000 visitors; the curator is Alfred H. Barr.
John Logie Baird's experimental 30-line television system is first transmitted, by the British Broadcasting Corporation in London.
Persia signs the Litvinov Protocol.
Ramsay MacDonald forms the United Kingdom's second Labour government.
The United Kingdom general election again returns a hung parliament; the Liberals in Parliament determine which party will govern.
The second of the Davos University Conferences opens in Switzerland; this includes the Cassirer–Heidegger debate in philosophy.
Carl Gustaf Ekman becomes Prime Minister of Sweden, for the second and final time.
Heinrich Brüning is appointed Chancellor of Germany.
Mount Merapi volcano in central Java, Indonesia, erupts, destroying numerous villages and killing 1,300 people.
Nurse Ellen Church becomes the world's first flight attendant, working on a Boeing Air Transport trimotor.
Scotch Tape, invented by Richard Gurley Drew, is sold by the 3M company in the United States for the first time.
The Chittagong Rebellion begins in India with the Chittagong armoury raid.
The Việt Nam Quốc Dân Đảng launch the Yên Bái mutiny in the hope of ending French colonial rule in Vietnam.
The dedication of George Washington's sculpted head is held at Mount Rushmore, South Dakota.
The first British Empire Games open in Hamilton, Ontario, Canada.
The volcanic island of Anak Krakatau begins to form permanently in the Sunda Strait.
Assassination of Giuseppe (Joe the Boss) Masseria, New York City Mafia boss.
Construction of the Empire State Building is completed in New York City.
Heavy hydrogen, later named deuterium, is discovered by American chemist Harold Urey.
Murder of Paul Anlauf and Franz Lenck: Two Berlin police officers are killed by Communists.
Niceto Alcalá-Zamora is elected president of the Spanish Republic.
Norway issues a royal proclamation claiming the uninhabited part of eastern Greenland as Erik the Red's Land.
Paul Doumer is elected president of France.
Pehr Evind Svinhufvud is elected president of Finland.
Pierre Laval forms a government in France.
South Dakota native Ernest Lawrence invents the cyclotron, used to accelerate particles to study nuclear physics.
The Finnish Parliament House opens in Helsinki, Finland.
The Second Encirclement Campaign against Jiangxi Soviet in China is launched by the Kuomintang government, to destroy the Communist forces in Jiangxi Province.
The worst hurricane in British Honduras history kills an estimated 1,500.
Altona Bloody Sunday: In Altona, Germany, a bloody clash with heavy police involvement occurs when Nazi marchers enter a working class area with many communist supporters; 18 are killed.
Amelia Earhart flies from the United States to County Londonderry, Northern Ireland in 14 hours 54 minutes.
German president Hindenburg begins negotiations with Adolf Hitler about the formation of a new government.
Gregor Strasser resigns as the chief of the NSDAP's organizational department in protest against Hitler's "all or nothing" strategy.
Haile Selassie announces an anti-slavery law in Abyssinia.
January 28 incident: Conflict between Japan and China in Shanghai.
The British authorities in India arrest and intern Mahatma Gandhi and Vallabhbhai Patel.
The Kennedy–Thorndike experiment is published, showing that measured time as well as length is affected by motion, in accordance with the theory of special relativity.
The Mäntsälä rebellion occurs in Finland.
The Papen government lifts the ban against the SS and SA in Germany.
The Sydney Harbour Bridge opens in Australia.
The court of Helsinki sentences Vilho Kallio, Ville Saari and Ida Maria Viden to prison for the Tattarisuo mutilation case.
American airship Akron crashes off the coast of New Jersey, killing 73 of its 76 crewmen. It is the worst aviation accident in history up to this date.
Australian aviator Sir Charles Kingsford Smith makes the first commercial flight between Australia and New Zealand.
Japan announces it will leave the League of Nations.
King Kong: The original King Kong film, starring Fay Wray and directed by Merian C. Cooper, debuts in New York City.
Loggers cause a forest fire in the Coast Range of Oregon, later known as the first forest fire of the Tillamook Burn. It is extinguished on September 5, after destroying.
Mohandas Gandhi begins a 3-week hunger strike because of the mistreatment of the lower castes in India.
Reichskonkordat: Vatican state secretary Eugenio Pacelli (later Pope Pius XII) signs an accord with Germany.
The Fujian People's Government is declared in Fujian Province, China.
The U.S. Congress abrogates the United States use of the gold standard, by enacting a joint resolution nullifying the right of creditors to demand payment in gold.
Wilmersdorfer Tennishallen delegates convene in Berlin to protest against the persecution of Jehovah's Witnesses in Nazi Germany.
A gas explosion at Gresford Colliery in Wrexham, north-east Wales, kills 266 miners and rescuers.
American outlaws Bonnie and Clyde are ambushed and killed by police in Bienville Parish, Louisiana.
Austrian Civil War: The Fatherland Front consolidates its power in a series of clashes across the country.
Daniel Salamanca Urey, President of Bolivia, is deposed in a military coup, and replaced by José Luis Tejada Sorzano.
Donald Duck makes his film debut in Walt Disney's Silly Symphony cartoon The Wise Little Hen.
Imam Yahya of Yemen and Ibn Saud of Saudi Arabia conclude a peace treaty.
King Leopold III of Belgium succeeds to the throne, following the death of his father King Albert I.
The 6th Nuremberg Rally is staged by the German Nazi Party.
The Great Hakodate Fire kills at least 2,166 people in southern Hokkaido, Japan.
The International Telecommunication Union, a specialist agency of the League of Nations, is established.
The Wehrmacht swears a personal oath of loyalty to Adolf Hitler.
A Greek monarchy referendum is held by self-proclaimed Regent Georgios Kondylis. Almost 98% of the votes favor restoration of the monarchy, although the referendum's integrity is dubious.
After 11 years in exile, George II returns to Greek soil as King of Greece at Corfu, from London.
An estimated 250 people are killed when a dam bursts near Ovada, Italy.
Italian premier Benito Mussolini and French Foreign Minister Pierre Laval conclude an agreement, in which each power agrees not to oppose the other's colonial claims.
King Prajadhipok (Rama VII) of Siam abdicates the throne; he is succeeded by his 9-year-old-nephew Ananda Mahidol (Rama VIII).
Manuel L. Quezon is elected 2nd President of the Philippines.
Sails from Southampton to Rosyth to be broken up.
Sun Myung Moon, a teenage Presbyterian convert in Korea under Japanese rule, claims to have a revelation from Jesus, telling him to complete his mission from almost 2,000 years ago.
T. E. Lawrence ("Lawrence of Arabia") is involved in a motorcycle accident, near his home in Dorset, England, resulting in his death a few days later.
The Chaco War between Paraguay and Bolivia ends.
The first canned beer is sold in Richmond, Virginia, United States, by Gottfried Krueger Brewing Company.
The world's first regular television program (by Fernsehsender Paul Nipkow) is transmitted from the Funkturm in Berlin, Germany.
The wreckage of the RMS Lusitania is discovered.
A tornado hits Tupelo, Mississippi, United States, killing 216 people and injuring over 700.
Buenaventura Durruti, a major Spanish anarchist, is fatally shot in Madrid, dying the following day.
Construction of Hoover Dam is completed in the United States.
English-born aviator Beryl Markham becomes the first woman to make an east-to-west solo transatlantic flight, from Abingdon-on-Thames, England, to Baleine, Nova Scotia.
Radium E becomes the first radioactive element to be made synthetically.
Reza Shah of Iran issues the Kashf-e hijab which bans all Islamic veils such as the hijab, in addition to many types of male traditional clothing.
Second Italo-Ethiopian War: Battle of Amba Aradam – Italian forces gain a decisive tactical victory, effectively neutralizing the army of the Ethiopian Empire.
Speaking in Rome, Benito Mussolini announces the foundation of the empire, as Italian East Africa is formed from the Italian territories of Eritrea, Ethiopia and Italian Somaliland.
Streptococcous meningitis is successfully treated for the first time with a sulfonamide.
The Anti-Comintern Pact is signed by Germany and Japan.
Anastasio Somoza García becomes President of Nicaragua.
Frank Whittle ground-tests the world's first jet engine designed to power an aircraft, at Rugby, England.
Italy withdraws from the League of Nations.
Nine nations meet in the Nyon Conference, led by the United Kingdom and France, to address international piracy in the Mediterranean.
Roosevelt gives his famous Quarantine Speech in Chicago.
Second Sino-Japanese War: Japanese troops take Shanghai.
Spanish Civil War: Falangist troops take Málaga.
Spanish Civil War: The government of the autonomous Basque Country agrees to surrender to the nationalists.
The last recorded Bali tiger dies.
Wallis Simpson marries the Duke of Windsor, the former Edward VIII, in France.
Éamon de Valera is elected President of the Executive Council (prime minister) of the Irish Free State, by the Dáil (parliament).
Arising from The Munich Agreement, Hungary is "awarded" the Felvidek region of South Slovakia and Ruthenia.
British Royal Navy is ordered to sea.
Fire destroys 214 buildings in Ludza, Latvia.
Konstantin Päts becomes the first President of Estonia.
Poland presents an ultimatum to Lithuania, to establish normal diplomatic relations that were severed over the Vilnius Region.
State-owned railway networks are created by merger, in France (SNCF) and the Netherlands (Nederlandse Spoorwegen – NS).
The Battle of Teruel ends in a Nationalist victory with recapture of the city, a turning point in the Spanish Civil War.
The Mauthausen concentration camp is built in Austria.
The Neuengamme concentration camp opens near Hamburg.
Wrong Way Corrigan takes off from New York, ostensibly heading for California. He lands in Ireland instead.
Lina Medina, a 5-year-old Peruvian girl, gives birth to a baby boy, becoming the youngest confirmed mother in medical history.
Operation Himmler: Nazi German troops posing as Poles stage a series of false flag operations on the border (including the Gleiwitz incident), giving a pretext for the invasion of Poland.
Pioneering U.S. aviator Amelia Earhart is officially declared dead, eighteen months after her disappearance.
Sinks the British battleship at anchor in Scapa Flow (Scotland), with the loss of 833 crew.
The Neuengamme concentration camp becomes autonomous.
The Slovak–Hungarian War begins.
WWII: The first soldier of the British Expeditionary Force is killed: Corporal Thomas Priday triggers a French land mine.
Abbott and Costello make their film debut, in One Night in the Tropics.
In Cambodia, the Khmer Issarak is formed to overthrow the French Army within the country.
Indian nationalist Udham Singh assassinates Sir Michael O'Dwyer at Caxton Hall in London, for which he is hanged on 31 July at HM Prison Pentonville.
The Vought XF4U-1, prototype of the F4U Corsair U.S. fighter later used in WWII, makes its first flight.
The first section of the Pennsylvania Turnpike, the United States' first long-distance controlled-access highway, is opened.
WWII: British submarine is sunk off the coast of Norway.
WWII: Chad is the first French colony to proclaim its support for the Allies.
WWII: Luftwaffe Chief and Generalfeldmarschall Hermann Göring assumes control of most war industries in Germany, in his capacity as Plenipotentiary for the Four Year Plan.

The Holocaust: In Berdychiv (Ukraine), 20–30,000 Jews are shot dead.
The Northern Rhodesian Labour Party holds its first congress in Nkana.
The Willys MB U.S. Army Jeep is first produced.
WWII: Admiral Kichisaburō Nomura begins his duties as Japanese Ambassador to the United States.
WWII: Emperor Haile Selassie of Ethiopia re-enters Addis Ababa, which has been liberated from Italian forces; this date is subsequently commemorated as Liberation Day in the country.
WWII: Finland (as a co-belligerent with Germany) attacks the Soviet Union, starting the Continuation War.
WWII: German troops enter Belgrade.
WWII: In the North Atlantic, Fairey Swordfish aircraft from the carrier cripple the steering of in an aerial torpedo attack.
WWII: Joseph Grew, the U.S. ambassador to Japan, reports to Washington a rumor overheard at a diplomatic reception, concerning a planned surprise attack on Pearl Harbor, Hawaii.
WWII: Siege of Leningrad – German forces begin a siege against the Soviet Union's second-largest city, Leningrad. Stalin orders the Volga Germans deported to Siberia.
Walt Disney's fourth animated film Dumbo is released in the United States.
Washington state's Grand Coulee Dam begins to generate electricity.
WWII: American tanker reaches Malta, as part of the convoy of Operation Pedestal.
WWII: Battle of Christmas Island – Japanese troops occupy Christmas Island without resistance, following a mutiny by British Indian Army troops against their British officers.
WWII: Invasion of Sumatra: Japanese forces of the 38th Division under General Tadayoshi Sano capture Tanjungkarang airfield, which is put to work for air operations against Java.
WWII: Malayan Campaign: The last organized Allied forces leave British Malaya, ending the 54-day campaign, and the Johor–Singapore Causeway is severed.
WWII: Second Battle of El Alamein: British troops go on the offensive against the Axis forces.
WWII: The Holocaust: The systematic deportation of Jews from the Warsaw Ghetto begins.
WWII: The, carrying civilians, Allied soldiers, and Italian prisoners of war, is torpedoed off the coast of West Africa and sinks, killing 1,649 people.
WWII: Tulagi is invaded by Japanese forces in the British Solomon Islands of the South Pacific, as part of Operation Mo.
Gulf Hotel fire: A fire at the Gulf Hotel in Houston, Texas kills 55.
The U.S. Federal Writers' Project ceases operation.
WWII: Battle of Porta: The Royal Italian Army is defeated by the Greek People's Liberation Army.
WWII: Battle of Sidi Bou Zid: In the Tunisia Campaign, German Panzer divisions commanded by Hans-Jürgen von Arnim are victorious over the United States Army.
WWII: Battle of Wau – Australian forces, with United States support, resist a Japanese advance in the New Guinea campaign.
WWII: Battle of the Bismarck Sea – United States and Australian forces sink Japanese convoy ships, then strafe survivors in the water.
WWII: British Royal Navy destroyer is sunk by a mine in the Aegean Sea, with the loss of 119 of the ship's company and 134 troops.
WWII: Greek-Polish athlete and saboteur Jerzy Iwanow-Szajnowicz is executed by the Germans at Kaisariani.
WWII: United States forces enter liberated Naples.
Éamon de Valera, Taoiseach of the Republic of Ireland, makes the speech "The Ireland That We Dreamed Of", commonly called the "comely maidens" speech, in Dublin Castle.
Edward Stettinius, Jr. becomes the last United States Secretary of State of the Roosevelt administration, filling the seat left by Cordell Hull.
In Sweden, Ruben Rausing patents Erik Wallenberg's method of packaging milk in paper, origin of the international company Tetra Pak.
Serial killer Dr Marcel Petiot is apprehended at a Paris Métro station after 7 months on the run.
The Dutch famine ("Hongerwinter") begins, in the occupied northern part of the Netherlands.
The United Nations Monetary and Financial Conference begins at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire, United States.
The United States Forest Service and the Wartime Advertising Council release the first posters featuring Smokey Bear.
WWII: American destroyer escort sinks the sixth Japanese submarine in two weeks. This anti-submarine warfare performance remains unmatched through the 20th century.
WWII: American submarine torpedoes Japanese transports and; 7,998 drown.
WWII: Battle of Kwajalein: American forces land on Kwajalein Atoll and other islands in the Japanese-held Marshall Islands.
WWII: Bombing of Yawata – The United States Army Air Forces conduct the first air raid on the Japanese home islands.
WWII: Fourth Moscow Conference: British Prime Minister Winston Churchill and Soviet Premier Joseph Stalin begin a 9-day conference in Moscow, to discuss the future of Europe.
WWII: Operation Market Garden: Allied airborne landings begin in the Netherlands and Germany.
WWII: Two hundred Communist prisoners are shot by the Germans at Kaisariani, Athens, Greece, in reprisal for the killing of General Franz Krech by Partisans at Molaoi.
Egyptian premier Ahmad Mahir Pasha is assassinated in Parliament after declaring war on Germany and Japan.
George Albert Smith becomes president of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
The American-led Allied Occupation of Japan effectively begins with General Douglas MacArthur's arrival at Atsugi Air Base.
The Iranian government demands that all Soviet and British troops leave the country.
The Tudeh party starts a bloodless coup, and will form Azerbaijan within days. Soviet troops prevent Iranian troops from getting involved.
WWII: German troopship is sunk by the Soviet submarine S-13; 3,608 drown.
WWII: Kobe, Japan is fire-bombed by 331 B-29 bombers, killing over 8,000 people.
Women's suffrage: Women are allowed to vote in the French Legislative Election for the first time.
A two-day violent tornado outbreak occurs across the Central United States, with at least 15 significant tornadoes killing four people and injuring 42 others.
Bell's chief test pilot, Jack Woolams, dies in a plane crash while flying the P-39 "Cobra I" over Lake Ontario preparing for an air race the following day.
In Indonesia, Sukarno incites his supporters to fight Dutch colonial occupation.
In a speech at Westminster College, in Fulton, Missouri, Winston Churchill talks about the Iron Curtain.
King David Hotel bombing: The Irgun bombs the King David Hotel (headquarters of the British civil and military administration) in Jerusalem, killing 90.
Miguel Alemán Valdés takes office as President of Mexico.
Naperville train disaster: The Chicago, Burlington & Quincy's Exposition Flyer crashes at speed into the rear of the Advance Flyer at Loomis Street in Naperville, Illinois; 45 are killed.
Operation Black Tulip, the expulsion of Germans from the Netherlands, begins in Amsterdam.
The Canadian schooner Bluenose founders on a Haitian reef.
The Gold Coast has an African majority in its parliament.
The International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) (World Bank) begins operations.
The Noakhali riots in Bengal begin: several hundred Hindus are massacred by Muslims.
The first general election ever in Vietnam is held.
A rebellion against French rule erupts in Madagascar.
Alcide de Gasperi forms a new government in Italy, the first postwar Italian government not to include members of the Italian Communist Party.
Elizabeth Short, an aspiring actress nicknamed the "Black Dahlia", is found brutally murdered in a vacant lot in Los Angeles; the mysterious case is never solved.
Indonesian airline Garuda Indonesia is established.
Pakistan and Yemen join the United Nations.
The Cold War begins: The Truman Doctrine is proclaimed, to help stem the spread of Communism.
The Estado Novo in Portugal orders 11 military officers and 19 university professors, who are accused of revolutionary activity, to resign.
The Karlslust dance hall fire in Berlin, Germany, kills over 80 people.
The first Azad Kashmir Government is established within Pakistan, headed by Sardar Muhammad Ibrahim Khan as its first President supported by the government of Pakistan.
The movie Miracle on 34th Street, a Christmastime classic, is first shown in theaters.
The ship Exodus leaves France for Palestine, with 4,500 Jewish Holocaust survivor refugees on board.
Alger Hiss appears before the HUAC, to deny the allegations of Whittaker Chambers.
Brandeis University is formally founded in Massachusetts.
Daniel François Malan defeats Jan Smuts and becomes Prime Minister of South Africa, which starts the era of apartheid.
In Venezuela, president Rómulo Gallegos is ousted by a military junta.
Malayan Emergency: Batang Kali massacre: Scots Guards shoot 24 Chinese villagers in Malaya.
Robert Schuman becomes Prime Minister of France.
The Danube Commission is created by the Belgrade Convention.
The RAND Corporation is established, as an independent nonprofit policy research and analysis institution, in the United States.
The city of Rabwah is established in Pakistan.
The first of the Ben Yehuda Street bombings in Jerusalem kills between 49 and 58 civilians and injures between 140 and 200.
United Airlines Flight 624, a Douglas DC-6, crashes near Mount Carmel, Pennsylvania, killing 43 and injuring 84 people on board.
A typhoon strikes a fishing fleet off Korea, killing several thousand.
Dock workers strike in the United Kingdom.
László Rajk, ex-foreign minister of Hungary, is sentenced to death.
Nereid, a moon of Neptune, is discovered by Gerard Kuiper.
Pamir is the last commercial sailing ship to round Cape Horn, under sail alone.
The B-50 Superfortress Lucky Lady II (under Captain James Gallagher) lands in Fort Worth, Texas, United States, after completing the first non-stop around-the-world airplane flight.
The Basketball Association of America and the National Basketball League finalize the merger that will create the National Basketball Association.
The German Democratic Republic (East Germany) is officially established.
The Indian Constituent Assembly adopts India's constitution.
The North Atlantic Treaty Organization is established.
The Tokyo Stock Exchange resumes operations, after a four-year shutdown.
The cornerstone of the Headquarters of the United Nations on Manhattan is laid.
A phenomenal winter storm ravages the northeastern United States, brings 30–50 inches of snow and temperatures below zero, and kills 323 people.
Air Battle of South Korea: After a month-long campaign, the majority of North Korea's People's Air Force is destroyed by anti-communist forces.
British submarine collides with Swedish oil tanker Divina in the Thames Estuary and sinks; 64 die.
Chiang Kai-shek is re-elected as president of the Republic of China.
Cunard liner Aquitania arrives at the scrapyard in Faslane at the end of a 36-year career, the longest of any in the 20th Century.
Indonesia is admitted to the United Nations.
Jordan formally annexes the West Bank.
Korean War: Hill 303 massacre – 39 U.S. soldiers are executed after being captured in battle by North Korea.
Mauna Loa in Hawaii starts erupting.
The Belgian government collapses, after the March 12 referendum.
The Goyang Geumjeong Cave massacre begins in South Korea.
The International Police Association (IPA) – the largest police organization in the world – is formed.
The Jayuya Uprising is started by Puerto Rican Nationalists against the United States-supported government.
The Kefauver Committee hearings into U.S. organized crime begin.
The Korean War begins: Troops and T-34 tanks of the North Korean People's Army cross the 38th parallel into South Korea.
A military coup occurs in Bolivia.
A state of emergency is declared in Egypt, due to increasing riots.
Charlotte Whitton becomes mayor of Ottawa and Canada's first woman mayor of a major city.
King Farouk I of Egypt declares himself king of the Sudan, with no international recognition or support.
King Leopold III of Belgium abdicates in favour of his son Baudouin, who on July 17 takes the oath as king of Belgium.
Korean War: Third Battle of Seoul – Chinese and North Korean forces capture Seoul for the second time.
The National Ballet of Canada performs for the first time in Eaton Auditorium, Toronto.
The Sri Lanka Freedom Party is founded by S. W. R. D. Bandaranaike.
The United Nations General Assembly declares that China is an aggressor in the Korean War, in United Nations General Assembly Resolution 498.
The first birch bark manuscript is discovered in Novgorod.
The state of war between the United States and Germany is officially ended.
The trial of Julius and Ethel Rosenberg for conspiracy to commit espionage begins in the United States.
UNIVAC I is dedicated by the U.S. Census Bureau.
Winter of Terror: Avalanches in the Alps kill 240 and bury 45,000 for a time, in Switzerland, Austria and Italy.
An accident causing 13 deaths results in closure of the Grenzlandring as an auto race circuit in Wegberg, Germany.
Ann Davison becomes the first woman to single-handedly sail the Atlantic Ocean.
Black Saturday in Egypt: Rioters burn Cairo's central business district, targeting British and upper-class Egyptian businesses.
Greece and Turkey join the North Atlantic Treaty Organization.
Japan joins the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
The Pan-Malayan Labour Party is founded in Malaya, as a union of statewide labour parties.
The United Nations cedes Eritrea to Ethiopia.
U.S. lieutenant colonels Joseph O. Fletcher and William P. Benedict land a plane at the geographic North Pole.
A tornado outbreak tears through Port Huron, Michigan and Sarnia, Ontario, leaving eight people dead and 123 people injured.
Batepá massacre: Hundreds of native creoles, known as forros, are massacred in São Tomé, by the colonial administration and Portuguese landowners.
First Indochina War: Battle of Dien Bien Phu – French paratroopers consolidate their position at Điện Biên Phủ.
Hussein is crowned King of Jordan.
Italian general election: the Christian Democracy party wins a plurality in both legislative houses.
Lari Massacre in Kenya: Mau Mau rebels kill up to 150 Kikuyu natives.
Nikita Khrushchev becomes head of the Soviet Central Committee.
Soviet prime minister Georgi Malenkov announces that the Soviet Union has a hydrogen bomb.
The Asian Socialist Conference opens in Rangoon, Burma.
The Mutual Defense Treaty Between the United States and the Republic of Korea is concluded in Washington, D.C.
The Thieves World, which has been transformed into the Russian mafia, are freed from prisons by the Malenkov regime, ending the Bitch Wars.
The first ascent of Nanga Parbat in the Pakistan Himalayas, the world's ninth highest mountain, is made by Austrian climber Hermann Buhl alone on a German–Austrian expedition.
The last prisoners are repatriated from Devil's Island to France.
U.S. President Dwight D. Eisenhower delivers his Atoms for Peace address, to the United Nations General Assembly.
A Royal Canadian Air Force Canadair Harvard collides with a Trans-Canada Air Lines Canadair North Star over Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan, killing 37 people.
Beginning of the Kengir uprising in the Gulag.
First Indochina War: Viet Minh troops successfully ambush the armoured French column 'G.M. 42' in the Battle of Chu Dreh Pass in the Central Highlands. It is the last battle of the war.
Landslides caused by heavy rains hit Salerno, Italy, killing about 300.
Lt. Col. Gamal Abdel Nasser becomes premier of Egypt.
SEATO is established in Bangkok, Thailand.
The Castle Romeo nuclear test explosion is executed at Bikini Atoll, in the Marshall Islands.
The Cochabamba–Santa Cruz highway connecting western and eastern Bolivia is inaugurated.
The Italian broadcaster RAI officially begins transmitting.
The US-based National Negro Network is established, with 46 member radio stations.
U.S. President Dwight D. Eisenhower dedicates the USMC War Memorial (Iwo Jima Memorial), at the Arlington National Cemetery.
Commercial television starts in the United Kingdom with the Independent Television Authority's first ITV franchises beginning broadcasting in London, ending the BBC monopoly.
Eight Communist Bloc countries, including the Soviet Union, sign a mutual defence treaty in Warsaw, Poland, that is called the Warsaw Pact.
Geneva Summit between the United States, Soviet Union, United Kingdom and France.
Hundreds of people are killed in anti-French rioting in Morocco and Algeria.
In Chicago's Democratic primary, Mayor Martin H. Kennelly loses to the head of the Cook County Democratic Party, Richard J. Daley, 364,839 to 264,077.
José Ramón Guizado becomes president of Panama.
The Freedom Charter of the anti-apartheid South African Congress Alliance is adopted, at a Congress of the People in Kliptown.
The International Federation of Blood Donor Organizations is founded in Luxembourg.
The Salk polio vaccine, having passed large-scale trials earlier in the United States, receives full approval by the Food and Drug Administration.
Vladimir Nabokov's controversial novel Lolita is published in Paris, by Olympia Press.
West Germany becomes a sovereign country, recognized by Western countries such as France, the United Kingdom, Canada and the United States.
A laboratory experiment involving scrap thorium at Sylvania Electric Products in Bayside, New York, results in an explosion.
British spies Guy Burgess and Donald Maclean resurface in the Soviet Union, after being missing for 5 years.
In Yugoslavia, former prime minister Milovan Đilas is arrested after he criticizes Josip Broz Tito.
Morocco, Sudan and Tunisia join the United Nations.
Spain relinquishes its protectorate in Morocco.
The Anglo-Egyptian Condominium ends in Sudan after 57 years.
The Flag of the United States Army is formally dedicated.
The Italian ocean liner sinks after colliding with the Swedish ship SS Stockholm in heavy fog south of Nantucket island, killing 51.
The constitutional union between Indonesia and the Netherlands is dissolved.
Vyacheslav Molotov resigns as foreign minister of the Soviet Union; he later becomes ambassador to Mongolia.
West Germany bans the Communist Party of Germany.
All 326,000 Dutch nationals are expelled from Indonesia.
Andrei Gromyko becomes foreign minister of the Soviet Union.
Asghar Khan becomes the first native Commander-in-Chief of the Pakistan Air Force and the world's youngest Air Vice Marshal at 36 years old.
Celâl Bayar is re-elected president of Turkey.
Cuban Revolution: Fulgencio Batista’s forces bomb anti-government riots in Cienfuegos.
Egypt reopens the Suez Canal to all shipping.
Harold Macmillan becomes Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
Hurricane Audrey demolishes Cameron, Louisiana, U.S., killing 400 people.
Israel withdraws from the Sinai Peninsula.
May 24 incident: Anti-American riots erupt in Taipei, Taiwan.
The Africanized bee is accidentally released in Brazil.
The Saarland joins West Germany.
A Pan American World Airways Boeing 707 makes its first transatlantic flight.
A message from U.S. President Dwight D. Eisenhower is broadcast from the SCORE satellite.
In Cuba, Castro's revolutionary army begins its attacks on Havana.
Notting Hill race riots: Riots occur between blacks and whites in Notting Hill, London.
The European Economic Community (EEC) comes into being.
The U.S.S.R. performs a nuclear test at Novaya Zemlya.
The United States launches the Vanguard 1 satellite.
The first Thor-Able rocket is launched, carrying Pioneer 0, from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station Space Launch Complex 17. The launch fails due to a first stage malfunction.
The iron barque Omega of Callao, Peru, the world's last full-rigged ship trading under sail alone, sinks on passage carrying guano from the Pachacamac Islands for Huacho.
U.S. President Dwight D. Eisenhower becomes the first American elected official to appear on color television.
A new government of the State of Singapore is sworn in by Sir William Goode. Two former ministers are re-elected to the Legislative Assembly.
Cuba: Fulgencio Batista flees Havana when the forces of Fidel Castro advance.
Cyprus gains independence.
Danish passenger/cargo ship, returning to Copenhagen after its maiden voyage to Greenland, strikes an iceberg and sinks off the Greenland coast with the loss of all 95 on board.
First appearance of Astérix the Gaul, in a French comic magazine.
Soviet Union leader Nikita Khrushchev meets Mao Zedong in Beijing.
The Declaration of the Rights of the Child is adopted by the United Nations.
The Inter-American Development Bank (IADB) is established.
The Soviet government recognizes the new Castro government of Cuba.
The Workers' Stadium sports venue in Beijing (China) is officially opened.
The first skull of Australopithecus is discovered by Louis Leakey and his wife Mary in the Olduvai Gorge of Tanzania.
Vanguard 2, the first weather satellite, is launched to measure cloud cover for the United States Navy.
A joint Swiss and Austrian expedition makes the first ascent of the Asian mountain Dhaulagiri, the world's 7th highest.
Cameroon becomes independent from France.
In Huntsville, Alabama, U.S. President Dwight D. Eisenhower formally dedicates the Marshall Space Flight Center.
In the Soviet Union.
King Bhumibol Adulyadej of Thailand arrives in Washington, D.C. for a 4-day royal visit to the U.S.
New Zealand's first television station begins broadcasting, in the city of Auckland.
Nigeria becomes independent from the United Kingdom, and Nnamdi Azikiwe becomes its first native-born Governor General.
Prime Minister of the United Kingdom Harold Macmillan makes the Wind of Change speech to the South African Parliament in Cape Town.
The U-2 incident: Several Soviet surface-to-air missiles shoot down an American Lockheed U-2 spy plane. Its pilot, Francis Gary Powers of the Central Intelligence Agency, is captured.
The United Nations Security Council decides to send troops to Katanga to oversee the withdrawal of Belgian troops.
The admission of Mauritania to the United Nations is vetoed by the Soviet Union.
Upper Volta (modern-day Burkina Faso) becomes independent from France.
A patent for the body electrode invented by Richard M. Berman and Bernard Schwartz is applied for.
Albania–Soviet relations: The Soviet Union severs diplomatic relations with Albania.
Cemal Gürsel becomes the fourth president of Turkey (his former title is head of state and government; he is elected as president by constitutional referendum).
Fidel Castro announces that the Bay of Pigs Invasion has been defeated.
Monetary reform in the Soviet Union.
Rebellion of the Pilots: A military uprising overthrows the Trujillo regime in the Dominican Republic.
Soviet submarine K-19 suffers a reactor leak in the North Atlantic.
Soviet submarine S-80 sinks in the Barents Sea, killing all 68 crew.
The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) is formed to replace the Organisation for European Economic Co-operation (OEEC).
The Single Convention on Narcotic Drugs is signed at New York.
The USSR launches Venera 1 towards Venus.
Vostok 2: Soviet cosmonaut Gherman Titov becomes the second human to orbit the Earth, and the first to be in outer space for more than one day.
Alcatraz escape attempt: Frank Morris, John Anglin and Clarence Anglin escape from the Alcatraz Island prison in the United States; it is never confirmed that they make it ashore.
An agreement is signed between Britain and France, to develop the Concorde supersonic airliner.
Captured American spy pilot Francis Gary Powers is exchanged for captured Soviet spy Rudolf Abel, in Berlin.
OAS leader Edmond Jouhaud is sentenced to death in France.
The North Yemen Civil War erupts.
The Organisation armée secrète (OAS, a right-wing paramilitary organization opposed to Algerian independence) bombs the French Foreign Ministry.
The Rolling Stones make their debut at London's Marquee Club, opening for Long John Baldry.
The Scandinavian States of the Nordic Council sign the Helsinki Convention on Nordic Co-operation.
Western Samoa becomes independent from New Zealand.
Yi–Ta incident: At least 60,000 Chinese citizens migrate from the People's Republic of China to the Soviet Union, predominantly (but not exclusively) ethnic Kazakhs.
American test pilot Joe Walker, flying the X-15, reaches an altitude of 65.8 miles, making it a sub-orbital spaceflight by recognized international standards.
Berthold Seliger launches near Cuxhaven a 3-stage rocket with a maximum flight altitude of more than (the only sounding rocket developed in Germany).
First games played in the Bundesliga, the primary professional Association football league in West Germany, replacing the Oberliga.
Hurricane Flora, one of the worst Atlantic storms in history, hits Hispaniola and Cuba, killing nearly 7,000 people.
Indigenous Australians are legally allowed to drink alcohol in New South Wales.
Malaysia is formed through the merging of the Federation of Malaya and the British crown colony of Singapore, North Borneo (renamed Sabah) and Sarawak.
Malcolm X makes a historic speech in Detroit, Michigan ("Message to the Grass Roots").
The 5.6 Marj earthquake affects northern Libya with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe), causing 290–375 deaths and 375–500 injuries.
The Institute of Mental Health (Belgrade) is established.
The Organisation of African Unity is established in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.
The car manufacturing firm Lamborghini is founded in Italy.
Vostok 6 carries Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova, the first woman into space.
A U.S. Air Force jet training aircraft that strays into East Germany is shot down by Soviet fighters near Erfurt; all three crewmen are killed.
A minor criticality accident takes place at a United Nuclear Corporation Fuels recovery plant in Wood River Junction, Rhode Island, United States, causing the death of one worker.
At the 36th Academy Awards ceremony, Sidney Poitier becomes the first African-American to win an Academy Award in the category Best Actor in a Leading Role in Lilies of the Field.
Che Guevara addresses the United Nations General Assembly. A bazooka attack is launched at the Headquarters of the United Nations in New York City.
Indian Hungry generation poets, including Malay Roy Choudhury, are arrested on charges of conspiracy against the state and obscenity in literature.
Malawi receives its independence from the United Kingdom.
Mariner program: Mariner 3 spacecraft is launched from Cape Kennedy but fails.
South Korean President Park Chung Hee declares martial law in Seoul, after 10,000 student demonstrators overpower police.
South Korean President Park Chung Hee reshuffles his Cabinet, after a series of student demonstrations against his efforts to restore diplomatic and trade relations with Japan.
The Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland is dissolved.
The Mozambican War of Independence is launched by FRELIMO.
Vietnam War: In a coup, General Nguyễn Khánh replaces Dương Văn Minh as South Vietnam's chief of state and establishes a new constitution, drafted partly by the U.S. Embassy.
Kakanj mine disaster: A mining accident in Kakanj, Bosnia and Herzegovina, results in 128 deaths.
Martial law is announced in Rhodesia. The United Nations General Assembly accepts British intent to use force against Rhodesia if necessary by a vote of 82–9.
Martin Luther King Jr. and 25,000 civil rights activists successfully end the 4-day march from Selma, Alabama, to the capitol in Montgomery.
Muhammad Ali knocks out Sonny Liston in the first round of their championship rematch with the "Phantom Punch" at the Central Maine Civic Center in Lewiston.
NASA launches Gemini 5 (Gordon Cooper, Pete Conrad) on the first 1-week space flight, as well as the first test of fuel cells for electrical power on such a mission.
The Canadian satellite Alouette 2 is launched.
The First Minister of Northern Ireland and the Taoiseach of the Republic of Ireland meet for the first time in 43 years.
The Gambia becomes independent from the United Kingdom.
The Indonesian government outlaws the Communist Party of Indonesia.
The West German parliament extends the statute of limitations on Nazi war crimes.
U.S. spacecraft Mariner 4 flies by Mars, becoming the first spacecraft to return images from the Red Planet.
Venera program: The Soviet Union launches the Venera 3 space probe from Baikonur, Kazakhstan toward Venus.
A coup led by the police and military of Ghana raises the National Liberation Council to power while president Kwame Nkrumah is abroad.
Aberfan disaster in South Wales (U.K.): 144 are killed by a collapsing coal spoil tip.
An Air France personnel strike begins.
Hurricane Inez strikes Hispaniola, leaving thousands dead and tens of thousands homeless in the Dominican Republic and Haiti.
In Rhodesia, security forces kill seven ZANLA men in combat; Chimurenga, the ZANU rebellion, begins.
In a coup, Colonel Jean-Bédel Bokassa takes over as military ruler of the Central African Republic, ousting President David Dacko.
Loss of MV Darlwyne: a pleasure cruiser disappears off the Cornwall coast of England with the loss of all 31 aboard.
Luna 10 is the first manmade object to enter lunar orbit.
NASA spacecraft Gemini 8 (David Scott, Neil Armstrong) conducts the first docking in space, with an Agena target vehicle.
TABSO Flight 101, from Sofia, Bulgaria, crashes near Bratislava, Czechoslovakia, killing all 82 people on board.
The United Kingdom ceases all trade with Rhodesia.
Vietnam War: Bình Hòa massacre.
Zambia threatens to leave the Commonwealth of Nations because of British peace overtures to Rhodesia.
Alexei Kosygin arrives in the UK for an 8-day visit. He meets The Queen on February 9.
Guerrilla leader Che Guevara and his men are captured in Bolivia; they are executed the following day.
Israel declares the annexation of East Jerusalem.
Major floods hit Lisbon, Portugal, killing 462.
Moscow's 537 m tall TV tower is finished.
Six-Day War (approach): Israeli fighters shoot down 7 Syrian MIG-21s.
Solicitor General Thurgood Marshall is nominated as the first African American justice of the United States Supreme Court.
Supersonic airliner Concorde is unveiled in Toulouse, France.
The Spring Mobilization Conference, a gathering of 700 antiwar activists is held in Washington D.C. to chart the future moves for the U.S. antiwar movement.
The first of its many UFO sightings is made at Pudasjärvi, Finland.
The first phase of the Cambodian Civil War begins between the Kingdom of Cambodia and the Khmer Rouge.
Vietnam War: United States Marine Corps and Army of the Republic of Vietnam troops launch Operation Deckhouse Five in the Mekong Delta.
West Germany receives 36 East German prisoners it has "purchased" through the border posts of Herleshausen and Wartha.
Austin Currie, Member of the Parliament of Northern Ireland, along with others, squats in a house in Caledon to protest discrimination in housing allocations.
British racing driver Jim Clark is killed in a Formula 2 race at Hockenheim.
Crown Prince Harald of Norway marries Sonja Haraldsen, the commoner he has dated for 9 years.
French submarine Minerve sinks in the Mediterranean Sea, killing 52.
Japan's biggest heist, the never-solved "300 million yen robbery", occurs in Tokyo.
May 68: Student protestors begin battling with police on the streets of Paris.
Radical feminist Valerie Solanas shoots Andy Warhol at his New York City studio, The Factory; he survives after a 5-hour operation.
The I'm Backing Britain campaign starts spontaneously.
The Vienna Convention on Road Signs and Signals is signed and ratified.
The first Rotaract club is chartered in North Charlotte, North Carolina.
The magnitude () 7.6 Casiguran earthquake affects the Aurora province in the Philippines with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent), killing at least 207 and injuring 261.
The semiconductor company Intel is founded in what becomes known as the Silicon Valley of California.
Vietnam War: Hà My massacre.
Vietnam War: The Tet Offensive comes to an end in South Vietnam.
An annular solar eclipse is visible in Pacific Ocean and South America, and is the 41st solar eclipse of Solar Saros 134.
Apollo program: The Apollo 12 spacecraft splashes down safely in the Pacific Ocean, ending the second crewed mission to the Moon.
Charles de Gaulle steps down as president of France after suffering defeat in a referendum the day before.
Experimental research showing that protons were composed of smaller particles, the first evidence of quarks, is published.
Pope Paul VI arrives in Entebbe, Uganda for the first visit by a reigning Pope to Africa.
Pope Paul VI increases the number of Roman Catholic cardinals by one-third, from 101 to 134.
Pope Paul VI issues Mysterii Paschalis, a motu proprio, deleting many names from the Roman calendar of saints (including Valentine, who was celebrated on this day).
RFC series begins with Network Working Group RFC 1 on ARPANET host software.
The Government of Spain hands over Ifni to Morocco.
The Stonewall riots, a milestone in the modern gay rights movement in the United States, began in New York City.
The Woodstock Festival is held near White Lake, New York, featuring some of the top rock musicians of the era.
A coup in Argentina brings a new junta of service chiefs; on June 18, Roberto M. Levingston becomes President.
An Egyptian delegation leaves for Moscow to ask for economic and military aid.
An assassination attempt against King Hussein of Jordan precipitates the country's Black September crisis.
Chilean army commander René Schneider is shot in Santiago; the government declares a state of emergency. Schneider dies October 25.
Guinea recognizes the German Democratic Republic.
Multi-business conglomerate Virgin Group is founded as a discount mail-order record retailer by Richard Branson in the UK.
Palestinian armed forces reinforce guerillas in Irbidi, Jordan.
The 7.1 Tonghai earthquake shakes Tonghai County, Yunnan province, China, with a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme). Between 10,000 and 14,621 are killed and 30,000 injured.
The Aswan High Dam in Egypt is completed.
The Expo '70 World's Fair opens in Suita, Osaka, Japan.
The Khmer Republic is proclaimed in Cambodia, escalating the Cambodian Civil War between the government and the Khmer Rouge.
The World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is founded.
A civilian government takes power in Greece.
A coup attempt is exposed and foiled in Egypt.
A fire in a mental hospital in Burghölzli, Switzerland kills 28 people.
Decimal Day: The United Kingdom and Ireland both switch to decimal currency (see also decimalisation).
Hastings Banda is proclaimed President for Life of Malawi.
Japanese Emperor Hirohito travels abroad.
Norway begins oil production in the North Sea.
Texas Stadium opens in Irving, Texas. In the inaugural game, the host Dallas Cowboys defeat the New England Patriots 44–21.
The United Kingdom lifts all restrictions on gold ownership.
U.S. department store chain J. C. Penney debuts its trademark Helvetica wordmark which has been used ever since.
An Alitalia DC-8 crashes west of Palermo, Sicily; 115 die.
An avalanche on Mount Fuji in Japan kills 19 climbers.
At least 24 people have been killed by elephants crazed by heat and drought in separate incidents in the Chandka Forest of India, according to news agency reports.
Iraq nationalizes the Iraq Petroleum Company.
Japan Airlines Flight 471 crashes outside New Delhi airport, killing 82 of 87 occupants.
King Birendra succeeds his father as King of Nepal.
Kurt Waldheim becomes Secretary-General of the United Nations.
The Troubles, Northern Ireland.
U.S. President Richard Nixon makes an unprecedented 8-day visit to the People's Republic of China and meets with Mao Zedong.
Vietnam War: Vietnamization – The United States Army turns over the massive Long Binh military base to South Vietnam.
A British government White Paper on Northern Ireland proposes the re-establishment of an Assembly elected by proportional representation, with a possible All-Ireland council.
Elections are held for the Northern Ireland Assembly, which will lead to power-sharing between unionists and nationalists in Northern Ireland for the first time.
Henri Pescarolo and co-driver Gérard Larrousse (both France) win the 24 Hours of Le Mans in the Equipe Matra MS670B.
Pioneer program: Pioneer 10 sends back the first close-up images of Jupiter.
South Korean politician Kim Dae-jung is kidnapped in Tokyo by the KCIA.
The Congress of the United States overrides President Richard Nixon's veto of the War Powers Resolution, which limits presidential power to wage war without congressional approval.
The Data Act (Sw. Datalagen) − the world's first national data protection law − is enacted in Sweden.
The Soviet Mars 5 space probe is launched.
The United Kingdom, the Republic of Ireland, and Denmark enter the European Economic Community, which later becomes the European Union.
The United States Senate votes 92–3 to confirm Gerald Ford as Vice President of the United States.
Varig Flight 820 crashes near Orly, France; 123 people are killed.
A group of peasant women in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand, India, use their bodies to surround trees to prevent loggers from felling them, giving rise to the Chipko movement.
Bülent Ecevit of CHP forms the new government of Turkey.
Guillaume Affair: exposure of an East German spy Günter Guillaume within the West German government, leading to the resignation of West German Chancellor Willy Brandt.
Helmut Schmidt becomes the new Chancellor of West Germany.
Japanese Red Army members seize the French Embassy in The Hague, Netherlands.
Lufthansa Flight 540 crashes in Nairobi, Kenya, due to a mechanical failure, killing 59 of its 157 occupants.
The British election ended in a hung parliament after the Jeremy Thorpe-led Liberal Party achieves its biggest vote.
The Greek military junta is replaced by a civilian government, the metapolitefsi.
The Paris summit, reuniting the European Communities' heads of state and government, commences.
The World Tourism Organization (WTO) is established.
Fifteen West African countries sign the Treaty of Lagos, creating the Economic Community of West African States.
In New Zealand, Māori leader Whina Cooper leads a march of 5,000 people, in support of Maori claims to their land.
São Tomé and Príncipe declare independence from Portugal.
Taman Mini Indonesia Indah opens to the public in Jakarta, Indonesia.
The "Group of 6" industrialized nations is formed and holds its 1st summit at the Château de Rambouillet in France.
The 2 June Movement kidnaps West German politician Peter Lorenz. He is released on March 4 after most of the kidnappers' demands are met.
The Banqiao Dam, in China's Henan Province, fails after Typhoon Nina; over 200,000 people perish.
The term of Tuanku Al-Mutassimu Billahi Muhibbudin Sultan Abdul Halim Al-Muadzam Shah ibni Almarhum Sultan Badlishah, as the 5th Yang di-Pertuan Agong of Malaysia, ends.
Watergate scandal (United States): John N. Mitchell, H. R. Haldeman and John Ehrlichman are found guilty of the Watergate cover-up.
West Ham United win the FA Cup at Wembley, beating Fulham 2–0 in the final.
Wreck of is found in the Kea Channel by Jacques Cousteau.
Chairman of the Chinese Communist Party Mao Zedong dies in Beijing after a series of heart attacks.
General Murtala Mohammed of Nigeria is assassinated in a military coup.
Neville Wran becomes Premier of New South Wales.
North Vietnam dissolves the Provisional Government of South Vietnam and unites the two countries to form the Socialist Republic of Vietnam.
Sagarmatha National Park in Nepal is created.
The 8.0 Moro Gulf earthquake hits off the coast of Mindanao, Philippines, triggering a destructive tsunami, killing between 5,000 and 8,000 people and leaving more than 90,000 homeless.
The Double Six Crash, a plane crash in Kota Kinabalu, Malaysia, kills everyone on board, including Sabahan Chief Minister Tun Fuad Stephens.
The International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights enters into force.
The clock of "Big Ben" at the Palace of Westminster in London suffers internal damage and requires frequent repairs. The clock is stopped at times on 26 of the next 275 days.
Thorbjörn Fälldin replaces Olof Palme as Prime Minister of Sweden.
Transkei gains "independence" from South Africa.
Two coal mine explosions claim 26 lives at the Blue Diamond Coal Co. Scotia Mine, in Letcher County, Kentucky.
U.S. President Gerald Ford defeats challenger Ronald Reagan in 3 Republican presidential primaries: Kentucky, Tennessee and Oregon.
A federal court in Stuttgart, West Germany, sentences Red Army Faction members Andreas Baader, Gudrun Ensslin, and Jan-Carl Raspe to life imprisonment.
Prime Minister Indira Gandhi of India calls for fresh elections to the Lok Sabha, and releases all political prisoners.
The Centenary Test between Australia and England begins at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
The Libyan–Egyptian War, sparked by a Libyan raid on Sallum, begins.
The Likud Party, led by Menachem Begin, wins the national elections in Israel.
The Porsche 928 debuts at the Geneva Motor Show.
The worst storm in Athens' modern history causes havoc across the Greek capital and kills 38 people.
Three bombs explode in Moscow within 37 minutes, killing seven. The bombings are attributed to an Armenian separatist group.
Three members of the rock band Lynyrd Skynyrd die in a charter plane crash outside Gillsburg, Mississippi, three days after the release of their fifth studio album Street Survivors.
Óscar Romero, an outspoken opponent of violence, becomes Archbishop of San Salvador, El Salvador.
Air India Flight 855, a Boeing 747 passenger jet, crashes off the coast of Bombay, killing 213.
Egyptian President Anwar Sadat and Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin win the Nobel Peace Prize for their progress toward achieving a Middle East accord.
Egyptian raid on Larnaca International Airport: Egyptian Special Forces attempt to rescue several hostages in Larnaca, Cyprus; 20 Egyptian commandos are injured or killed.
Ethiopia begins a massive offensive in Eritrea.
Film director Roman Polanski skips bail in the United States and flees to France, after pleading guilty to charges of engaging in sex with a 13-year-old girl.
French Foreign Legion paratroopers land in Kolwezi, Zaire, to rescue Europeans in the middle of a civil war.
Operation Litani: Israeli forces invade Lebanon.
P.W. Botha succeeds John Vorster as Prime Minister of South Africa.
Pope John Paul I dies after only 33 days as the Roman Catholic Pontiff.
Pope Paul VI dies at Castel Gandolfo.
The 50th Academy Awards are held at the Dorothy Chandler Pavilion in Los Angeles, with Annie Hall winning Best Picture.
Two British commercial divers, Michael Ward and Tony Prangley, die of hypothermia and drowning in the East Shetland Basin after their diving bell plunges to the seabed at a depth of over.
Federal Reserve System changes from an interest rate target policy to a money supply target policy.
Geylang Bahru family murders: Four children, aged five to ten, are brutally killed in Geylang Bahru, Singapore.
In China, a Hawker Siddeley Trident crashes into a factory near Beijing, killing 31 people on the ground and injuring 200.
Indianapolis 500: Rick Mears wins the race for the first time, and car owner Roger Penske for the second time.
Nicaraguan president General Anastasio Somoza Debayle resigns and flees to Miami.
Raymond Washington, co-founder of the Crips, one of the largest, most notorious gangs in the United States, is killed in a drive-by shooting in Los Angeles.
Saint Vincent and the Grenadines gains independence from the UK.
South Africa grants independence to the "homeland" of Venda (not recognised outside South Africa).
The People's Republic of China invades northern Vietnam, launching the Sino-Vietnamese War.
The Permanent Peoples' Tribunal, an international opinion tribunal, is founded in Bologna at the initiative of Senator Lelio Basso.
The Wall, a rock opera concept album by Pink Floyd, is first released.
Abolhassan Banisadr is sworn in as the first President of Iran after winning the January 25 presidential election.
Bülent Ulusu, ex admiral, forms the new government of Turkey.
John Frum supporters in Vanuatu storm government offices on the island of Tanna. Vanuatu government troops land the next day and drive them away.
M-19 guerrillas begin the Dominican embassy siege in Colombia, holding 60 people hostage, including 14 ambassadors.
The Dominican embassy siege in Colombia ends with all remaining hostages released after the guerrillas are allowed to escape to Cuba.
The Gang of Four trial begins in China.
The London Gold Fixing hits its highest price ever of $843 per troy ounce.
The Sumpul River massacre occurs in Chalatenango, El Salvador.
The most recent atmospheric nuclear weapons test to date was conducted by China.
The, the ship housing pirate radio station Radio Caroline, sinks off the English coast.
Vigdís Finnbogadóttir becomes the 4th President of Iceland, the world's first democratically directly elected female president.
Vigdís Finnbogadóttir is elected President of Iceland, making her the first woman democratically elected as head of state.
A bomb explodes at the United States Ramstein Air Base in West Germany, injuring 20 people.
A funeral service is held in West Germany for Nazi Grand Admiral Karl Doenitz following his death on December 24.
Donkey Kong is released, marking the first Donkey Kong and Mario smash hit arcade game developed by Nintendo in Japan.
France's National Assembly votes to abolish Capital punishment in France.
In Riyadh, the Gulf Cooperation Council is created among Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates.
Iran–Iraq War: Iranian forces break the Siege of Abadan in Operation Samen-ol-A'emeh.
Pensions in Chile: The new Chilean pension system, based on private pension funds, begins.
The Church of England General Synod votes to admit women to holy orders.
The Indonesian passenger ship Tampomas II catches fire and capsizes in the Java Sea, killing 580 people.
The founding congress of the Nepal Workers and Peasants Organization faction led by Hareram Sharma and D. P. Singh begins.
Wojciech Jaruzelski declares martial law in Poland, to prevent the dismantling of the communist system by Solidarity.
Beaune coach crash: In Beaune, France, 53 persons, 46 of them children, die in a highway accident (France's worst).
Cameroon president Ahmadou Ahidjo resigns, replaced by Paul Biya who rules the country for more than 40 years.
Four Iranian diplomats are kidnapped upon Israel's invasion of Lebanon.
In Hong Kong, health warnings on cigarette packets are made statutory.
In Israel, 400,000 marchers demand the resignation of Prime Minister Menachem Begin.
In Malaysia and Singapore, clocks are adjusted to the same time zone, UTC+8.
London-based Laker Airways collapses, leaving 6,000 stranded passengers and debts of £270 million.
Mauno Koivisto is elected President of Finland.
The December murders occur in Suriname.
The European Court of Human Rights rules that teachers who cane, belt or tawse children against the wishes of their parents are in breach of the Human Rights Convention.
Yasuhiro Nakasone becomes Prime Minister of Japan.
A reactor shutdown due to failure of fuel rods occurs at Kursk Nuclear Power Plant, Russia.
Germany's first elected Green Party representatives take their seats in the West German Bundestag, dressed in jeans and sweaters and accompanied by bongo drums.
Hamburger SV defeat Juventus 1–0 in the final of the European Cup.
Japan's former Prime Minister Kakuei Tanaka is found guilty of taking a $2 million bribe from Lockheed, and sentenced to 4 years in jail.
Reading Rainbow debuts on PBS.
South Africa approves a new constitution granting limited political rights to Coloureds and Asians as part of a series of reforms to apartheid.
Soviet authorities pass harsher punishments for drunkenness and absenteeism, responding to public calls to curb high rates of alcoholism.
The Turkish part of Cyprus declares independence.
The migration of the ARPANET to TCP/IP is officially completed (this is considered to be the beginning of the true Internet).
The team of A. J. Foyt, Preston Henn, Bob Wollek and Claude Ballot-Léna win the 24 Hours of Daytona automobile race in a Porsche 935.
A methane gas explosion at Abbeystead water treatment works in Lancashire, UK, kills 16 people.
An explosion on board a Maltese patrol boat disposing illegal fireworks at sea off Gozo kills seven soldiers and policemen.
Anti-Sikh mass murder takes place in Delhi and various parts of India following the assassination of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
Astronauts Bruce McCandless II and Robert L. Stewart make the first untethered space walk.
Barefoot South African runner Zola Budd and Mary Decker of the U.S. collide in the Olympic 3000 meters final, neither finishing as medallists.
Iran accuses Iraq of using chemical weapons; the United Nations condemns their use on March 30.
John Turner becomes the 17th Prime Minister of Canada.
South Africa, Mozambique and Portugal sign an agreement on electricity supply from the Cahora Bassa dam.
Sri Lankan Civil War, Kent and Dollar Farm massacres: the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam begin their first massacres of the Sinhalese people, in North and East Sri Lanka. 127 are killed.
The Canadian entertainment company Cirque du Soleil is founded.
An 8.0 earthquake strikes Mexico City, killing between 5,000 and 45,000 people and injuring 30,000 more.
Armero tragedy: The Nevado del Ruiz volcano erupts, killing an estimated 23,000 people, including 21,000 killed by lahars, in the town of Armero, Colombia.
Australia cancels its involvement in U.S.-led MX missile tests.
British Airtours Flight 28M: The 737's left engine catches fire while on its takeoff roll at Manchester Airport in the UK and 55 people are killed while trying to evacuate the aircraft.
British and Irish police foil a "mainland bombing campaign" sponsored by the Provisional Irish Republican Army which targets luxury vacation resorts.
Coca-Cola changes its formula and releases New Coke. The response is overwhelmingly negative and the original formula is back on the market in less than three months.
Gérard Hoarau, exiled political leader from the Seychelles, is assassinated in London.
Live Aid benefit concerts in London and Philadelphia raise over £50 million for famine relief in Ethiopia.
Philadelphia police drop bombs on a row home occupied MOVE during a gun battle between police and MOVE, killing six adults and five children.
The GNU Manifesto, written by Richard Stallman, is first published.
The cruise ship Achille Lauro is hijacked in the Mediterranean Sea by four heavily armed Palestinian terrorists. One passenger, American Leon Klinghoffer, is killed.
The inaugural WrestleMania is held in Madison Square Garden, New York, and is "main-evented" by Hulk Hogan and Mr. T vs. Paul Orndorff and Roddy Piper in a tag-team match.
A bomb explodes on a Trans World Airlines flight from Rome to Athens, killing 4 people.
A magnitude 5.7 earthquake destroys most of the Bulgarian town of Strajica, killing 2 people.
