NBC unveils its current peacock logo at the finale of its 60th anniversary special.
Pan Am Flight 73, with 358 people on board, is hijacked at Karachi International Airport by four Abu Nidal terrorists.
Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme is shot to death on his way home from the cinema in Stockholm, Sweden.
The 58th Academy Awards are held in Los Angeles, with Out of Africa winning Best Picture.
The Gateway Bridge in Brisbane, Australia, at this time the world's longest prestressed concrete free-cantilever bridge, is opened.
The Maxi Trial (Italian: Maxiprocesso) begins in the bunker room of the Ucciardone prison (Palermo). It will be the largest trial against the Sicilian Mafia.
The Rogers Commission releases its report on the Space Shuttle Challenger disaster.
Titan 34D-9 explodes just after launch while carrying the final KH-9 satellite.
Typhoon Wayne formed over the South China Sea, going on to become one of the longest-lived tropical cyclones at 21 days, and kill 490.
Walt Disney Pictures releases the company's 26th animated film, The Great Mouse Detective.
A Rüppell's vulture chick is hatched at the Milwaukee County Zoo, the first time the animal has been successfully bred in North America.
A Soviet-made Ilyushin Il-62 airliner, operated by LOT Polish Airlines, crashes into a forest just outside Warsaw, killing all 183 people on board.
A tsunami hits the Gulf of Alaska.
An insurrection in Sri Lanka by the Marxist–Leninist group, JVP, begins.
Bolivia reintroduces the Boliviano currency.
Great Basin National Park is dedicated; it is the 49th national park in the United States and the first in the state of Nevada.
In a coup d'état in Burundi, President Jean-Baptiste Bagaza is deposed by Major Pierre Buyoya.
Production I.G is founded by Mitsuhisa Ishikawa and Takayuki Goto.
South Korean politician, presidential candidate of the ruling party Roh Tae-woo makes a speech promising a wide program of nationwide reforms, the result of the June Democracy Movement.
Terry Waite, the special envoy of the Archbishop of Canterbury in Lebanon, is kidnapped in Beirut.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average closes above the 2,500 mark for the first time, at 2,510.04.
The New Zealand Nuclear Free Zone, Disarmament, and Arms Control Act is passed, the first of its kind in the world.
The United States and Poland agree to exchange ambassadors after a four-year break in relations.
The pilot of a British Aerospace BAE Harrier GR5 registered ZD325 accidentally ejects from his aircraft. The jet continues to fly until it runs out of fuel and crashes into the Irish Sea.
A meeting of Islamic Jihadi leaders, including Osama bin Laden, takes place, leading to the founding of Al-Qaeda.
Aloha Airlines Flight 243 safely lands after losing its roof in midair, killing a flight attendant and injuring 65 people.
Eritrean War of Independence: Having defeated the Nadew Command, the EPLF enters the town of Afabet, victoriously concluding the Battle of Afabet.
In Soviet Armenia, the 6.8 Spitak earthquake kills nearly 25,000, injures 31,000 and leaves 400,000 homeless.
Singing Revolution: In the Estonian Soviet Socialist Republic, 300,000 people gather to express their support for independence.
The Ocean Odyssey drilling rig suffers a blowout and fire in the North Sea, resulting in one death.
The Piper Alpha production platform in the North Sea is destroyed by explosions and fires, killing 165 oil workers and 2 rescue mariners. 61 workers survive.
The cargo ship Khian Sea deposits 4,000 tons of toxic waste in Haiti after wandering around the Atlantic for sixteen months.
The constitution of the Sixth Republic of Korea comes into effect.
Ante Marković succeeds Branko Mikulić as Prime Minister of Yugoslavia.
Gazprom, an energy production and sales organization in Russia, becomes state-run enterprise, changing from the Soviet Ministry of Gas Industry.
Hong Kong begins the forcible repatriation of Vietnamese boat people, starting with a group of 59 who are flown to Hanoi.
Margaret Thatcher's new local government tax (the poll tax) is introduced in Scotland. It will be introduced in England and Wales the following year.
Representatives of the government of Ethiopia and Eritrean separatists meet in Atlanta, with former U.S. President Jimmy Carter attempting to broker a peace settlement.
The New York Times discloses involvement of West German company Imhausen and Salzgitter AG in building a chemical weapon plant in Rabta, Libya.
The Parliament of Greece indicted former Prime Minister of Greece Andreas Papandreou and four of his ministers in connection to the Koskotas scandal.
The first commercial dial-up Internet connection in North America is made, by The World STD.
Tim Berners-Lee produces the proposal document that will become the blueprint for the World Wide Web.
Zaid al-Rifai resigns as Prime Minister of Jordan in the wake of riots over government-imposed price hikes that began on April 18.
"The Second Battle of Trafalgar": A massive anti-poll tax demonstration in Trafalgar Square, London, turns into a riot; 471 people are injured, and 341 are arrested.
A 7.0 earthquake shakes the Chinese province of Qinghai leaving 126 dead.
Cold War: Checkpoint Charlie is dismantled.
East Germany and West Germany announce they will unite on October 3.
Foster v British Gas plc decided in the European Court of Justice, a leading case on the definition of the "state" under European Union law.
Mega Borg oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico near Galveston, Texas.
Nawaz Sharif is sworn in as the Prime Minister of Pakistan.
Ramiz Ali declares that the rejection of Communism will not be repeated in Albania, but that the changing European political climate will nevertheless require adjustments.
Spain grants Protestantism and Judaism legal equality with the Roman Catholic Church.
The German federal election (the first election held since German reunification) is won by Helmut Kohl, who remains Chancellor of Germany.
The Supreme Soviet of the Soviet Union grants Gorbachev special powers for 18 months to secure the Soviet Union's transition to a market economy.
The US and the USSR agree to end production of chemical weapons and to destroy most of their stockpiles of chemical weapons.
The city of Tiraspol in the Moldavian SSR briefly declares independence.
A major collapse at the Emaswati Colliery in Swaziland traps 26 miners 65 meters below the surface; they are rescued 30 hours later.
Chemical Bank and Manufacturers Hanover Corporation amalgamate, becoming the largest bank merger in history.
Czechoslovakia becomes the second Eastern European country to abandon its command economy.
Dissolution of the Soviet Union: Ukraine declares independence, followed by Belarus the next day, from the Soviet Union.
Dissolution of the Soviet Union: Ukrainians vote overwhelmingly for independence from the Soviet Union in a referendum.
Economy of the Soviet Union: Government-imposed price increases double or triple the cost of consumer goods in the Soviet Union.
End of Apartheid: The African National Congress leads a general strike, demanding representation in the government and an end to the value-added tax.
Former Iranian prime minister Shapour Bakhtiar is assassinated in the Parisian suburb of Suresnes.
Gulf War: At 4 a.m. local time ground troops cross the Saudi Arabian border and enter Kuwait, thus starting the ground phase of the war.
In the Swedish general election, the Social Democrats suffer their worst election results in 60 years, leading to the resignation of Prime Minister Ingvar Carlsson.
Iraq disarmament crisis: Iraq declares some of its chemical weapons and materials to the UN, as required by Resolution 687, and claims that it does not have a biological weapons program.
Somaliland secedes from Somalia; its independence is not recognised by the international community.
A riot breaks out in the Carandiru Penitentiary in São Paulo, Brazil, resulting in the Carandiru massacre.
Abkhazia declares independence from Georgia.
Algerian Civil War: The government of Algeria declares a state of emergency and begins a crackdown on the Islamic Salvation Front.
Boutros Boutros-Ghali of Egypt replaces Javier Pérez de Cuéllar of Peru as United Nations Secretary-General.
Emperor of Japan Akihito begins the first imperial visit to China, telling a Beijing audience he feels deep sorrow for the suffering of the Chinese people during World War II.
First Nagorno-Karabakh War: in the disputed territory of Nagorno-Karabakh, fighting between Armenians and Azeris leaves at least 60 people dead.
Fuel leaking into a sewer causes a series of explosions in Guadalajara, Mexico; 215 are killed, 1,500 injured.
In poor conditions caused by Cyclone Forrest, Vietnam Airlines Flight 474 crashes near Nha Trang, killing 30.
The 18th G7 summit is held in Munich.
The Collective Security Treaty Organization is established by six post-Soviet states belonging to the Commonwealth of Independent States.
Bill Clinton and Al Gore are inaugurated as US President and Vice President.
In Moscow, Presidents George H. W. Bush (United States) and Boris Yeltsin (Russia) sign the second Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty.
Jurassic Park releases in cinemas in the United States.
Murder of James Bulger: Two-year-old James Bulger is abducted from New Strand Shopping Centre by two ten-year-old boys Robert Thompson and Jon Venables, who later torture and murder him.
Oscar Luigi Scalfaro appoints Carlo Azeglio Ciampi Prime Minister of Italy.
Russia completes removing its troops from Lithuania.
The 19th G7 summit is held in Tokyo, Japan.
The Cambodian monarchy is restored, with Norodom Sihanouk as king.
The Israeli Supreme Court acquits accused Nazi death camp guard John Demjanjuk of all charges and he is set free.
The Maastricht Treaty takes effect, formally establishing the European Union.
The North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) passes the legislative houses in the United States, Canada and Mexico.
The Republic of Macedonia is admitted to the United Nations under a provisional reference "the former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia".
The South Korean ferry Seohae capsizes off Pusan, South Korea; 292 are killed.
Cold War: the last Russian troops leave Germany.
Ernesto Zedillo takes office as President of Mexico.
Four United States F-16s shoot down four Serbian J-21s over Bosnia and Herzegovina for violation of the Operation Deny Flight and its no-fly zone.
In the aftermath of the Chadian–Libyan conflict, the International Court of Justice rules that the Aouzou Strip belongs to the Republic of Chad.
Nelson Mandela is inaugurated as South Africa's first black president.
North Korean President Kim Il Sung dies, but officially continues to hold office.
Soyuz TM-18: Valeri Polyakov begins his 437.7-day orbit of the Earth, eventually setting the world record for days spent in orbit.
Sultan Azlan Muhibbudin Shah ibni Almarhum Sultan Yusuff Izzudin Shah Ghafarullahu-lahu ends his term as the 9th Yang di-Pertuan Agong of Malaysia.
The first Eurostar train passengers travel through the Channel Tunnel.
A fire in Baku Metro, Azerbaijan, kills 289 passengers, becoming the world's worst subway disaster.
AFC Ajax wins the UEFA Champions League at the Ernst Happel Stadium in Vienna by defeating A.C. Milan 1–0.
Astronaut Norman Thagard becomes the first American to ride into space aboard a Russian launch vehicle, lifting off from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
Burmese dissident Aung San Suu Kyi is freed from house arrest.
Five-year-old Gyaincain Norbu is enthroned as the 11th reincarnation of the Panchen Lama at Tashilhunpo Monastery.
Japanese police rescue 365 hostages from a hijacked All Nippon Airways Flight 857 at Hakodate airport. The hijacker was armed with a knife and demanded the release of Shoko Asahara.
Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz announce the discovery of 51 Pegasi b, the first confirmed extrasolar planet orbiting an ordinary main-sequence star.
Microsoft releases Windows 95 to the public.
The 6.6 Western Macedonia earthquake strikes northwestern Greece with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe), injuring 25 and causing $450 million in damage.
The Millbrook Commonwealth Action Programme, a programme to implement the Harare Declaration, is announced by the Commonwealth Heads of Government.
The Washington Post and The New York Times publish the Unabomber Manifesto.
Twenty-seven nations sign the Barcelona Treaty, creating the Union for the Mediterranean.
Valeri Polyakov completes 366 days in space while aboard the Mir space station, breaking a duration record.
A Zairean cargo plane crashes into a crowded market in the center of the capital city of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kinshasa, killing around 300 people.
A permanent peace agreement is signed at Malacañang Palace between the Government of the Philippines and the Moro National Liberation Front.
A rocket ignited during a fireworks display in Arequipa, Peru knocks down a high-tension power cable into a dense crowd, electrocuting 35 people.
Bosnian Serbs break off contact with the Bosnian government and with representatives of IFOR, the NATO localised force, in reaction to the arrest of several Bosnian Serb war criminals.
Dolly the sheep, the first mammal to be successfully cloned from an adult cell, is born at the Roslin Institute in Midlothian, Scotland, UK.
France undertakes its last nuclear weapons test.
Jerry Rawlings is re-elected as President of Ghana.
José María Aznar, leader of the Popular Party, is elected as Prime Minister of Spain, replacing Felipe González.
Sri Lanka wins the Cricket World Cup by beating Australia in the final.
The Tutsi-led Burundian army performs a coup and reinstalls previous president Pierre Buyoya, ousting current president Sylvestre Ntibantunganya.
U.S. president Bill Clinton signs the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty at the United Nations.
A military coup in Sierra Leone replaces President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah with Major Johnny Paul Koroma.
American rapper The Notorious B.I.G. is murdered in Los Angeles.
In Des Moines, Iowa, Bobbi McCaughey gives birth to septuplets in the second known case where all seven babies are born alive, and the first in which all survive infancy.
In San Diego, 39 Heaven's Gate cultists commit mass suicide at their compound.
K. R. Narayanan is sworn in as India's 10th president and the first member of the Dalit caste to hold this office.
Korean Air Flight 801 crash lands west of Guam International Airport, resulting in the deaths of 228 people.
Madeleine Albright becomes the first female Secretary of State of the United States, after confirmation by the United States Senate.
Microsoft releases Windows 98 Beta 3.
NASA's Pathfinder space probe lands on the surface of Mars.
Scotland votes in favour of a devolved Parliament, forming the Scottish Parliament less than two years later.
Severe Tropical Storm Linda devastates southern Vietnam and Thailand, killing 3,275 people.
The Emergency Alert System is introduced in the United States.
Uruguay's worst air disaster occurs when Austral Líneas Aéreas Flight 2553 crashes near Nuevo Berlín, killing all 74 on board.
Afghan Civil War: The Taliban takes control of Mazar-i-Sharif.
Australia holds its first National Sorry Day.
Cavalese cable car disaster: A United States military pilot causes the deaths of 20 people near Trento, Italy, when his low-flying EA-6B Prowler severs the cable of a cable-car.
Former Brigadier-General Ansumane Mané seizes control over military barracks in Bissau, marking the beginning of the Guinea-Bissau Civil War.
Hugo Chávez, politician and former officer of the Venezuelan army, is elected President of Venezuela.
Japan launches the probe Nozomi to Mars, joining the United States and Russia as an outer space-exploring nation.
Quett Masire voluntarily steps down as President of Botswana after 18 years in office.
The European Union announces an arms embargo against Serbia and Montenegro.
The Lunar Prospector spacecraft is launched into orbit around the Moon, and later finds evidence for frozen water, in soil in permanently shadowed craters near the Moon's poles.
Dagestan incursions: Hundreds of Chechen guerrillas invade the Russian republic of Dagestan, triggering the short war.
David Steel becomes the first Presiding Officer (Speaker) of the modern Scottish Parliament.
East Timor votes for independence from Indonesia in a referendum.
Kiribati, Nauru and Tonga join the United Nations.
T-Mobile Park (formerly known as Safeco Field) opens for the first time.
Thabo Mbeki is inaugurated as the second president of South Africa, marking the first peaceful transfer of executive power in the country's post-democratization history.
The 7.2 Düzce earthquake shakes northwestern Turkey with a maximum Mercalli intensity of IX (Violent). At least 845 people are killed and almost 5,000 are injured.
The King of Bhutan allows television transmissions to commence in the Kingdom for the first time, coinciding with the King's Silver Jubilee.
The adult animated sitcom Futurama premiered on Fox.
The euro currency is established, and the European Central Bank assumes full powers.
The hormone Ghrelin is discovered and named.
Thirty-one people die in the Ladbroke Grove rail crash, west of London, England.
Twenty-three people die in a fire at the Sealand Youth Training Center in South Korea.
U.S. President Bill Clinton is acquitted in impeachment proceedings in the United States Senate.
A new class of composite material is fabricated, which has a combination of physical properties never before seen in a natural or human-made material.
Alaska Airlines Flight 261 crashes off the California coast into the Pacific Ocean, killing all 88 passengers and crew.
Hatfield rail crash: A Great North Eastern Railway Intercity 225 express train is derailed, killing four people and injuring many others, in Hatfield, Hertfordshire, England.
In southern Nigeria, a leaking petroleum pipeline explodes, killing about 250 villagers who were scavenging gasoline.
Israeli opposition leader Ariel Sharon visits the Temple Mount in East Jerusalem, sparking an uprising that becomes the Second Intifada.
Kaprun disaster, Austria: A funicular fire in an Alpine tunnel kills 155 skiers and snowboarders.
The United States dollar becomes the official currency of Ecuador, replacing the Ecuadorian sucre.
The last naturally conceived Pyrenean ibex is found dead, presumed to have been killed by a falling tree.
The last wholly Swedish-owned arms manufacturer, Bofors, is sold to American arms manufacturer United Defense.
UNESCO holds the inaugural celebration of International Mother Language Day.
A 7.7 Gujarat earthquake shakes Western India with a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme), leaving thousands of people dead and more than 166,000 others injured.
An ebola outbreak is confirmed in Gabon.
Declaration to establish the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation is signed.
Extreme Championship Wrestling files for bankruptcy and ceases operations, is eventually bought by its competitor, the World Wrestling Federation.
Greece becomes the 12th country to join the Eurozone.
Moldova joins the World Trade Organization.
NASCAR Champion Dale Earnhardt is killed in a crash during the Daytona 500.
Shijiazhuang bombings: 108 people are killed in a series of bombings in Shijiazhuang, China.
The Končulj Agreement results in the disarmament of the Liberation Army of Preševo, Medveđa and Bujanovac, ending the Insurgency in the Preševo Valley.
The Leonids meteor shower occurs in its heaviest concentration in decades as Earth passes through a debris cloud.
The World Trade Organization begins the Doha Development Round to negotiate lower trade barriers between countries and integrate developing nations into the global economy.
United States invasion of Afghanistan: In response to the September 11 attacks, Afghanistan is invaded by a US-led coalition, beginning the War in Afghanistan.
Belarus restricts religious activity outside of the Belarusian Orthodox Church with a new law.
Hurricane Lili crosses Cuba and several other Caribbean islands before making landfall in Louisiana.
In American football, Tom Brady's victory in the Tuck Rule Game causes a national controversy.
Jemaah Islamiyah militants detonate multiple bombs in two nightclubs in Kuta, Bali, killing 202 people and injuring over 300 people, making it the worst terrorist act in Indonesia's history.
Nepali Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba asks King Gyanendra to dissolve the parliament amid escalation of the Nepalese Civil War.
Operation Enduring Freedom – Philippines: The Philippines and the United States begin a joint operation to combat Jihadist groups in the Philippines.
Salvadoran generals José Guillermo García and Carlos Eugenio Vides Casanova are found liable for torture in an American court.
The ImClone stock trading case begins when ImClone Systems CEO Samuel D. Waksal is arrested for insider trading.
The Rome Statute comes into force, thereby establishing the International Criminal Court.
UNITA guerrilla leader Jonas Savimbi is killed in clashes against government troops led by Angolan President José Eduardo dos Santos in Moxico Province, Angola.
A ceasefire is reached at the Line of Control in Kashmir.
After acknowledging that it has produced enriched uranium, Iran agrees to suspend its nuclear program.
Former General François Bozizé seizes power through a military coup in the Central African Republic.
Former President of France Valéry Giscard d'Estaing presents his draft for a Constitution of the European Union.
Major Fernando Pereira leads a failed coup against President Fradique de Menezes in São Tomé and Príncipe.
Prometea, the world's first cloned horse, is born.
Tel Aviv central bus station: Two Palestinian suicide bombers attack a neighborhood in Tel Aviv, killing at least 23 people and injuring 103.
The Human Genome Project is completed, with 99% of the human genome sequenced to 99.99% accuracy.
The Station nightclub fire: A fire broke out at a music venue in West Warwick, Rhode Island, United States, killing 100 people and injuring 230.
Typhoon Dujuan makes landfall in Guangdong as a category 1 typhoon with sustained winds of 90 mph.
A fire breaks out at the Duchess Anna Amalia Library.
Google makes its initial public offering.
NASA releases the Hubble Ultra-Deep Field image of early galaxies.
NASA's MESSENGER space probe is launched, with its primary mission being the study of Mercury.
Palestinian president Yasser Arafat dies. Mahmoud Abbas is appointed as his successor.
Patriarch Peter VII of Alexandria is killed in a helicopter crash.
Poland bans the use of chlorofluorocarbons.
TNA introduced their television program, Impact! and broadcast on Fox Sports Net.
The Gherkin opens in London.
The International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture enters into force.
The RMS Queen Mary 2, at the time the largest ocean liner ever built, is christened by its namesake's granddaughter, Queen Elizabeth II.
The Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants enters into force.
The prehistoric human species Homo floresiensis is described.
Typhoon Nanmadol kills 775 people in the Philippines.
At least 60 people are killed and 115 more are wounded in a series of coordinated suicide bombings in Amman, Jordan.
Cedar Revolution: Syria withdraws the last of its military garrison from Lebanon, ending its 29-year military occupation of the country.
Chad descends into civil war after various rebel forces, with support from Sudan, attack the capital, N'Djamena.
English whisky is re-established in England.
Four coordinated suicide bombings hit central London, killing 52 people and injuring over 700.
Helios Airways Flight 522, en route from Larnaca, Cyprus to Prague, Czech Republic via Athens, crashes in the hills near Grammatiko, Greece, killing 121 passengers and crew.
Hurricane Katrina makes landfall along the U.S. Gulf Coast, causing severe damage, killing over a thousand people and causing an estimated $108 billion in damage.
Jeanna Giese from Wisconsin, United States, comes home from the hospital and officially becomes the first person to ever survive rabies without a vaccination.
North Korea agrees to stop building nuclear weapons in exchange for aid and cooperation.
The Huygens spacecraft lands on Titan, the largest moon of Saturn.
The Kyoto Protocol officially goes into effect.
The President of Kyrgyzstan, Askar Akayev, is deposed following mass anti-government demonstrations and flees the country.
The United Nations Climate Change Conference is held in Montreal.
The second crewed Chinese spacecraft, Shenzhou 6, is launched.
Egyptian passenger ferry,, sinks in the Red Sea off the coast of Saudi Arabia, killing over 1,000 people.
Evo Morales is inaugurated as president of Bolivia.
Former President of Iraq Saddam Hussein is sentenced to death by hanging by the Iraqi Special Tribunal. He is later executed by hanging for crimes against humanity on December 30.
Fredrik Reinfeldt replaces Göran Persson as Prime Minister of Sweden.
News was revealed of a thwarted terrorist plot to detonate liquid explosives disguised as soft drinks, aboard multiple transatlantic air flights.
Nintendo releases the Wii.
Russia temporarily cuts shipment of natural gas to Ukraine during a price dispute.
The 6.4 Yogyakarta earthquake shakes central Java in Indonesia with an MSK intensity of IX (Destructive), leaving more than 5,700 dead and 37,000 injured.
The Offshore MPA project is initiated.
The Qinghai–Tibet railway begins operation, making Tibet the final province-level entity of China to establish a conventional railway.
The Royal Thai Army overthrows the government of Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra in a coup.
The military seizes power in Fiji, in a coup d'état led by Commodore Frank Bainimarama.
An 8.0 earthquake strikes Peru, killing at least 519 people, injuring more than 1,300, and causing tsunami warnings in the Pacific Ocean.
Canadian professional wrestler Chris Benoit commits a double-murder suicide on his wife and youngest son at their home in Fayetteville, Georgia, United States.
Finnish racing driver Kimi Räikkönen won his first Formula One World Championship, driving for Scuderia Ferrari at the Brazilian Grand Prix.
Latvian Prime Minister Aigars Kalvītis and Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Fradkov sign a border treaty between Latvia and Russia, officially demarcating the border between the two.
Microblogging social network Tumblr is launched to the public.
Nancy Pelosi becomes the first female speaker of the United States House of Representatives.
Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum of Dubai makes the largest single charitable donation in modern history, committing €7.41 billion to an educational foundation in the Middle East.
The Armed Forces of the Philippines lay siege to the Peninsula Manila after soldiers led by Senator Antonio Trillanes stage a mutiny.
The First Ivorian Civil War ends with a peace agreement.
The Phoenix spacecraft is launched toward Mars to study its north pole.
The SELENE spacecraft launches, with its objective being to study the Moon.
Windows Vista is released to consumers by Microsoft.
A Belavia CRJ-100 crash lands at Zvartnots International Airport in Yerevan, Armenia. 7 people are injured.
African Union and Comoros forces invade the rebel-held island of Anjouan, returning the island to Comorian control.
Cyclone Nargis passes through Myanmar, killing more than 138,000 people.
Cyprus and Malta adopt the euro currency.
International Convention on Cluster Munitions is adopted in Dublin.
Radovan Karadžić, the first president of the Republika Srpska, is arrested in Belgrade, Serbia, on allegations of war crimes, following a 12-year-long manhunt.
SpaceX Falcon 1 becomes the world's first privately developed space launch vehicle to successfully make orbit.
Spanair Flight 5022 crashes at Madrid–Barajas Airport, killing 154 people on board.
The Large Hadron Collider (LHC) is officially inaugurated at Geneva.
XL Airways Germany Flight 888T. An Airbus A320 due to be redelivered to Air New Zealand stalls and crashes over Mediterranean Sea resulting the deaths of 7.
At least 157 demonstrators are massacred by the Guinean military at the Stade du 28 Septembre during a protest against the government that came to power in a coup d'état the previous year.
British racing driver Jenson Button won his first Formula One World Championship, driving for Brawn GP at the Brazilian Grand Prix.
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 was released.
Caspian Airlines Flight 7908, en route from Tehran, Iran, to Yerevan, Armenia crashes into the Jannatabad village in Qazvin Province; killing all 168 on board.
Former Serbian president Milan Milutinović is acquitted by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia regarding war crimes during the Kosovo War.
German football club RB Leipzig is founded by Red Bull.
Maersk Alabama Hijacking occurs, the ship being taken over by Somalian pirates off the coast of Somalia.
Rachel Crandall Crocker founds the International Transgender Day of Visibility.
The first ("Genesis") block of the blockchain of the cryptocurrency and decentralized payment system Bitcoin is established by the creator of the system, known as Satoshi Nakamoto.
Tiféret Israel Synagogue attack, profanation of the oldest synagogue in Caracas, Venezuela.
A tennis match between Nicolas Mahut and John Isner at the Wimbledon Championships, becomes the longest tennis match in history.
Ethiopian Airlines Flight 409 crashes into the Mediterranean shortly after take-off from Beirut–Rafic Hariri International Airport, killing all 90 people on board.
Građevni kombinat 'Međimurje' from Čakovec, one of the largest Croatian construction and civil engineering companies, ceased to exist.
Nine activists are killed in a clash with soldiers when Israeli Navy forces raid and capture a flotilla of ships attempting to break the Gaza blockade.
Nude, Green Leaves and Bust by Pablo Picasso sells in New York for US$106.5 million, setting another new world record for a work of art sold at auction.
The tallest man-made structure to date, the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, is officially opened.
A magnitude 7.2 Mw earthquake jolts eastern Turkey near the city of Van, killing over 600 people and damaging about 2,200 buildings.
Approximately 100 people die after a petrol pipeline explodes in Nairobi.
Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak resigns after widespread protests calling for his departure, leaving control of Egypt in the hands of the military, until a general election can be held.
Libyan rebels take control of the capital Tripoli, effectively overthrowing the government of Muammar Gaddafi.
South Sudan secedes from Sudan, per the result of the independence referendum held in January.
The United Kingdom severs diplomatic relations with Iran and expels diplomats, less than 24 hours after protesters attacked the British embassy in Tehran.
The United Nations Security Council votes 10–0 to create a no-fly zone over Libya in response to allegations of government aggression against civilians.
A pastel version of The Scream, by the Norwegian painter Edvard Munch, sells for US$120 million in a New York City auction, setting a new world record for an auctioned work of art.
Curiosity, the Mars Science Laboratory mission's rover, successfully lands on Mars.
Sauli Niinistö is inaugurated as the 12th President of Finland.
The Cicada 3301 internet hunt begins.
The Congress of Paraguay approves the impeachment of president Fernando Lugo.
The National Movement for the Liberation of Azawad unilaterally declares the independence of Azawad from Mali.
The Séléka overthrows the government of the Central African Republic which leads to the outbreak of a Civil war.
The UN General Assembly approves a motion granting Palestine non-member observer state status.
Tokyo Skytree, the tallest self-supporting tower in the world at 634 metres high, is opened to the public.
Turkish adventurer Erden Eruç becomes the first person in history to complete a solo human-powered circumnavigation of the Earth.
A magnitude 7.2 earthquake struck Bohol, Philippines, leaving 222 dead, 8 missing, and 976 people injured.
A police helicopter crashes into The Clutha, a pub in Glasgow, Scotland, killing 10 people and injuring 31.
Emir of Qatar Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani abdicates and his son Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani assumes power.
Grand Theft Auto V earns more than half a billion dollars on its first day of release.
Park Geun-hye becomes the first woman to become the president of South Korea.
The uncrewed Mars Orbiter Mission is launched by India from its launch pad in Sriharikota.
Willem-Alexander is inaugurated as King of the Netherlands following the abdication of Beatrix.
XIV World Youth Day, in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
Air Algérie Flight 5017, a McDonnell Douglas MD-83, crashes in Mali, killing all 116 people on board.
Joko Widodo is inaugurated as the 7th President of Indonesia.
Latvia adopts the euro as its currency and becomes the 18th member of the Eurozone.
Narendra Modi succeeds Manmohan Singh as the 14th Prime Minister of India.
Syrian civil war: ISIS militants launched an offensive to capture the town of Kobanî, which lasted for six months.
The Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant declares itself a caliphate.
The South Korean ferry MV Sewol capsizes and sinks after an unmanageable cargo shift, killing 304 people, mostly high school students.
The XXII Olympic Winter Games are held in Sochi, Russia. Slopestyle events are introduced for the first time.
The self-proclaimed Luhansk People's Republic declares its independence from Ukraine.
Two hostages and terrorist Man Haron Monis are killed in the Lindt Cafe siege in Sydney, Australia.
Typhoon Rammasun makes landfall in Hainan, China as a category 5 super typhoon, killing 88 and causing $7.14 billion in damages.
A magnitude 7.8 earthquake strikes Nepal and causes 8,857 deaths in Nepal, 130 in India, 27 in China and 4 in Bangladesh with a total of 9,018 deaths.
A partial solar eclipse is visible in southern Africa, the southern Indian Ocean, and Antarctica. It is the 54th eclipse of Saros cycle 125.
A stampede during the Hajj pilgrimage in Mecca kills at least 2,200 people and injures more than 900 others, with more than 650 missing.
After Houthi forces seize the presidential palace, Yemeni President Abd Rabbuh Mansur Hadi resigns after months of unrest.
An Airbus A320-211 operated by Germanwings is deliberately crashed by First officer Andres Lubitz in the French Alps, killing all 150 people on board.
Hurricane Patricia becomes the most intense hurricane ever recorded in the Western Hemisphere and the second strongest worldwide, with winds of 215 mph and a pressure of 872 mbar.
Lithuania officially adopts the euro as its currency, replacing the litas, and becomes the 19th Eurozone country.
The ancient city sites of Nimrud, Hatra and Dur-Sharrukin in Iraq are demolished by the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant.
A study finds the VSV-EBOV vaccine against the Ebola virus between 70 and 100% effective, thus making it the first proven vaccine against the disease.
An earthquake of magnitude 6.2 hits central Italy, killing 299 people.
An earthquake of magnitude 6.6 strikes southern Taiwan, killing 117 people.
Following the fallout caused by the execution of Nimr al-Nimr, Saudi Arabia and several other countries end their diplomatic relations with Iran.
LaMia Flight 2933 crashes into a mountain near Medellín, Colombia, killing 71 of the 77 people on board, including members of the Brazilian Chapecoense football squad.
NASA's Juno spacecraft enters orbit around Jupiter and begins a 20-month survey of the planet.
The United Kingdom votes in a referendum to leave the European Union, triggering the so-called Brexit.
At the level crossing of the Hanko–Hyvinkää railway line, a passenger train collided with an off-road truck of the Nyland Brigade in Raseborg, Finland; four people died and 11 were injured.
Cassini–Huygens ends its 13-year mission by plunging into Saturn, becoming the first spacecraft to enter the planet's atmosphere.
Emma Morano, an Italian supercentenarian, becomes the last known person born in the 19th century to die.
Iraqi Civil War: Mosul is declared fully liberated from the Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant.
Istanbul nightclub shooting: A gunman dressed as Santa Claus opens fire at the Reina nightclub in Istanbul, Turkey, killing 39 people and injuring 79 others.
Nature publishes an article recognising the high-velocity asteroid ʻOumuamua as originating from outside the Solar System, i.e. the first known interstellar object.
The Goodwin Fire, a wildfire, starts in Yavapai County, Arizona near Mayer and forces evacuations of more than a hundred people.
The United Kingdom triggers Article 50 of the Lisbon Treaty, starting the Brexit negotiations, the talks for the United Kingdom to leave the European Union.
The United States officially recognizes Jerusalem as Israel's capital.
WannaCry ransomware attack: Computers around the world are hit by a large-scale ransomware cyberattack, which goes on to affect at least 150 countries.
Bulgaria takes over the Presidency of the Council of the European Union, after the Estonian presidency.
NASA's InSight probe successfully lands on the surface of Mars.
NASA's Kepler space telescope mission ends after the spacecraft runs out of fuel.
Nabi Tajima, the last known person born in the 19th century dies.
Pedro Sánchez is appointed new Prime Minister of Spain, a day after a vote of no confidence against his predecessor, Mariano Rajoy.
The Yang di-Pertuan Agong, Sultan Muhammad V, pardons Malaysian opposition leader Anwar Ibrahim who is immediately released.
Typhoon Mangkhut impacts the Philippines, Taiwan, Hong Kong and China, resulting in more than 60 fatalities.
Adventist Health System rebranded its facilities to the trade name AdventHealth.
During Holy Week, a major fire engulfs Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris, resulting in the roof and main spire collapsing.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is indicted on charges of bribery, fraud and breach of trust.
Sanna Marin, at the age of 34, becomes the world's youngest serving prime minister after being selected to lead Finland's Social Democratic Party.
The Amazon Catholic bishops synod proposes that married men be ordained as priests, which would reverse the Church's centuries-old discipline of celibacy.
The Dow Jones plunges more than 500 points, due to concerns over the yield curve inversion.
The Parliament of the United Kingdom is prorogued amid unprecedented protests from opposition MPs, who hold up signs in the House of Commons and refuse to back the shutdown.
The Republic of Ireland promises to plant 440 million trees in twenty years to combat climate change.
The U.S. Justice Department charges Chinese tech firm Huawei with multiple counts of fraud, raising U.S.–China tensions.
U.S. President Donald Trump, during an official state visit to Japan, becomes the first foreign leader to meet with Japanese emperor Naruhito.
Amazon CEO Jeff Bezos becomes the first person in history to have a net worth exceeding US$200 billion, according to Forbes.
Apple releases the first Mac computers (a new MacBook Air, Mac mini and MacBook Pro) powered by Apple silicon chips.
COVID-19 pandemic: China reports no new cases for the first time since the pandemic began, according to the National Health Commission.
Hanau shootings: Eleven people are killed and five injured in a terrorist shooting spree by a far-right extremist targeting shisha bars in Hanau, near Frankfurt, Germany.
Koshobe massacre: Boko Haram terrorists attack a village in Borno, Nigeria, killing 110 people and wounding 6 people.
The Geneva Consensus Declaration on Promoting Women's Health and Strengthening the Family is signed by government representatives from 34 countries.
The Hellenic Parliament elects Katerina Sakellaropoulou as president of Greece.
A 7.2-magnitude earthquake strikes Haiti, killing more than 2,500 people.
Barbados becomes a republic on its 55th anniversary of independence while remaining a member of the Commonwealth of Nations.
COVID-19 pandemic: The number of recorded deaths from COVID-19 surpasses 5 million.
COVID-19 pandemic: The number of vaccinations administered worldwide exceeds 3 billion.
Clashes in Apure between Colombian FARC dissidents and the Venezuelan Armed Forces cause at least six casualties, as well as displacing 4,000 Venezuelans.
The African Continental Free Trade Area comes into effect.
The China National Space Administration launches the first module of its Tiangong space station, named Tianhe, beginning a two-year effort to build the station in orbit.
The China National Space Administration sends its first three astronauts to occupy the Tiangong Space Station, the country's first space station.
The G7 agrees on a global minimum corporate tax rate of 15% intended to prevent tax avoidance by some of the world's biggest multinational companies.
The Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, the first legally binding international agreement comprehensively to prohibit nuclear weapons, comes into effect.
The United States officially rejoins the Paris Agreement, 107 days after leaving.
A large eruption of Hunga Tonga–Hunga Ha'apai, a submarine volcano in Tonga, triggers tsunami warnings in Australia, Canada, Chile, Fiji, Japan, New Zealand, Samoa, and the United States.
Abdalla Hamdok resigns as Prime Minister of Sudan amid deadly protests.
Cyclone Batsirai kills a total of 123 people across Madagascar, Mauritius, and Réunion two weeks after Tropical Storm Ana killed 115 people in the same region.
OpenAI releases ChatGPT, an artificial intelligence chatbot able to answer questions and write essays.
Spanish club Real Madrid beat English club Liverpool 1–0 to win the UEFA Champions League final played at the Stade de France in Paris, France.
The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration reveals its first image of Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way.
The Large Hadron Collider recommences full operations, three years after being shut down for upgrades.
The National Assembly of Hungary elects former minister for Family Affairs, Katalin Novák, as president of Hungary in a 137–51 vote.
A train collision in Odisha, India results in at least 296 deaths and more than 1,200 others injured.
Chris Hipkins succeeds Jacinda Ardern as Prime Minister of New Zealand, six days after she announced her resignation.
Google DeepMind releases the Gemini Language Model. Gemini will act as a foundational model integrated into Google's existing tools, including Search and Bard.
Lawmakers in the Russian State Duma vote to withdraw Russia from 21 conventions of the Council of Europe.
SpaceX's Starship rocket, the largest and most powerful rocket ever built, launches for the first time in a test flight from Texas. It explodes four minutes after launch.
The United Nations Security Council votes unanimously to end MINUSMA, its peacekeeping mission in Mali.
Japan becomes the 5th country to achieve a soft landing on the Moon, with its SLIM mission.
Negotiations on the accession of Moldova and Ukraine to the European Union have officially begun.
Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus assumes office as Chief Adviser of an interim government formed after Sheikh Hasina's resignation in Bangladesh.
The G7 countries agree to phase out unabated coal power by 2030–2035.
A 6.9 earthquake shakes the island of Cebu in the Philippines, leaving 71 people dead and 559 injured.
Croatia completes the process of joining the European Economic Area.
Gaza war: A ceasefire goes into effect, lasting until an Israeli surprise attack on 18 March.
Indonesia becomes the tenth member to join BRICS.
OpenAI's model GPT-5 is released.
The G20 Johannesburg summit is held in South Africa, the first time a G20 summit has been held in Africa.
The No Kings protests occur across many cities in the U.S., as well as Canada, Europe, Japan and Mexico, against Donald Trump.
US President Donald Trump issues sweeping trade tariffs on many countries, including a 10% baseline tariff for all imports.
